docs.title: GitHub Copilot & Agentic Workflows: Train-the-Trainer
docs.text:
Use this curriculum to teach GitHub Copilot and GitHub Agentic Workflows. Choose from 29 sessions across 7 modules, including paths for product and delivery teams and HVE engineering.

Most sessions pair 1 hour of trainer content with a 2-hour hands-on lab. Session m4-02 has a 90-minute lab, Session m5-02 has a 2-hour 30-minute lab, and Session m5-03 has a 3-hour lab.

docs.title: Who this is for
docs.text:
• Trainers teaching development teams to use GitHub Copilot
  • Developer advocates building Copilot adoption programs
  • Engineering leads teaching Copilot skills within their teams
  • DevOps engineers integrating Copilot into CI/CD and infrastructure workflows
  • Product and delivery leaders teaching non-developers to understand, steer, and review agent work

docs.title: For technical-track trainers
docs.text:
• Strong software development background (any language)
  • Familiarity with GitHub (repos, PRs, issues, Actions)
  • GitHub Copilot Enterprise Cloud access
  • Comfort with live coding and demos
  • Docker for the Session m6-01 observability lab

docs.title: For technical-track trainees
docs.text:
• Working knowledge of at least one programming language
  • GitHub account with Copilot access
  • VS Code installed with GitHub Copilot extension
  • Basic Git proficiency
  • Node.js 22 or later and standalone CLI /refine access before Session m1-03
  • Working language servers for Session m3-04 (JavaScript) and Session m2-06 (Python)

docs.title: For product and delivery trainees
docs.text:
• Basic knowledge of their product or delivery process
  • A GitHub account with GitHub Copilot access
  • Browser access to the training repository
  • The GitHub Copilot app
  • The approved GitHub MCP server and a writable training repository

Product and delivery learners do not need programming experience, Git command-line knowledge, or repository administration skills.

GitHub Copilot access is required for Sessions m7-01 to m7-06. If a learner does not have access, stop and reschedule their Module 7 training once they do.

docs.title: Curriculum overview
docs.text:
Session IDs start with their module: m2-01 is the first session in Module 2. Numbers restart at 01 in each module. Directories use the same ID, such as sessions/session-m2-01-copilot-cli/.

Use data/session-catalog.json for the teaching order. Use the full module-local ID in saved sets and session links.

docs.title: Module 1: Copilot Fundamentals (Beginner)
docs.text: # Session Difficulty Duration Summary m1-01 Introduction to GitHub Copilot Beginner 3 hrs Explains what Copilot is, how the LLM and billing model work, data privacy, and how to install and configure it. m1-02 Copilot Chat & Inline Suggestions Beginner 3 hrs Covers Copilot Chat surfaces, slash commands, chat participants, model selection, and the CLI for daily development. m1-03 Prompt Engineering Fundamentals Beginner 3 hrs Builds a todo API with focused prompts and a checked CLI /refine rewrite.

docs.title: Module 2: Copilot in Practice (Intermediate to Advanced)
docs.text:
# Session Difficulty Duration Summary m2-01 GitHub Copilot in the CLI Intermediate 3 hrs Checks plan critique, CLI controls, queued/background work, recovery, and live fleet results. m2-02 Agent Mode in the IDE Intermediate 3 hrs Introduces agent mode, Copilot's autonomous plan-act-observe loop for multi-step, multi-file coding tasks in the IDE. m2-03 Copilot Spaces & Context Management Intermediate 3 hrs Curates context and inspects loaded CLI instructions to correct a stale rule before implementation. m2-04 Copilot for Code Review & PRs Intermediate 3 hrs Compares human review, local /review and /security-review, and Copilot PR findings before focused fixes. m2-05 GitHub Copilot App for Developers Intermediate 3 hrs Compares checked rubber-duck and /spar critiques, returns a forked plan note, and reviews repair and PR readiness. m2-06 Repair and Refactor a Broken Python Application Intermediate 3 hrs Repairs Python in failure order, checks LSP references, and refactors from an accepted plan without changing reports. m2-07 Migrate a Legacy Java Service to Modern .NET Advanced 3 hrs Ports a legacy Java service to modern .NET while preserving behavior through focused tests.

App access is required for Session m2-05 and Session m7-05's developer route. Check the required commands before delivery. Prepared outputs do not replace live work.

docs.title: Module 3: Agentic Workflows (Advanced)
docs.text: # Session Difficulty Duration Summary m3-01 Copilot App, Plugins & Canvas Extensions Advanced 3 hrs Uses the Copilot App Customize area to build a shared canvas with state limits, defined actions, and a review record. m3-02 Copilot Cloud Agent Advanced 3 hrs Covers assigning GitHub issues to the cloud agent for autonomous resolution, branch, code, tests, and draft PR. m3-03 MCP Servers & Custom Tool Integration Advanced 3 hrs Introduces the Model Context Protocol, server architecture, configuration, and building custom MCP servers. m3-04 Custom Agents & Agent Profiles Advanced 3 hrs Checks JavaScript LSP results and a live test-only agent that stops at a source-code conflict. m3-05 Agent Skills & the Copilot Ecosystem Advanced 3 hrs Tests live skills, compares interviews before /plan, and reviews scoped Chronicle suggestions.

docs.title: Module 4: DevOps & Infrastructure with Copilot (Intermediate to Advanced)
docs.text: # Session Difficulty Duration Summary m4-01 GitHub Actions & Workflow Generation Intermediate 3 hrs Carries one Node.js application through CI generation, deployment design, workflow repair, and custom-action validation. m4-02 Infrastructure as Code with Copilot Advanced 2 hrs 30 min Builds, connects, validates, and security-reviews Terraform modules. Bicep is an optional comparison. m4-03 CI/CD Pipeline Debugging & Agentic Remediation Advanced 3 hrs Diagnoses pipeline failures from logs and local checks, including a staged failure and reviewed security remediation.

docs.title: Module 5: Specification-Driven Frameworks (Advanced)
docs.text: # Session Difficulty Duration Summary m5-01 Brady's Squad: Human-Led AI Teams Advanced 3 hrs Uses Squad to assign scoped work to persistent roles and save decisions and results for review. m5-02 Spec Kit: Specification-Driven Development Advanced 3.5 hrs Uses Spec Kit for task-to-issue conversion, staged implementation, convergence, and living-spec evolution. m5-03 HVE Core: Evidence-Led Delivery with RPI Advanced 4 hrs Uses HVE Research, Plan, Implement, Review, and Follow-up to develop one API feature and submit it for a human decision.

docs.title: Module 6: Advanced Topics & Capstone (Advanced)
docs.text: # Session Difficulty Duration Summary m6-01 Build Reliable Agent Applications with the GitHub Copilot SDK Advanced 3 hrs Builds a TypeScript agent application with streaming, a custom tool, permission decisions, blocking hooks, tests, and OpenTelemetry traces. m6-02 End-to-End Capstone Project Advanced 3 hrs Connects governance, specification, agentic delivery, review, and handover in one integration scenario.

docs.title: Module 7: Product and Delivery Teams (Beginner to Intermediate)
docs.text:
# Session Difficulty Duration Summary m7-01 Work Effectively in the GitHub Copilot App Beginner 3 hrs Uses repository context, inspects available capabilities, and creates a reviewed working brief. m7-02 Interview Ideas and Shape Better Work Beginner 3 hrs Turns an unclear request into a repository decision brief and approved GitHub issue proposal. m7-03 Plan Work with GitHub Issues and MCP Intermediate 3 hrs Creates and checks a GitHub issue plan through the GitHub MCP server. m7-04 Build and Use a Planning Canvas Intermediate 3 hrs Creates a planning canvas and aligns its visible state with GitHub issues. m7-05 Orchestrate Agents and Workstreams Intermediate 3 hrs Supervises live child sessions over GitHub issues, or local code and PR snapshots in the developer route. m7-06 Automate Delivery Follow-up and Connect Work Systems Intermediate 3 hrs Runs one draft-only Automation and records whether GitHub or Azure Boards remains authoritative.

Total track duration: 88 hours across 29 sessions

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
1. Read the curriculum plan to see what each session teaches and which sessions come first. Use the glossary for product and workflow terms.

  2. Check track-template/ to see how a session is organized. Every session follows the same format.

  3. Browse the learning tracks and choose one that fits your audience's role and experience. Product and Delivery Teams and HVE Engineering have dedicated paths.

  4. Pick your path:

Audience Recommended Path Sessions Duration Copilot Beginners Module 1 01 to 03 9 hrs Copilot Practitioners Modules 1 to 2 + developer orchestration 01 to 07, 29, 24, 27, 26 33 hrs Agentic Developers Modules 1 to 3 + developer orchestration 01 to 12, 29, 24 42 hrs DevOps Engineers Module 1 + Session m2-02 + Module 4 01 to 05, 13 to 15 21 hrs SDK Application Developers Modules 1 to 3 + Session m6-01 01 to 12, 17 39 hrs Product and Delivery Teams Module 7 20 to 25 18 hrs HVE Practitioners HVE Engineering 01 to 07, 10 to 11, 28 31 hrs Full Track All Modules All available sessions 88 hrs
  1. Prepare your environment:
  2. GitHub Enterprise Cloud organization with Copilot enabled according to customer policy
  3. Pre-configured repositories for each lab (see individual session READMEs)
  4. VS Code with GitHub Copilot and GitHub Copilot Chat extensions

  5. GitHub Copilot app for sessions that use canvases or orchestration

  6. Use the trainer notes to teach each session. Afterwards, update the materials based on what worked and where learners needed help.

docs.title: Adding or moving sessions
docs.text:
Use module-local session IDs: m1-01 through m7-NN. The number after the hyphen starts at 01 in each module. Directories use sessions/session-m2-01-copilot-cli/.

Add a new session after the last ID in its module. Keep catalog entries and navigation grouped by module, even when a session is added later. Tracks can choose a different teaching order without changing session IDs.

Follow the session template in track-template/README.md and update the catalog, curriculum plan, navigation, relevant tracks, and prerequisites together. Keep existing IDs stable once published.

docs.title: GitHub Copilot & Agentic Workflows: Train-the-Trainer Curriculum Plan
Overall learning objectives
docs.text:
After this curriculum, you should be able to:

  1. Explain GitHub Copilot's architecture, capabilities, model ecosystem, and limitations to technical audiences
  2. Demonstrate inline suggestions, Chat, agent mode, and Spaces in live coding sessions
  3. Teach prompt engineering techniques for Copilot's IDE, CLI, and app workflows
  4. Guide teams through agentic workflows: IDE agent mode, canvases, cloud agent, custom agents, and MCP integration
  5. Build custom agents (.github/agents/), agent skills (.github/skills/), canvas extensions, and MCP server integrations
  6. Automate GitHub Actions, IaC (Terraform/Bicep), and CI/CD workflows with Copilot assistance
  7. Orchestrate multi-agent teams using optional tools such as Squad for advanced agentic automation
  8. Apply specification-driven development to turn enterprise requirements into governed delivery artifacts
  9. Run hands-on labs where trainees build real projects using the full Copilot toolchain
  10. Assess trainee progress and adapt delivery based on audience skill level and domain focus
  11. Teach product and delivery teams to use the GitHub Copilot app, save plans in repository files, and supervise agent work without programming
  12. Use GitHub MCP, canvases, orchestration, and Automations with human review and result checks

docs.title: Modules and tracks
docs.text:
The curriculum has 7 modules. Use Modules 1 to 3 as the technical core. Combine the role-based and technical electives in Modules 4 to 7 to suit your audience.

Module 1: Copilot Fundamentals ──────────────── (Beginner, 3 sessions)
    │
Module 2: Copilot in Practice ──────────────── (Intermediate to Advanced, 7 sessions)
    │
Module 3: Agentic Workflows ───────────────── (Advanced, 5 sessions)
    │
    ├── Module 4: DevOps & Infrastructure ──── (Intermediate to Advanced, 3 sessions)
    │   └── Requires: Module 1 + Session m2-02
    │
    ├── Module 5: Specification-Driven Frameworks ─ (Advanced, 3 sessions)
    │   └── Uses Squad, Spec Kit, and HVE as worked framework examples
    │
    └── Module 6: Advanced Topics & Capstone ─────── (Advanced, 2 sessions)
        └── Session m6-01 is independent; Session m5-02 is required before the capstone

Module 7: Product and Delivery Teams ─────────────── (Beginner to Intermediate, 6 sessions)
    └── Standalone role-based path; no programming prerequisite
