docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m1-02: Copilot Chat & inline suggestions
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Copilot Fundamentals

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Session m1-01

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content, 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use Copilot Chat to understand, diagnose, fix, test, and review one calculator module. You will move between sidebar Chat, inline Chat, terminal context, and workspace context. The requirements and checks from Session 1 still apply.

The project contains a weighted-average defect and a later zero-total-weight change request. Record the context and prompts that helped, then check every change with standard-library tests.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Choose a Chat surface that matches the task.
  • Use selected code, files, terminal output, and workspace search as context.
  • Use task shortcuts such as explain, fix, tests, and documentation when the current surface offers them.
  • Refine a conversation without broadening the requested change.
  • Compare model choices allowed by policy against the same tests when more than one choice is available.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Learners need GitHub Copilot Chat and Python 3.10 or later. If either is unavailable, stop the lab.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/ Slides slides.md Lab lab/ Starter project lab/starter/ Reference result lab/solution/

docs.title: Use the right context, then check the change
docs.text: Session m1-02 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time Inline suggestions and Chat 6 min Choose a Chat surface 10 min Select context deliberately 11 min Explain, fix, test, document 10 min Conversational refinement 8 min Model and metering decisions 7 min Debugging demo and handoff 8 min

docs.title: Two interaction modes
docs.text:
Inline suggestions Chat Draft at the cursor Respond to an explicit request Best for the next small edit Best for explanation and multi-step work Context comes from the editing surface Context can be selected or named

Both produce proposals that need review.

docs.title: Choose the surface by the work
docs.text:
Work Useful surface Multi-step diagnosis Sidebar Chat Change selected code Inline Chat Ask one short question Lightweight or quick surface Explain recent command output Terminal context

Use the controls available in the editor.

docs.title: Sidebar and inline Chat
docs.text:
Sidebar Chat

  • keeps a task thread visible;
  • supports follow-up questions;
  • works well for cross-file reasoning.

Inline Chat

  • starts from selected code;
  • shows an edit close to the source;
  • fits a narrow change.

docs.title: Quick and terminal context
docs.text:
A lightweight surface is useful when history is unnecessary.

Terminal context is useful for:

  • a failed test command;
  • an unfamiliar error;
  • the next command to check the result.

Read the actual output before acting on the summary.

docs.title: Context should be explicit
docs.text:
Weak:

Fix this.

Reviewable:

The weighted-average test expects 95 but receives 140.
Inspect the selected method and focused test.
Identify the defect without changing other methods.

docs.title: Workspace, file, selection, terminal
docs.text:
Context Use it for Selection One function or block Named file Known cross-file dependency Workspace search Broad structure or usage Terminal output Recent command results

Include the context the task needs.

docs.title: Explain before changing
docs.text:
Ask for:

  1. the current formula;
  2. the role of each guard;
  3. the failing example;
  4. the exact mismatch.

An explanation can expose a wrong assumption before code changes.

docs.title: Fix narrowly
docs.text:
Fix only weighted_average so it divides by total weight.
Preserve the method signature and length check.
Add no dependency.

Scope is part of correctness.

docs.title: Generated tests need review
docs.text:
Check whether each test:

  • states accepted behavior;
  • would fail for the original defect;
  • calculates the expected value correctly;
  • avoids invented requirements;
  • uses existing tools.

Check the expected behavior too. A generated test can encode the same mistake as the code.

docs.title: Refine one concern at a time
docs.text:
Explain
   ↓
Diagnose
   ↓
Fix one behavior
   ↓
Add focused tests
   ↓
Review the complete method

Focused turns make mistakes easier to locate.

docs.title: Know when to restart
docs.text:
Continue the thread when:

  • the task is unchanged;
  • the useful context remains accurate;
  • the current structure is sound.

Start fresh when stale assumptions keep returning.

docs.title: Compare against the task
docs.text:
If policy allows two available model choices:

  1. use the same synthetic prompt;
  2. keep the same context;
  3. run the same tests;
  4. compare correctness and useful citations.

Judge the results by the checks, not how well they read.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
The live path requires Chat access allowed by your organization.

When access or comparison is unavailable:

  • inspect the code manually;
  • write the intended prompts in chat-notes.md;
  • implement and test the same change;
  • compare with the reference solution.

docs.title: Demo: weighted average
docs.text:
weighted_sum = sum(
    value * weight
    for value, weight in zip(values, weights)
)
return weighted_sum / len(values)

For [80, 100] with weights [1, 3], the denominator must be 4.

docs.title: Failure to fix
docs.text:
Expected: 95
Actual:   140

The focused test gives Chat a concrete symptom. The reviewed fix changes the denominator to the total weight.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
You will use one calculator project to:

  1. reproduce the defect;
  2. explain and diagnose it;
  3. apply a narrow fix;
  4. review generated tests;
  5. use workspace and terminal context;
  6. decide zero-total-weight behavior;
  7. run the full suite.

Deliverable: corrected code, passing tests, and a Chat decision record.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m1-02 lab: Diagnose and extend a calculator with Chat
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Session m1-01 and Python 3.10 or later

Deliverable: A corrected and extended calculator, a passing test suite, and a completed chat-notes.md

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will use different Chat surfaces on one Python calculator project. A focused test exposes a weighted-average bug. After fixing it, you will add missing tests, answer a workspace question, and handle a change request that requires a judgment about zero total weight.

Part Work Time 1 Prepare the project and reproduce the failure 15 min 2 Explain and diagnose the defect 25 min 3 Apply the fix and expand tests 30 min 4 Review the project with workspace and terminal context 20 min 5 Decide and implement the change request 20 min 6 Compare, document, and check 10 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Use synthetic data in a training repository you may use for the exercise.

Before starting, check GitHub Copilot Chat access in your editor. If Chat does not work, stop the lab. Manual implementation does not replace the Chat and inline-suggestion practice.

If model comparison is allowed, use only choices approved for the exercise and set any required metered-work stop condition. If no second choice is available, compare the assisted result with the reference solution.

docs.title: Part 1: Prepare and reproduce (15 minutes)
docs.text:
cd sessions/session-m1-02-chat-and-inline/lab/starter
python -m py_compile calculator.py test_calculator.py
python -m unittest -v

Three tests should pass. The weighted-average test should fail because the result is 190 instead of 95.

Read calculator.py, test_calculator.py, change-request.md, and chat-notes.md.

Checkpoint: You can state the failing input, actual result, and expected result without asking Chat to guess them.

docs.title: Part 2: Explain and diagnose (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Use inline Chat or the sidebar with the weighted_average selection.

Start with an explanation request:

Explain the weighted_average method line by line. State the mathematical formula
it implements. Do not propose a fix yet.

Compare the response with the failing test. Then ask:

The test expects weighted_average([80, 100], [1, 3]) to equal 95, but the method
returns 140. Identify the defect. Limit the answer to this method.

If the surface supports an explain shortcut, try it with the same selection. Record the useful context and the diagnosis in chat-notes.md.

Checkpoint: The diagnosis identifies sum(weights) as the denominator.

docs.title: Part 3: Fix and expand tests (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Request a narrow fix:

Fix only weighted_average so it divides by the total weight. Preserve the public
method signature and the existing length check. Add no dependency.

Review the proposed diff before accepting it. Run:

python -m unittest -v \
  test_calculator.CalculatorTests.test_weighted_average_uses_total_weight

Next, use a tests shortcut or a direct prompt to propose tests for:

  • mismatched list lengths;
  • empty lists;
  • history recording;
  • a zero total weight.

Do not accept tests that invent behavior. Leave the zero-total-weight rule for the change request in Part 5.

Checkpoint: The original four tests pass. Proposed new tests are separated from the accepted contract.

docs.title: Part 4: Use workspace and terminal context (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Ask a workspace-level question:

@workspace Summarize the Calculator public behavior and identify which methods
have focused tests. Cite the relevant files.

If the current surface uses a different workspace-context mechanism, use its documented equivalent.

Run the tests again. Then use terminal context, if available:

Explain the most recent test result. Which behavior failed or passed, and which
file owns the next change?

Check the response yourself. Terminal context can summarize output; it does not replace reading the failure.

Checkpoint: Your notes distinguish code behavior, test output, and Chat interpretation.

docs.title: Part 5: Decide the change request (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Open change-request.md.

The request says to reject a zero total weight but leaves the exception type and message to you. Choose both. The reference solution uses:

ValueError("Total weight must not be zero")

Add a focused test first. Then update weighted_average. While reviewing the method, also decide how empty inputs should behave. Record both decisions in chat-notes.md.

Run:

python -m unittest -v

Checkpoint: The suite covers the original defect, mismatch, empty input, zero total weight, and history.

docs.title: Part 6: Compare and check (10 minutes)
docs.text:
If you may use two model choices, send both the same prompt:

Review weighted_average and its tests. List any accepted behavior that lacks a
test. Do not change code.

Compare only accuracy you can check and useful citations. Otherwise compare the Chat-assisted or manual result with lab/solution/.

Inspect the final diff:

git --no-pager diff -- calculator.py test_calculator.py chat-notes.md
python -m py_compile calculator.py test_calculator.py
python -m unittest -v

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
1. calculator.py uses total weight and rejects invalid weighted-average inputs.
  2. test_calculator.py covers the accepted behavior.
  3. chat-notes.md records the chosen surfaces, prompts, check results, judgment call, and comparison path.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Both Python files compile.
  • All eight reference tests pass.
  • The code, test, and notes state the zero-total-weight decision.
  • Chat changes stayed inside the calculator project.
  • No new dependency was added.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m1-02 trainer guide: Copilot Chat & inline suggestions
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Show the context available in each Chat surface. Use the same tests and review standards throughout the calculator exercise.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text:
Time Segment 0:00 to 0:06 Inline suggestions and Chat 0:06 to 0:16 Choose a Chat surface 0:16 to 0:27 Select context deliberately 0:27 to 0:37 Explain, fix, test, and document 0:37 to 0:45 Conversational refinement 0:45 to 0:52 Model and metering decisions 0:52 to 1:00 Prepared debugging demo and lab handoff

The timings match slides.md.

docs.title: Before delivery
docs.text:
• Run the starter suite and check for one expected failure.
  • Run the solution suite and check for eight passing tests.
  • Check which Chat surfaces learners may use in the selected editor.
  • Check current context-reference and shortcut syntax in official documentation.
  • Check whether a model comparison is permitted.
  • Prepare screenshots for demo recovery. They do not replace learner access.

Avoid fixed model catalogs, prices, keyboard shortcuts, or claims that a surface always sees a particular context source.

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:06: Inline suggestions and Chat
docs.text:
Slides: Copilot Chat & Inline Suggestions, Agenda, Two interaction modes

Remind learners that Session m1-01 used suggestions at the cursor. Now show how to ask for work in a conversation. Both paths still require a task, review, and checks.

docs.title: 0:06 to 0:16: Choose a surface
docs.text:
Slides: Choose the surface by the work, Sidebar and inline Chat, Quick and terminal context

Use the current editor to show the available surfaces. Teach the decision:

  • use sidebar Chat for a multi-step thread;
  • use inline Chat for a selected edit;
  • use a lightweight surface for a short question;
  • use terminal context for recent command output.

Do not make the shortcut the lesson. Product controls change.

docs.title: 0:16 to 0:27: Select context
docs.text:
Slides: Context should be explicit, Workspace, file, selection, terminal

Open the calculator project. Compare:

Fix this.

with:

The weighted-average test expects 95 but receives 140. Inspect the selected method
and the focused test. Identify the defect without changing other methods.

Point out that the second request names the symptom, expected behavior, scope, and failing test.

Explain the role of:

  • selected code for a local question;
  • named files for a specific cross-file question;
  • workspace search for architecture or usage;
  • terminal output for a recent failure.

docs.title: 0:27 to 0:37: Common task actions
docs.text:
Slides: Explain before changing, Fix narrowly, Generated tests need review

Demonstrate the current equivalents of explain, fix, tests, and documentation actions. They are shortcuts, not separate quality standards.

For generated tests, ask:

  • Does the test state accepted behavior?
  • Would it fail for the original defect?
  • Did it add a package or invent a requirement?
  • Is the expected value independently correct?

docs.title: 0:37 to 0:45: Conversational refinement
docs.text:
Slides: Refine one concern at a time, Know when to restart

Use this sequence:

  1. Explain the current formula.
  2. Identify the denominator defect.
  3. Fix only the denominator.
  4. Add tests for accepted edge cases.
  5. Review the whole method.

Continue a thread while the task and assumptions remain stable. Start a new thread when stale context is steering the answer.

docs.title: 0:45 to 0:52: Model and metering decisions
docs.text:
Slides: Compare against the task, Access policy

Use the default model allowed by policy unless the exercise permits another choice. If comparison is allowed, send the same synthetic prompt and judge the responses against the same tests. Otherwise, compare with the reference solution.

Do not infer access, cost, or data behavior from a label.

docs.title: 0:52 to 1:00: Prepared debugging demo
docs.text:
Slides: Demo: weighted average, Failure to fix, Lab handoff

Commands:

cd sessions/session-m1-02-chat-and-inline/lab/starter
python -m unittest -v

Demo sequence:

  1. Read the failing test.
  2. Ask for an explanation without a fix.
  3. Ask for a diagnosis constrained to weighted_average.
  4. Review the one-method diff.
  5. Run the focused test.
  6. Ask workspace context to summarize behavior and coverage.
  7. Open the change request but leave it for the lab.

docs.title: Teaching points
docs.text:
• A surface changes interaction and available context.
  • Naming the context reduces guessing.
  • A shortcut can draft work, but accepted behavior still comes from the task and tests.
  • Generated tests can encode the wrong requirement.
  • Model comparison is useful only when the task, prompt, and checks stay constant.
  • Read the terminal output yourself rather than relying on its summary.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Should I keep every task in one thread?

Keep related work together. Start fresh when assumptions or topic change.

Why did workspace context miss a file?

Search and retrieval may miss relevant files. Check citations and name the files when you know the scope.

Can Chat fix the project without tests?

It can propose a change. Without checks, confidence stays low.

What if a shortcut is absent?

Use a direct prompt with the same task and context.

docs.title: Lab readiness check
docs.text:
• The starter failure is reproducible.
  • Required Copilot Chat access is checked.
  • The permitted comparison path is known.
  • Learners know where to record prompts and check results.
  • The change request remains closed until Part 5.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m1-03: Prompt engineering fundamentals
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Copilot Fundamentals

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-02

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content, 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Build one todo API by improving prompts as the project evolves. Use intent, context, constraints, and examples to implement a store and Express routes. Then add priority filtering and record how context affected the proposal.

A useful prompt is only the start. The generated work still has to pass the project tests and API checks.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Write prompts that state the task, relevant context, boundaries, and examples.
  • Refine a useful result without mixing unrelated concerns.
  • Use CLI /refine and check that its rewrite preserves the intended task.
  • Use comments and neighboring files as deliberate context.
  • Recognize vague, overloaded, and untrusted instructions.
  • Turn a successful project prompt into a reusable pattern.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Learners need GitHub Copilot Chat, inline suggestions, the standalone CLI with /refine, Node.js 22 or later, and the declared npm dependency. Set up the CLI before delivery; Session m2-01 is not a prerequisite. If a requirement is unavailable, stop the lab.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/ Slides slides.md Lab lab/ Starter project lab/starter/api-starter/ Reference result lab/solution/api-complete/

docs.title: Make the work reviewable before asking for code
docs.text: Session m1-03 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time Prompting as task design 7 min Four prompt components 13 min Comments and context 9 min Iterative refinement 10 min Anti-patterns and untrusted instructions 9 min Todo-store demonstration 8 min Patterns and lab handoff 4 min

docs.title: A prompt is a work request
docs.text:
Weak:

Build the todo feature.

The model must guess which file to change, how it should behave, how to handle errors, which dependencies it may use, and when the work is done.

A useful prompt states the decisions that affect the result.

docs.title: Four useful components
docs.text:
Intent       What change is needed?
Context      What should inform the work?
Constraints  What boundaries must hold?
Examples     What does accepted behavior look like?

Use only the components the task needs.

docs.title: Intent
docs.text:
Name the action and scope:

Implement TodoStore.create in lib/todo-store.js.

Better than:

Make the store work.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Useful context can include:

  • a focused test;
  • a related file;
  • the actual failure;
  • an accepted design decision;
  • repository instructions.

Include enough context to reduce guessing. Leave out files that obscure the task.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
State boundaries that affect the result:

Use plain JavaScript.
Add no package.
Change only TodoStore.create.
Return a copy of stored data.

Scope and dependency limits are part of correctness.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Input:
{ title: "  Write clear prompts  " }

Expected:
{
  id: 1,
  title: "Write clear prompts",
  status: "pending",
  priority: "normal"
}

Examples make behavior concrete.

docs.title: A reviewable prompt
docs.text:
Implement only TodoStore.create in lib/todo-store.js.
Use the focused test as the contract.
Trim the title, apply the documented defaults, return a copy,
and add no package.
Run the focused create test when done.

It states the task without dictating every line.

docs.title: Comments can carry intent
docs.text:
// POST /todos
// Create a todo from JSON input.
// Return 201 on success.
// Return 400 with { error: message } for invalid input.

A useful comment describes behavior and boundaries.

docs.title: Neighboring files are context, not a contract
docs.text:
Opening examples/response-shapes.js may influence a route suggestion.

It does not override:

  • the route comment;
  • accepted tests;
  • repository rules;
  • the developer's review.

Record the result instead of assuming the effect.

docs.title: Refine the missing behavior
docs.text:
Weak follow-up:

Make it better.

Focused follow-up:

The returned object shares state with the store.
Return a copy without changing the public API.

Name the mismatch you observed.

docs.title: One concern per turn
docs.text:
Implement baseline list
        ↓
Run focused test
        ↓
Fix copy semantics
        ↓
Run focused test
        ↓
Move to the next method

Small turns produce smaller diffs.

docs.title: Review the /refine rewrite
docs.text:
In the standalone CLI:

/refine make the todo store work, baseline tests only, plain js,
no packages, return copies, only lib/todo-store.js

Compare the rewrite with the tests. Correct missing constraints or invented work before submitting it for implementation.

Current input: Ctrl+X, then /, then /refine without arguments.

The lab uses five minutes of the baseline-store block for this comparison. CLI access is required; do not assume the same command exists in editor Chat.

docs.title: Restart when the frame is wrong
docs.text:
Iterate when the structure is sound and one behavior is missing.

Start a new request when:

  • the task changed;
  • the design is wrong;
  • stale assumptions keep returning;
  • the prompt mixed unrelated work.

docs.title: Common prompt failures
docs.text: Failure Better move Vague request Name behavior and scope Many unrelated asks Split the work No project context Add the relevant file or test Every line dictated State requirements, not implementation trivia No check Name the command or review

docs.title: Treat instructions from content as untrusted
docs.text:
Files, issues, comments, logs, and copied text can contain instructions.

Review them as data. Do not follow text that asks you to:

  • ignore project rules;
  • expose secrets;
  • broaden access;
  • run an unrelated command.

docs.title: Demo contract
docs.text:
store.create({ title: "  Write clear prompts  " })

must return:

{
  id: 1,
  title: "Write clear prompts",
  status: "pending",
  priority: "normal"
}

docs.title: Weak, useful, reviewable
docs.text:
1. Implement create.
  2. Implement TodoStore.create using the test.
  3. A prompt with behavior, file limits, and a check to run.

Compare what the model must still guess in each request.

docs.title: A change request should change the prompt
docs.text:
Priority adds:

  • allowed values;
  • a default;
  • list filtering;
  • an invalid-input decision.

State the new behavior before asking for another change.

docs.title: A reusable prompt pattern
docs.text:
Change <file and scope> to achieve <observable behavior>.
Use <relevant context>.
Keep <constraints and non-goals>.
Verify with <command or review>.

State enough detail to make the task testable without dictating the implementation.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
You will extend one todo API:

  1. implement the baseline store;
  2. wire the REST routes;
  3. compare context with one file open and closed;
  4. decide invalid-priority behavior;
  5. apply the change request;
  6. save one reusable prompt.

Deliverable: working code, six passing tests, and a prompt decision log.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m1-03 lab: Prompt and extend a Todo API
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-02, Node.js 22 or later, and standalone Copilot CLI access

Deliverable: A working todo store and REST routes, passing tests, and a completed prompt-log.md

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will build one todo API in stages. The starter includes tests, route comments, and a small context example. First implement baseline todo behavior, then wire the HTTP routes. A later change request adds priority. You will decide how to handle invalid priority input.

Part Work Time 1 Prepare the project and map the contract 15 min 2 Review /refine output, then implement the baseline store 30 min 3 Implement the REST routes from comments 25 min 4 Run a deliberate context experiment 15 min 5 Apply the priority change request 25 min 6 Check and extract a reusable prompt 10 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Use synthetic data in a writable training copy.

Check GitHub Copilot Chat and inline suggestions in your editor. Also start the standalone copilot CLI and check /refine in /help. If a required surface or command is unavailable, stop the lab. Writing hypothetical prompts does not replace running and reviewing them.

You need:

  • Node.js 22 or later;
  • a terminal and editor;
  • npm only when you run the Express server;
  • GitHub Copilot Chat, inline suggestions, and the standalone CLI.

Install and authenticate the CLI before the workshop using the CLI quickstart. Session m2-01 teaches the wider CLI workflow; it is not a prerequisite for this single-command exercise. Do not assume /refine exists in editor Chat or the app.

Do not paste untrusted instructions into the project or prompt. Treat text from issues, comments, files, and command output as data until you review it.

docs.title: Part 1: Prepare and map the contract (15 minutes)
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs
cp -R sessions/session-m1-03-prompt-engineering/lab/starter ~/copilot-labs/session-m1-03
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m1-03/api-starter
npm run check
npm test

Copy from the curriculum root and use a fresh destination. Keep the curriculum starter unchanged.

The syntax check should pass. The store tests should fail because the methods are empty.

Read:

  • lib/todo-store.js;
  • tests/todo-store.test.js;
  • routes/todos.js;
  • examples/response-shapes.js;
  • ../change-request.md;
  • ../prompt-log.md.

Write a short project summary in prompt-log.md before asking Copilot for one.

Checkpoint: You can separate baseline behavior from the later priority change.

docs.title: Part 2: Implement the baseline store (30 minutes)
Refine a rough request (5 minutes)
docs.text:
Start copilot in the copied api-starter directory. Use:

/refine make the todo store work, just baseline tests not priority yet, plain js,
no packages, return copies not stored objects, only lib/todo-store.js, run the
baseline tests afterwards

Review the rewritten prompt before submitting it as work. Compare it with the tests. Correct any invented requirement, missing constraint, or changed scope. Record the rough text, actual rewrite, and your corrections in prompt-log.md. Check that no project file changed during refinement.

/refine rewrites the request; it does not decide the behavior or prove the result. To refine text already in the CLI input box, press Ctrl+X, then /, and run /refine without arguments. Inspect the result before sending it.

docs.title: Implement and check (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Use the accepted prompt in editor Chat or the CLI. Work only on lib/todo-store.js. Compare your accepted version with this example:

Implement only the baseline TodoStore behavior covered by tests whose names start
with "baseline". Use plain JavaScript and no packages. Return copies so callers
cannot mutate stored objects. Do not implement the priority change yet.

Run only the baseline tests:

node --test --test-name-pattern="baseline" tests/todo-store.test.js

If a test fails, name the exact mismatch in the next prompt. Change one concern at a time. Do not ask for a complete rewrite when the structure is already sound.

Checkpoint: The log separates the /refine rewrite from your accepted prompt. Four baseline tests pass. The change tests still fail.

docs.title: Part 3: Implement the REST routes (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open routes/todos.js. The comments state the route contract. Use each comment as an inline prompt, one handler at a time.

For Chat, use a prompt such as:

Implement only GET /todos in routes/todos.js. Use the existing TodoStore instance.
Map validation errors to status 400 with { error: message }. Do not change the
store or add middleware.

Repeat for get-by-ID, create, update, and delete. Review status codes and response shapes before accepting.

Install the declared dependency only if you will run the server:

npm install
npm start

In another terminal:

curl http://localhost:3000/
curl http://localhost:3000/todos
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/todos \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Review the API"}'

Stop the server after the checks.

Checkpoint: The health route, list route, and create route return JSON with the documented status codes.

docs.title: Part 4: Run the context experiment (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Delete or undo one route handler so it can be proposed again.

  1. Close examples/response-shapes.js.
  2. Request the handler with only the route comment visible.
  3. Record the proposed error shape without accepting it.
  4. Open examples/response-shapes.js.
  5. Request the same handler again with the same wording.
  6. Record any difference.

The context may change the proposal, or it may not. Record either result. Keep the implementation that matches the route contract.

Checkpoint: prompt-log.md records the two contexts and what you observed.

docs.title: Part 5: Apply the priority change (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open ../change-request.md.

The request defines allowed values and filtering. Decide how to handle invalid priority values before editing. The reference solution rejects invalid priority with:

Priority must be one of: low, normal, high

Add or review the change tests, then prompt for the smallest update:

Add the accepted priority behavior to TodoStore and the list route. Preserve all
baseline behavior. Default new todos to normal. Reject other values with the exact
message in the test. Add no package.

Run:

npm test
npm run check

Checkpoint: All six tests pass, and the route supports a priority query filter.

docs.title: Part 6: Check and extract a reusable prompt (10 minutes)
docs.text:
Inspect the complete project diff:

git --no-pager diff -- \
  lib/todo-store.js routes/todos.js tests/todo-store.test.js ../prompt-log.md
npm run check
npm test

Write one reusable prompt in prompt-log.md. It should state the exact file, task, constraints, accepted behavior, and check command without restating the implementation line by line.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
1. lib/todo-store.js implements baseline and priority behavior.
  2. routes/todos.js maps store results to the documented HTTP responses.
  3. tests/todo-store.test.js passes all six tests.
  4. prompt-log.md records the /refine comparison, iterations, the context experiment, the invalid-priority decision, and one reusable prompt.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• npm run check succeeds.
  • npm test passes six tests.
  • /refine ran in the CLI; its rewrite was checked before implementation.
  • Baseline behavior still passes after the priority change.
  • The code, tests, and notes state the invalid-priority behavior.
  • No package beyond the declared Express dependency was added.
  • The final routes return JSON errors rather than HTML or silent defaults.

docs.title: Session m1-03 trainer guide: Prompt engineering fundamentals
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Teach learners to design the task before writing the prompt. Show how to state the work, choose relevant context, set boundaries, and give a useful example. Refine one concern at a time.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text:
Time Segment 0:00 to 0:07 Prompting as task design 0:07 to 0:20 Intent, context, constraints, and examples 0:20 to 0:29 Comments and neighboring-file context 0:29 to 0:39 Iterative refinement 0:39 to 0:48 Prompt anti-patterns and untrusted instructions 0:48 to 0:56 Prepared todo-store demonstration 0:56 to 1:00 Reusable patterns and lab handoff

The timings match slides.md.

docs.title: Before delivery
docs.text:
• Check Node.js 22 or later and standalone CLI authentication.
  • Run starter syntax checks.
  • Run the solution tests.
  • Prepare a demo copy of the todo store.
  • Check GitHub Copilot Chat and inline-suggestion access.
  • Check /refine in CLI /help; do not substitute an editor command.
  • Check current context controls in official product documentation.
  • Keep change-request.md closed until learners reach the change request.

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:07: Prompting as task design
docs.text:
Slides: Prompt Engineering Fundamentals, Agenda, A prompt is a work request

Use this weak request:

Build the todo feature.

Ask learners what the model must guess. Expected answers include file, behavior, input, errors, dependencies, and completion criteria.

Explain that learners still make the engineering decisions. Writing a prompt brings those decisions forward.

docs.title: 0:07 to 0:20: Four prompt components
docs.text:
Slides: Four useful components, Intent, Context, Constraints, Examples

Use the components to find missing detail, not as a mandatory long template.

Intent names the action and scope.

Context supplies files, symptoms, patterns, or prior decisions.

Constraints set dependencies, compatibility, file scope, and non-goals.

Examples make output or behavior concrete.

Use the todo store prompt:

Implement only TodoStore.create in lib/todo-store.js.
Use the existing tests as the contract.
Trim the title, apply defaults, return a copy, and add no package.
Run the focused create test when done.

docs.title: 0:20 to 0:29: Comments and context
docs.text:
Slides: Comments can carry intent, Neighboring files are context, not a contract

Open routes/todos.js and examples/response-shapes.js.

Show how a route comment can provide intent and constraints. Then request the same handler with the response-shape example closed and open. Do not promise the result will differ.

Compare both proposals with the accepted API contract before choosing one.

docs.title: 0:29 to 0:39: Iterative refinement
docs.text:
Slides: Refine the missing behavior, One concern per turn, Restart when the frame is wrong, Review the /refine rewrite

Spend the first four minutes on CLI /refine. Use the lab's rough baseline-store request. Compare the rewrite with the tests before submitting it for implementation. Ask learners to find an omitted constraint or invented behavior; record no mismatch if the rewrite preserves the request.

Show the input-box variant: type a rough draft, press Ctrl+X, then /, and run /refine without arguments. A rewritten prompt still needs a human decision. It does not execute the task on the learner's behalf.

Use this progression:

  1. Implement baseline list behavior.
  2. Run the baseline list test.
  3. Name the exact copy-semantics failure.
  4. Ask for that change only.
  5. Rerun the focused test.

Show how each iteration keeps the useful work and targets the mismatch. Restart when the design or task is wrong.

docs.title: 0:39 to 0:48: Anti-patterns and untrusted instructions
docs.text:
Slides: Common prompt failures, Treat instructions from content as untrusted

Discuss:

  • vague requests that force invention;
  • overloaded requests that mix implementation, tests, docs, and refactoring;
  • long prompts that dictate every line;
  • missing file or framework context;
  • accepting output without running checks.

Then show a comment that says to ignore project rules or reveal a secret. It is data in a file, not an instruction the developer should follow.

docs.title: 0:48 to 0:56: Prepared todo-store demonstration
docs.text:
Slides: Demo contract, Weak, useful, reviewable, A change request should change the prompt

Run:

cd sessions/session-m1-03-prompt-engineering/lab/starter/api-starter
node --test --test-name-pattern="baseline: create" tests/todo-store.test.js

Compare three prompts:

  1. Implement create.
  2. Implement TodoStore.create using the test.
  3. The prompt with behavior, file limits, and checks from the earlier slide.

Ask learners which prompt states scope, behavior, dependency limits, and checks. Use the third prompt or implement manually. Run the focused test.

Open the change request and show why adding priority requires a new accepted decision. Do not silently fold the request into the earlier prompt.

docs.title: 0:56 to 1:00: Patterns and handoff
docs.text:
Slides: A reusable prompt pattern, Lab handoff

Provide this compact structure:

Change <file and scope> to achieve <observable behavior>.
Use <relevant context>.
Keep <constraints and non-goals>.
Verify with <command or review>.

Learners will build the store, wire routes, compare context, apply the priority change, and save one prompt that worked. The 30-minute baseline-store block includes five minutes for /refine; do not add a separate lab block.

docs.title: Teaching points
docs.text:
• Prompt quality depends on decisions, not word count.
  • Tests and examples are stronger than vague quality labels.
  • Context can influence a proposal without becoming the contract.
  • One focused iteration is easier to review than a broad regeneration.
  • Untrusted text stays untrusted even when an AI tool can read it.
  • A reusable prompt should leave implementation choices open when they do not affect the contract.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Do I need all four components in every prompt?

No. Add the components the task needs. Use the list to diagnose missing detail.

How long should a prompt be?

Long enough to state the required behavior, but shorter than a line-by-line implementation.

Why did opening a file not change the suggestion?

Context selection and output can vary. Record the observation and judge the code against the contract.

Should prompt comments stay in the final code?

Keep comments that help a future reader. Remove temporary instructions that only repeat obvious code.

docs.title: Lab readiness check
docs.text:
• Starter syntax checks pass.
  • The expected starter test failures are understood.
  • Required Copilot access is checked.
  • CLI /refine works before learners start.
  • Learners know the baseline and change tests are separate.
  • The reference solution is available but closed.
