docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m2-02: Agent mode in the IDE
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Copilot in Practice Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 Duration: 3 hours (1 hr trainer content + 2 hr lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Build and extend one Todo API with agent mode in an IDE. Compare Ask and Agent mode on the same feature, then redirect a multi-file change. At each checkpoint, decide whether to accept the work, revise it, or stop.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Explain the difference between assistant and agent workflows
  • Use agent mode in VS Code for multi-step, multi-file tasks
  • Use the agent loop: plan, act, observe, review, and revise
  • Know when to use agent mode, Chat, or inline suggestions
  • Use TODO code actions to bridge IDE and cloud agent workflows
  • Review plans, diffs, commands, and test output at each checkpoint

docs.title: Session materials
docs.text: Resource Location Lab exercises lab/ Lab starter files lab/starter/ Lab solution files lab/solution/

docs.title: Key topics
docs.text:
• From autocomplete to assistant to agent
  • The agent loop: plan, act, observe, review, revise
  • Tool use: terminal commands, file operations, web search
  • Multi-file changes in agent mode
  • Trust boundaries and when to intervene
  • TODO code actions for cloud agent delegation
  • Chat vs. Agent mode decision framework

docs.title: Access and cost preflight
docs.text:
Follow the course safety baseline.

  1. Check the current GitHub docs and your organization's rules.
  2. Check the repository, data, and tools.
  3. Use a small task with tests.
  4. Set a usage limit for metered work.

docs.title: The agent loop
docs.text:
Plan → Act → Observe → Review → Revise or stop

Use the loop to review the work. Check current controls and behavior before a live demonstration.

docs.title: A safe task contract
docs.text:
## Goal
Add one small, testable behavior.

## Constraints
- Approved files and data only
- Required tests
- No unapproved dependencies

## Completion
- Tests and review evidence are available
- A human approves the change

docs.title: Review checkpoints
docs.text:
• Inspect the proposed file changes.
  • Review every command before it is run.
  • Check test results and unexpected side effects.
  • Stop when scope, data, policy, or the agreed stop rule is unclear.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Check that Agent mode works before the lab starts. If it does not, stop the lab. Manual editing does not demonstrate tool approval, steering, or agent review.

docs.title: Agenda and time plan
docs.text:
Time Topic Trainer move 0:00 Assistant-to-agent shift Contrast task shapes 0:08 Agent loop and tools Trace one iteration 0:18 Task contracts and trust Define boundaries 0:28 Multi-file live demo Pause at checkpoints 0:43 Chat vs. agent mode Apply decision framework 0:50 Intervention and TODO delegation Show safe handoff 0:57 Lab handoff and Q&A Check stop rules

Transition: "Autocomplete predicts text; an agent pursues a goal through tools."

docs.title: From autocomplete to agent
docs.text:
Mode Developer supplies Surface returns Inline Local code context A continuation Chat A question and references Guidance or a proposed edit Agent Goal, constraints, and repository A multi-step change with a diff and check results

More autonomy needs clear file limits, progress checks, and review.

docs.title: What agent mode can do
docs.text:
Subject to current product support and policy, agent mode may:

  • inspect repository files and conventions;
  • plan a sequence of changes;
  • edit multiple related files;
  • run approved terminal commands and tests;
  • observe failures and revise;
  • use approved tools, including configured MCP tools.

Product capability does not grant approval. Check what policy allows.

docs.title: One loop, many checkpoints
docs.text:
Goal and constraints
        ↓
Plan ──→ Act ──→ Observe
 ↑                   │
 └──── revise ───────┘
        ↓
Human review or stop

Trainer cue: Pause after each arrow and ask which plan, diff, or test result learners should see.

docs.title: Tool use and trust boundaries
docs.text:
Tool action Review question Read a file Is this path and data approved? Edit a file Is it required by the task? Run a command Is it understood, reversible, and scoped? Add a dependency Is it necessary, approved, and reviewed? Search the web May repository context leave the environment? Call an MCP tool Are server identity and permissions approved?

Stop rather than infer authorization.

docs.title: Multi-file work is a graph
docs.text:
route.ts ──calls──→ service.ts
   │                    │
   └──verified by──→ route.test.ts
                        │
                  documents behavior
                        ↓
                     README.md

Name the behavior you want to change. Review every changed file and check that its callers and tests still fit.

docs.title: Demo brief: one feature, three files
docs.text:
Add `completed` filtering to the task list endpoint.

Acceptance criteria:
- `GET /tasks?completed=true` returns completed tasks only.
- Invalid values return HTTP 400.
- Existing behavior without the parameter is unchanged.
- Focused tests cover true, false, and invalid values.

Constraints: no new dependencies; edit route, service, and tests only.

docs.title: Concrete demo code
docs.text:
const value = req.query.completed;
if (value !== undefined && value !== "true" && value !== "false") {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: "completed must be true or false" });
}

const completed = value === undefined ? undefined : value === "true";
return res.json(taskService.list({ completed }));

Ask the agent to implement and test the smallest valid change, then explain it.

docs.title: Narrate the demo
docs.text:
1. Show a clean working tree and the focused test command.
  2. Paste the task contract and request a plan before edits.
  3. Check that the plan names route, service, and tests.
  4. Approve only commands needed for the task.
  5. When a test fails, ask the agent to explain before revising.
  6. Inspect the final diff and run tests independently.

Transition: "A passing test checks one behavior. Review the rest of the diff too."

docs.title: Intervene, redirect, stop
docs.text:
Use a correction that preserves the original contract:

Stop. Do not change the response schema or add dependencies.
Keep the existing service API and add only the optional filter.
Show the revised plan before editing.

Stop for unexpected file scope, destructive commands, restricted data, unapproved network access, or repeated changes without new test results or an explained diagnosis.

docs.title: Same task: Chat or agent mode?
docs.text:
Use Chat when… Use agent mode when… You need explanation or options The outcome spans related files You want one surgical edit Tests can drive iteration Requirements are still forming Requirements and constraints are clear You need to retain manual control Tool output helps you check the work

Implement manually when policy, risk, or ambiguity makes an agent unsuitable.

docs.title: TODO code actions
docs.text:
A TODO can define a short task to delegate:

// TODO: reject duplicate task titles within the same project.

Before delegating:

  • convert the comment into acceptance criteria;
  • check the target repository and branch;
  • remove sensitive context;
  • define tests and reviewer ownership;
  • check current support and policy for the selected handoff.

docs.title: Demo debrief
docs.text:
Ask learners:

  • Which plan step gave the earliest useful signal?
  • Which command required the most scrutiny?
  • Did the agent touch exactly the expected files?
  • Which acceptance criterion was easiest to miss?
  • Would Chat have been safer or faster for this task?

Use the answers to discuss task selection.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
You will scaffold, implement, test, and refactor features with clear limits while:

  1. observing tool calls and multi-file edits;
  2. redirecting the agent after an intentional scope change;
  3. comparing manual and agent-mode implementations;
  4. trying a TODO delegation only when access is approved;
  5. recording the checks used to accept or reject output.

Continuing story: Build one Todo API, add ownership and due dates, then redirect its repository refactor.

Final deliverable: The tested API plus a traceable plan, comparison, course correction, and human decision.

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
1. Agent mode fits clearly defined, testable, multi-step work.
  2. Write the task limits before the agent starts.
  3. Tool approval and file scope are trust decisions.
  4. Redirect or stop the agent when needed.
  5. Human review closes the loop.

docs.title: Questions and lab readiness
docs.text:
Where should a reviewer intervene in your team's workflow?

  • What is your stop condition?
  • Which test will you run independently?
  • Is the starter repository and access ready?

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m2-02 lab: Agent mode in the IDE
docs.text: Duration: 2 hours Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 completed Deliverable: A tested Todo API built and extended with human review at each stage

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will build one Todo API and keep it for the full lab. Scaffold the project from a brief, then compare Ask and Agent mode on the same feature. Redirect the agent when the requirement changes. Finish with an accept, revise, or stop decision.

Stage Work Time 1 Prepare and scaffold the Todo API 30 min 2 Compare Ask and Agent mode on one feature 35 min 3 Redirect a multi-file change 35 min 4 Review the diff and test results, then finish the handoff 20 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Use a disposable workspace and synthetic data.

You need:

  • GitHub Copilot access in VS Code with Agent mode enabled;
  • Node.js and npm;
  • permission to let the agent read and edit the lab workspace;
  • permission to run the project test command;
  • lab/starter/project-brief.md, feature-spec.md, and course-correction.md.

If Copilot Agent mode is unavailable, stop the lab. Manual editing does not replace planning, tool approval, steering, and review in Agent mode.

Create a workspace outside the curriculum folder:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02
cp sessions/session-m2-02-agent-mode-ide/lab/starter/project-brief.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02/
cp sessions/session-m2-02-agent-mode-ide/lab/starter/feature-spec.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02/
cp sessions/session-m2-02-agent-mode-ide/lab/starter/course-correction.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-02

Create lab-notes.md with these headings:

# Session m2-02 Lab Notes

## Task contract
## Agent plan
## Tool and file review
## Ask versus Agent comparison
## Course correction
## Final decision

docs.title: Stage 1: Prepare and scaffold the Todo API (30 minutes)
Write the task contract
docs.text:
Read project-brief.md. Add a short contract to lab-notes.md:

Goal: Build the Todo API described in project-brief.md.
Allowed scope: The session-m2-02 workspace only.
Commands: npm install, npm test, and npm start.
Non-goals: No database, front end, deployment, or extra dependencies.
Completion: Required routes exist and the test suite passes.
Stop: Pause on network access beyond npm, destructive commands, or work outside scope.

docs.title: Ask Agent mode to plan first
docs.text:
Open the workspace in VS Code and select Agent mode. Use this prompt:

Read project-brief.md. Before editing, return a plan with the files you expect to
create, the commands you need, the tests that prove completion, and any decision
that is missing. Do not edit files yet.

Review the plan. Reject extra features and unexplained dependencies.

docs.title: Scaffold the project
docs.text:
After accepting the plan, continue:

Create the Todo API in a todo-api directory. Stay within the approved plan. Pause
before installing packages. After approval, implement the project and run its tests.

At each pause:

  1. Check the command and working directory.
  2. Check that the action supports the brief.
  3. Review changed files before the next command.
  4. Record any revision in lab-notes.md.

Run the checks yourself:

cd todo-api
npm test

If the generated project has no working test script, require the agent to add one that covers create, list, validation, update, and not-found behavior.

Compare the shape of your project with lab/solution/todo-api/. The reference is an example, not a file-for-file requirement.

docs.title: Checkpoint 1: baseline project works
docs.text:
• The project lives in todo-api/.
  • The routes in project-brief.md exist.
  • The agent stayed inside the workspace.
  • You reviewed package changes before installation.
  • npm test passes.
  • lab-notes.md contains the accepted plan and any corrections.

docs.title: Stage 2: Compare Ask and Agent mode on one feature (35 minutes)
docs.text: feature-spec.md adds ownership and due-date behavior to the same Todo API.

docs.title: Capture a clean baseline
docs.text:
Save the passing baseline:

cp -R todo-api todo-api-ask

docs.title: Attempt the feature in Ask mode
docs.text:
Open todo-api-ask/, switch to Ask mode, and ask:

Read feature-spec.md and explain the exact code and tests needed to add this feature
to todo-api. Give changes file by file. Do not assume files that are not present.

Apply enough of the suggested changes to test the workflow. Track:

  • messages sent;
  • manual file edits;
  • copy and paste operations;
  • commands you ran;
  • missing context or incorrect assumptions.

Stop after 12 minutes. Save the result or diff. Keep the original todo-api/ as the clean baseline for the Agent mode attempt.

docs.title: Implement the same feature in Agent mode
docs.text:
Switch to Agent mode:

Read feature-spec.md and inspect todo-api. Propose the smallest multi-file plan that
implements the feature without changing existing behavior. Include focused tests.
Wait for approval before editing.

Review the plan, approve only the work it describes, and watch each file and command. Then run:

cd todo-api
npm test

Add the comparison to lab-notes.md:

What you observed Ask mode Agent mode Prompts or messages Manual edits Files changed Commands run Corrections needed Final test result

docs.title: Checkpoint 2: feature and comparison are observable
docs.text:
• Existing tests still pass.
  • New tests cover owner and due-date behavior.
  • The implementation follows the existing project structure.
  • The Ask-versus-Agent table uses observed counts or examples.
  • You can explain why Agent mode did or did not help.

docs.title: Stage 3: Redirect a multi-file change (35 minutes)
docs.text: Open course-correction.md. Do not give it to the agent yet.

docs.title: Start the original task
docs.text:
Ask Agent mode:

Refactor todo-api so route handlers delegate storage operations to a small repository
module. Keep the HTTP contract unchanged. Add or update tests, and stop after the
repository module and first route integration are complete.

Inspect the first stage:

  • Did the agent preserve current behavior?
  • Did it choose a clear module boundary?
  • Did it avoid unrelated formatting or dependency changes?
  • Do focused tests pass?

docs.title: Apply the course correction
docs.text:
Now read course-correction.md and redirect the active task:

Pause. Apply the new constraints in course-correction.md. Revise the plan before
editing. Keep completed work only when it still fits the new requirement.

Reject any plan that needlessly rewrites the project. Check that the agent adjusts the repository boundary, validation, and tests while preserving the API.

Run the full suite:

cd todo-api
npm test

If the agent requests an unexpected dependency, network access, or broader file scope, choose stop. Record the unresolved work and complete the smallest safe change manually.

docs.title: Checkpoint 3: redirect or stop decision is recorded
docs.text:
• course-correction.md changed the plan before more edits.
  • The final diff stays inside todo-api/.
  • The API contract remains compatible.
  • Tests prove the changed behavior.
  • lab-notes.md records whether you accepted, revised, or stopped the run and why.

docs.title: Stage 4: Review evidence and finish the handoff (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Review the final project as if another engineer submitted it.

  1. Inspect git diff --stat and git diff, or use the editor's change view.
  2. Check that each changed file traces to the brief, feature spec, or course correction.
  3. Run npm test again.
  4. Start the service and make one create request and one filtered list request.
  5. Write the final decision: accept, revise, or stop.

Use lab/solution/final-review.md as the trainer reference. Review behavior, tests, and the diff rather than requiring an exact file layout.

Example requests:

curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/todos \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Review agent work","owner":"learner","dueDate":"2026-10-15"}'

curl "http://localhost:3000/api/todos?owner=learner"

Do not approve the work only because the agent reports success. Use the diff, tests, and API behavior.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4: another reviewer can reproduce the result
docs.text:
• The final diff matches the accepted scope.
  • Package changes are explained.
  • Test output is saved in lab-notes.md.
  • The manual API check matches the feature spec.
  • The final decision names remaining risk.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit the session-m2-02 workspace with:

  1. The completed todo-api/ project.
  2. Passing test output and two manual API checks.
  3. lab-notes.md with the task contract, plan, tool and file review, comparison, course correction, and final decision.
  4. A clear record of any stopped or rejected action.

Done: A reviewer can trace the final code to the approved plan, see where you redirected the agent, and reproduce the checks.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m2-02: IDE agent workflows
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery baseline
docs.text: Read the course safety baseline. Before the demo, check the current GitHub docs and your organization's rules. Editor modes, permissions, and model choices can change.

docs.title: Access and cost preflight
docs.text:
1. Choose the training repository and synthetic data.
  2. Check which tools and commands learners may use.
  3. Choose a small task with clear acceptance criteria.
  4. Set a usage limit if the work is metered.
  5. Check Agent mode access before the lab.

docs.title: Access failure
docs.text: Stop the learner lab and fix access. A prepared recording may preserve the trainer demonstration, but it does not count as learner completion.

docs.title: Session objective
docs.text:
Show learners how to review work at each step of the agent loop.

Plan → Act → Observe → Review → Revise or stop

Have learners define the task and approve actions. The assistant proposes work within those boundaries.

docs.title: Suggested agenda
docs.text: Segment Activity Preflight Check scope, data, tools, usage limits, and access. Plan Write the goal, constraints, and acceptance criteria. Act Inspect proposed changes and commands before approval. Observe Read test output, diffs, and unexpected effects. Review Check correctness, safety, scope, and maintainability. Access gate Stop when required Agent mode access is missing.

docs.title: Trainer talking points
docs.text:
"The agent loop does not delegate judgment. Plan before the change, inspect each action, check the result, and stop when the task leaves its stated scope."

"Use only the tools allowed for the training repository."

"For metered work, set a usage limit and name who can approve more."

docs.title: Task template
docs.text:
## Goal
Describe one user-visible, testable change.

## Constraints
- Named repository paths and synthetic data only
- Required checks and repository conventions
- No new dependencies or external access

## Completion
- Acceptance criteria are satisfied
- Test output is recorded
- A human reviewer approves the result

docs.title: Review rubric
docs.text:
• Is the plan small enough to check?
  • Does each proposed change stay within the planned files?
  • Are commands, dependencies, and data access understood before approval?
  • Do relevant checks pass?
  • Does a reviewer accept the outcome?
  • Did the work stay within the usage limit?

docs.title: Close
docs.text: Ask learners to identify one point in their workflow where a plan or review check would reduce risk.

docs.title: Minute-mapped delivery plan (60 minutes)
docs.text: Time Segment Result 0:00 to 0:08 Assistant-to-agent shift Learners distinguish a continuation, answer, and goal-driven task. 0:08 to 0:18 Agent loop and tools The group identifies what to check at every loop stage. 0:18 to 0:28 Task contracts and trust The contract and stop rules are visible. 0:28 to 0:43 Scripted multi-file demo The group reviews the plan, tool decisions, diff, and test output. 0:43 to 0:50 Chat, agent, or manual decision Learners select a workflow from task characteristics. 0:50 to 0:57 Intervention exercise Learners redirect or stop without expanding scope. 0:57 to 1:00 Close and lab handoff Required access is checked.

docs.title: Time-pressure cutpoints
docs.text:
• At 0:08, shorten the mode comparison to one example per mode.
  • At 0:18, keep read, edit, and command trust questions; omit optional tool categories.
  • At 0:28, use the prepared plan rather than waiting for a generated plan.
  • At 0:38, stop after route and test review; describe the service edit.
  • At 0:43, skip the mode table and state the decision rule.
  • At 0:50, run one redirect rather than two.
  • Never cut preflight, independent checks, or stop rules.

docs.title: Segment 1: From assistant to agent (0:00 to 0:08)
Trainer talking points
docs.text:
1. Inline assistance proposes a local continuation.
  2. Chat commonly answers or proposes a small edit.
  3. An agent can pursue a defined goal through multiple actions.
  4. More actions need more review; they do not reduce accountability.
  5. A tool's capabilities do not grant permission to use it. Check current documentation and organizational policy.
  6. Check current product modes, controls, models, and availability before delivery.

docs.title: Trainer interaction
docs.text:
Present three fictional tasks:

  • explain one regular expression;
  • change one error message;
  • add an optional filter across route, service, and tests.

Ask learners to choose Chat, a manual edit, or an agent workflow. Have them explain how much review their choice needs.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "At each step, you need output you can check before the agent continues."

docs.title: Segment 2: Plan, act, observe, review (0:08 to 0:18)
Detailed talking points
docs.text:
• Plan: map acceptance criteria to files, commands, and risks.
  • Act: approve only the required read, edit, or command.
  • Observe: inspect command output and changed files.
  • Review: compare behavior and scope with the task contract.
  • Revise: change one assumption at a time and check the new result.
  • Stop: end the task when scope, data, permissions, or repeated failures cross a boundary.

docs.title: Review prompts
docs.text:
After Plan, ask: "Does every step support an acceptance criterion?"

After Act, ask: "Was this file or command necessary?"

After Observe, ask: "What changed, and what does the output actually prove?"

After Review, ask: "Would the reviewer accept this result?"

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "The contract gives the agent and reviewer the same boundary."

docs.title: Segment 3: Task contract and trust preflight (0:18 to 0:28)
Exact trainer actions
docs.text:
1. Re-display the Delivery baseline and Access and cost preflight.
  2. Check that the repository contains only synthetic data.
  3. Check the current GitHub docs for Agent mode.
  4. Check the rules for file access, commands, network use, and tools.
  5. Identify the human reviewer.
  6. Set a usage limit and name who can approve more.
  7. Open the starter task before the first request.
  8. Write this contract:
Goal: add optional completed filtering to a fictional task list.

Acceptance criteria:
- completed=true returns only completed tasks.
- completed=false returns only incomplete tasks.
- another value produces the existing HTTP 400 error shape.
- omitting completed preserves current behavior.

Constraints:
- route, service, and focused tests only.
- no dependency, network access, or response-schema change.
- show a plan before editing.

Done:
- focused tests pass independently.
- final diff stays in scope.
- a human reviewer accepts the result.

docs.title: Trust-boundary questions
docs.text: Proposed action Question before approval Read a file Is its path and data approved? Edit a file Which criterion requires the edit? Run a test Is the command understood and scoped? Add a package Is it necessary and approved by a reviewer? Use a network or external tool Is that destination and permission approved?

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "We will direct one feature and pause at each checkpoint."

docs.title: Scripted demo: Optional task filter (0:28 to 0:43)
Setup
docs.text:
Use a disposable fictional TypeScript project or prepared excerpts.

The working tree must be clean.

Display this relationship:

route.ts → task-service.ts
    └────→ route.test.ts

Show the focused test command without running it yet.

Do not install packages or connect to external systems.

docs.title: Exact opening prompt
docs.text:
Implement the attached completed-filter task contract.
First inspect only the route, service, and focused test.
Return a three-step plan before editing.
Do not add dependencies, use the network, or change the response schema.
Stop if existing behavior is ambiguous.

docs.title: Expected plan
docs.text:
The wording may vary, but it should:

  1. inspect query parsing and existing error shape;
  2. pass an optional boolean to the service and filter without changing the unfiltered path;
  3. add true, false, invalid, and omitted-parameter tests.

docs.title: Exact trainer actions
docs.text:
1. Compare the plan with the contract.
  2. Reject any step involving unrelated files or dependencies.
  3. Approve only reads in the named scope.
  4. Ask the agent to show the proposed diff before broad commands when the current surface supports that review flow.
  5. Inspect parsing for exact "true" and "false" values.
  6. Inspect the service so undefined preserves existing behavior.
  7. Inspect tests for all four criteria.
  8. Run the focused test command independently.
  9. Inspect git diff --stat and the full diff.
  10. Search for unintended response-schema or dependency changes.
  11. Make the human accept, revise, or stop decision.

docs.title: Expected code shape
docs.text:
const value = req.query.completed;
if (value !== undefined && value !== "true" && value !== "false") {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: "completed must be true or false" });
}
const completed = value === undefined ? undefined : value === "true";
return res.json(taskService.list({ completed }));

This is an example, not a required framework pattern.

docs.title: Expected outcome
docs.text:
• Four focused cases are present.
  • Valid values filter correctly.
  • Invalid values preserve the stated error contract.
  • No parameter preserves the baseline list.
  • Only route, service, and focused tests changed.
  • No package or external access was introduced.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Ask learners:

  • Which test proves omitted behavior?
  • Could a truthiness conversion incorrectly accept "yes"?
  • Did the service mutate stored tasks?
  • Does the diff match the file relationships in the accepted plan?
  • Which result was independently reproduced?

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
Distribute the prepared contract and code shape.

Pairs write:

  1. a three-step plan;
  2. a query-parsing truth table;
  3. four test names and expected outcomes;
  4. a three-file change list;
  5. an approve, revise, or stop decision.

Reveal the illustrative code only after plans are complete.

Use this only to recover the trainer demonstration. Learners still need Agent mode for the lab.

docs.title: Demo recovery
docs.text:
• If Agent mode is unavailable during the demonstration, use the prepared example and fix access before the lab.
  • If the plan is too broad, say: "Stop. Use only the three named files and show a revised plan."
  • If a dependency is proposed, reject it and restate the no-dependency constraint.
  • If tests fail, ask for an explanation tied to one failing assertion before allowing revision.
  • If repeated revisions add no useful result, stop the run and explain the smallest acceptable correction.
  • If the run reaches its usage limit, stop and record progress.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "Agent mode fit this task because the change crossed related files and tests could guide each step. Other tasks may need a different workflow."

docs.title: Segment 5: Choose Chat, agent, or manual work (0:43 to 0:50)
Decision framework
docs.text:
Use Chat to explain a problem, suggest options, or propose one small edit.

Use an agent workflow for clear multi-file outcomes with named tools and tests.

Work manually when the change is tiny, requirements remain unclear, or autonomy adds review work.

Pause when permissions, data handling, policy, or a destructive action is unresolved.

docs.title: Quick classification exercise
docs.text: Task Preferred starting point Reason Explain a failing assertion Chat or human inspection No multi-file action is required. Rename a local variable Manual or inline The edit is small and directly observable. Add a route plus service tests Agent The files and tests are closely related. Decide an authorization policy Human owners This is an accountable policy decision.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "You can redirect the agent or stop it. You do not have to follow its first plan."

docs.title: Scripted exercise: Redirect and stop (0:50 to 0:57)
Setup
docs.text: Tell learners that a proposal has started changing the response schema and package.json.

docs.title: Exact redirect
docs.text:
Stop. Do not change package.json or the response schema.
Revert those proposed changes.
Keep the existing service API and add only the optional filter.
Show the revised plan before editing.

docs.title: Expected outcome
docs.text:
The revised plan returns to route, service, and tests.

The dependency and schema changes disappear from the proposed diff.

docs.title: Stop scenario
docs.text:
Then say an unexpected command requests network access.

Learners must choose stop and record the unresolved permission. Do not continue until the permission is resolved.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• The revised file list matches the contract.
  • No unrelated action remains queued.
  • The reason for stopping names the boundary crossed.
  • The reason for stopping is clear.

docs.title: "Should I approve every tool call so the agent can finish?"
docs.text: No. Check why the action is needed, what it affects, whether you can undo it, and whether you may use the data and tools. Reject or stop when the contract does not require the action.

docs.title: "Is agent mode always better for multi-file work?"
docs.text: No. Requirements, tests, risk, repository size, and review cost matter. Manual work or Chat may be more controlled.

docs.title: "Can an agent add a dependency?"
docs.text: Only through the organization's normal dependency approval and review process. This session's demo forbids it.

docs.title: "What if it keeps fixing its own failures?"
docs.text: Iteration helps only when each cycle improves the result. Stop repeated, broad, or unexplained changes and inspect the problem.

docs.title: "Can I let it run without watching?"
docs.text: Use only the modes and controls allowed for the repository. Review the actions, diff, and test output.

docs.title: "How do we know which files it read?"
docs.text: Use the product's file list and repository tools; do not guess. Keep the file list small and stop if you cannot tell what the agent read.

docs.title: "What about MCP or external tools?"
docs.text: Check the current product docs, server identity, permissions, and data path. The base demo does not need external tools.

docs.title: "How much will a run cost?"
docs.text: Do not quote static figures. Check the current terms, set a usage limit, and name who can approve more.

docs.title: Pitfalls, anti-patterns, and recoveries
docs.text: Anti-pattern Recovery "Fix the project" with no criteria Write one user-visible goal, non-goals, files, and tests. Approving commands by habit Pause and connect each command to a criterion. Counting changed files as progress Check behavior and test output instead. Allowing a surprise dependency Reject, restore the manifest, and use existing APIs. Trusting the agent's test summary Run the focused check independently. Reviewing only the final message Inspect complete diff and command output. Endless self-correction Stop after repeated cycles without a better result. Treating intervention as failure Normalize redirect, rollback, and stopping. Using sensitive examples Replace with synthetic fictional tasks. Teaching fixed UI or entitlement Check current docs before delivery.

docs.title: Closing script
docs.text: "Define the task before the agent starts. Use tests to check the result, then decide whether to accept it."

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Open lab/README.md.

Explain the four lab stages. Learners scaffold one Todo API, compare Ask and Agent mode on a feature, then redirect a repository refactor. They finish by deciding whether to accept the work.

Use only synthetic credentials and data. Stop the lab if Agent mode or the required repository permissions are unavailable.

docs.title: Lab readiness checklist
docs.text:
• Required Agent mode access is checked.
  • Repository copy contains no sensitive data.
  • Goal, constraints, tests, and stop rules are written.
  • Human reviewer is named.
  • A usage limit is recorded when it applies.
  • Learners know how to cancel and stop the lab.

docs.title: Session m2-03: Copilot Spaces & context management
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Copilot in Practice Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 Duration: 3 hours (1 hr trainer content + 2 hr lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Give Copilot the context a task needs. Use one Storefront API to select Space sources, add repository instructions, compare context levels, and store reusable prompts. Before implementation, inspect CLI /env and /instructions to find and correct a stale module-style instruction.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Create Copilot Spaces for team workflows
  • Write project-level and user-level custom instructions
  • Create reusable prompt files for team standards
  • Explain how instructions, Spaces, and Memory work together
  • Review and update context as a project changes
  • Distinguish instruction discovery, file scope, and observed model behavior
  • Choose the smallest source set that supports a task and check claims against it

docs.title: Session materials
docs.text: Resource Location Lab exercises lab/ Lab starter files lab/starter/ Lab solution files lab/solution/

docs.title: Key topics
docs.text:
• Copilot Spaces: selected context sources
  • .github/copilot-instructions.md: project-level instructions
  • .github/prompts/*.md: reusable prompt files
  • VS Code instruction settings
  • Context selection as a policy-approved workflow
  • Before/after context comparison
  • Runtime instruction inspection in the standalone CLI; stop if it is unavailable

docs.title: Give each task the source files it needs
Access and cost preflight
docs.text:
Follow the course safety baseline.

  1. Check the current GitHub docs and your organization's rules.
  2. Check the repository and data sources.
  3. Use a small question and synthetic data.
  4. Set a usage limit for metered work.

docs.title: Context selection
docs.text:
Choose sources a reviewer can explain:

  • repository instructions;
  • relevant source files and tests;
  • architecture or API documents;
  • approved task notes.

Do not include unapproved data merely to make a prompt more complete.

docs.title: Context packet exercise
docs.text:
Task: add validation to an API endpoint

Packet:
- route file
- corresponding tests
- API contract
- repository conventions

Ask learners to explain why each source is needed and what is excluded.

docs.title: Evaluate the result
docs.text:
• Does it cite or follow the selected repository files?
  • Is the scope limited to the task?
  • Are assumptions listed for human review?
  • Do relevant tests pass?

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Check Spaces and GitHub Copilot access before the lab. If either is unavailable, stop the lab. A manually assembled packet does not demonstrate Space creation, reuse, or behavior.

docs.title: Agenda and time plan
docs.text:
Time Topic Trainer move 0:00 Why context fails Diagnose a vague response 0:08 Context layers Build a source hierarchy 0:18 Spaces Select and share sources 0:30 Instructions and prompt files Show repository artifacts 0:42 Memory and maintenance Separate preview from policy 0:50 Before/after demo Compare with a rubric 0:58 Lab handoff Assign context packet

Transition: "Choose sources that answer the task before adding more prompt text."

docs.title: The context problem
docs.text:
Copilot cannot reliably apply information it cannot see. Extra context can create noise or expose data unnecessarily.

Common failure modes:

  • the relevant contract is absent;
  • stale documentation conflicts with source code;
  • broad context hides the key constraint;
  • local preferences are mistaken for team standards;
  • restricted data is included without approval.

Check both relevance and permission when selecting context. Keep the packet focused.

docs.title: A practical context hierarchy
docs.text:
Task intent and acceptance criteria
               ↓
Repository instructions and prompt workflow
               ↓
Curated Space: code, docs, issues, specifications
               ↓
Current file and explicit references
               ↓
Validated memory, when supported and approved

Specific task constraints override generic guidance. Clarify conflicts.

docs.title: Copilot Spaces
docs.text:
A Space is a selected set of sources for a recurring topic or workflow.

Good candidates include:

  • source repositories and key paths;
  • architecture and API documentation;
  • approved issues and specifications;
  • team guidance for a domain;
  • links whose ownership and freshness are known.

Do not use a Space to collect restricted information without approval.

docs.title: Curate for a purpose
docs.text:
Space: Storefront API
├── API specification
├── product route and model
├── architecture note
├── error-handling conventions
└── repository instructions

Exclude unrelated services, production data, secrets, abandoned proposals, and documents with no accountable owner.

Trainer cue: Ask learners what they would remove first if the answer became noisy.

docs.title: Sharing Spaces safely
docs.text:
Before sharing:

  1. Name the intended audience and task.
  2. Check that every source is approved for that audience.
  3. Add purpose-specific instructions.
  4. Assign an owner and review date.
  5. Test with a known question and compare against the source files.
  6. Remove or replace stale sources.

Check current access controls and sharing behavior before the demo.

docs.title: Repository-level instructions
docs.text:
Create .github/copilot-instructions.md for project-wide guidance:

# Repository guidance

- Use TypeScript strict mode.
- Validate request input at the route boundary.
- Keep business logic in `src/services/`.
- Run `npm test` before proposing completion.
- Do not add dependencies without reviewer approval.

Write rules a reviewer can check. Avoid vague goals such as "produce high-quality code."

docs.title: Reusable prompt files
docs.text:
Place team-reviewed workflows under .github/prompts/:

---
description: Review an API change against its contract
---

Read the selected route, service, tests, and API contract.
List mismatches before suggesting changes.
Do not edit files outside the selected feature.
End with the focused validation command.

Check the current supported filename and frontmatter behavior before delivery.

docs.title: Inspect what the CLI loaded
docs.text:
/env
/instructions

Find the copied stale CommonJS note and its route-file scope. Compare it with package.json and the current ES-module route.

Correct only that training note, restart, and inspect again. Do not toggle personal, managed, or security instructions.

Discovery is not proof of application. Check the proposed code too. The lab includes this work in its 30-minute instruction block.

docs.title: VS Code instruction settings
docs.text:
The curriculum references:

{
  "github.copilot.chat.codeGeneration.useInstructionFiles": true
}

Treat settings as version-sensitive:

  • check current documentation and the learner's IDE version;
  • show where workspace settings are reviewed;
  • do not claim an instruction loaded without observing the result;
  • retain the instructions as a useful manual checklist.

docs.title: Copilot Memory
docs.text:
Memory may let an agent retain and validate useful knowledge, depending on support and approval.

Use three questions:

  1. Source: Where did this fact come from?
  2. Scope: Does it apply to this user, repository, or task?
  3. Freshness: How will it be corrected when the code changes?

Never store secrets, restricted data, or guesses. Check current availability and controls.

docs.title: Demo: without grounded context
docs.text:
Prompt:

Add a low-stock report endpoint.

Expected discussion:

  • Which endpoint?
  • Which inputs and error schema?
  • Where is validation normally performed?
  • Which tests prove the behavior?
  • Which data is safe to include?

Do not score the response by confidence or length.

docs.title: Demo: with a context packet
docs.text:
Using the Storefront API specification, product route, product model, architecture
note, and repository instructions, propose the smallest low-stock endpoint change.

First list acceptance criteria and assumptions. Do not add dependencies.
End with two verification requests and cite the evidence used.

Check correctness and scope. Compare assumptions, source references, and the checks each response proposes.

docs.title: Concrete code target
docs.text:
function parseThreshold(value) {
  if (value === undefined) return 10;
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(value)) {
    throw new Error("threshold must be a non-negative integer");
  }
  return Number(value);
}

Ask where the static report route must appear relative to /:id. The correct next action may be clarification rather than code generation.

docs.title: Maintenance is part of context
docs.text:
Trigger Maintenance action API contract changes Update Space sources and prompts Repository convention changes Review instruction files Ownership changes Assign a new maintainer Output contradicts source Remove stale sources and retest Feature behavior changes Recheck official documentation

Schedule reviews; do not wait for failures.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
You will:

  1. keep one Storefront API for the full lab;
  2. select the smallest approved source set;
  3. add repository instructions and a low-stock endpoint;
  4. compare one logging task across context levels;
  5. store and test three reusable prompt files.

Final deliverable: A Storefront API context package with comparison results and the checks you ran.

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
1. Relevant context matters more than a large context packet.
  2. Select Space sources for a named purpose and audience.
  3. Instructions state project-wide rules; prompt files define reusable tasks.
  4. Memory requires source, scope, freshness, and current policy checks.
  5. Every context source needs an owner and maintenance path.

docs.title: Questions and lab readiness
docs.text:
Which source would you remove from a context packet, and why?

  • Which source is authoritative?
  • What must stay out of the Space?
  • Who will maintain the resulting artifacts?

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m2-03 lab: Spaces and context management
docs.text: Duration: 2 hours Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 completed Deliverable: A context package for one Storefront API, with recorded comparison results

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will use one Storefront API for the full lab. First select the sources for a Copilot Space. Then add repository instructions and compare the same task across context levels. Store reusable prompt files beside the project.

Stage Work Time 1 Prepare the project and select Space sources 30 min 2 Add instructions and inspect what the CLI loaded 30 min 3 Compare one task across context levels 30 min 4 Build and test a prompt library 30 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Use only the synthetic Storefront API files supplied with this lab.

You need:

  • required GitHub Copilot access in the editor;
  • Copilot Spaces access if you will use a live Space;
  • a repository or sandbox you may use for the Storefront API;
  • Node.js and npm;
  • permission to add repository instructions and prompt files;
  • standalone Copilot CLI access with /env and /instructions.

If Copilot Spaces, GitHub Copilot, or a required CLI command is unavailable, stop the lab. A local context packet does not replace creating a Space or inspecting the loaded instructions.

Create a writable copy:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-03
cp -R sessions/session-m2-03-spaces-and-context/lab/starter/ecommerce-project \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-03/storefront-api
cp sessions/session-m2-03-spaces-and-context/lab/starter/context-comparison.md \
  sessions/session-m2-03-spaces-and-context/lab/starter/stale-storefront.instructions.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-03/storefront-api/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m2-03/storefront-api
npm install
npm start

Open http://localhost:3000/api/products. The response should contain the seeded products.

docs.title: Stage 1: Prepare the project and select Space sources (30 minutes)
Inspect the context before adding it
docs.text:
Read these files:

Source Decision it supports README.md Project purpose, setup, and endpoints docs/api-spec.md Required HTTP behavior docs/architecture.md Layers, response envelopes, and naming src/models/product.js Product fields and validation src/routes/products.js Current route patterns

Write context-notes.md:

# Storefront API Context Notes

## Task
Add a low-stock report endpoint.

## Required sources
## Excluded sources
## Conflicts or stale statements
## Acceptance criteria

For this task, keep the source set small. Do not add unrelated repositories, private discussions, or production data.

docs.title: Live Space path
docs.text:
Create a Space named Storefront API Lab. Add the five reviewed files and these instructions:

Answer from the selected Storefront API sources. Follow docs/api-spec.md and
docs/architecture.md. Use the Product validation and response patterns already in
the project. State when a requested behavior is not defined by the sources.

Ask:

What files and acceptance criteria should guide a low-stock report endpoint?
Do not write code yet.

Check every claim against the selected sources.

docs.title: Checkpoint 1: context scope is visible
docs.text:
• context-notes.md names the task and acceptance criteria.
  • Every selected source has a reason to be present.
  • Unrelated or restricted sources are excluded.
  • Claims in the first answer trace to a selected file.
  • The live Space or local context packet is ready for reuse.

docs.title: Stage 2: Add repository instructions (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Create .github/copilot-instructions.md in the Storefront API:

# Storefront API Instructions

- Use ES modules.
- Keep route handlers under `src/routes/`.
- Follow the `{ data: ... }` success envelope.
- Return errors as `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`.
- Use `Product.validate()` before product data changes.
- Add no dependency unless the task requires it and a reviewer approves it.
- Keep examples and tests on synthetic data.

docs.title: Inspect a stale instruction before implementation (10 minutes)
docs.text:
In this copied workspace only, create .github/instructions/ and copy stale-storefront.instructions.md into it as storefront-style.instructions.md. Read the file before starting the CLI. It deliberately conflicts with the current ES-module contract.

Start copilot from the Storefront project and run:

/env
/instructions

Inspect instruction source paths and any file-match scope shown by the client. Do not toggle or edit personal, organization, or security instructions. In context-comparison.md, name the project instruction and the stale route note, then compare both with package.json and an existing route.

Ask Copilot to identify the conflict without editing. Correct only the stale training note to require ES modules. Restart the CLI and inspect /env and /instructions again before continuing. A file appearing in a list proves discovery, not that every scoped instruction applies to every task or that the model followed it.

If another source conflicts, stop and ask the trainer who owns it. Do not claim that an instruction in the prompt overrides managed rules.

Ask Copilot to plan the low-stock endpoint:

Plan a GET /api/products/reports/low-stock endpoint for this project. It should
accept an optional non-negative integer threshold and default to 10. Return only
products whose stock is at or below the threshold. Follow repository instructions.
Do not edit files.

Review the plan against the API spec, architecture, and model. Check the route order too: a static route must not be hidden behind /:id.

Then ask for the smallest implementation and a check:

Implement the accepted low-stock endpoint plan. Keep the current API behavior.
Run the smallest useful check and show the result.

Check manually:

curl "http://localhost:3000/api/products/reports/low-stock?threshold=80"
curl "http://localhost:3000/api/products/reports/low-stock?threshold=-1"

Compare your instruction file with lab/solution/ecommerce-project/.github/copilot-instructions.md.

docs.title: Checkpoint 2: instructions changed observable behavior
docs.text:
• The plan uses ES modules and existing response envelopes.
  • The route is placed before /:id.
  • Invalid thresholds produce a structured 400 response.
  • Existing product routes still work.
  • context-notes.md records one instruction Copilot followed and one item you still had to review.
  • CLI inspection identified the stale training source and its corrected text.

docs.title: Stage 3: Compare one task across context levels (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Open context-comparison.md. Use the same task in every experiment:

Add request-logging middleware to the Storefront API. Record timestamp, method,
URL, response time, and status code. Use info for 2xx, warn for 4xx, and error for
5xx. Add no logging package.

Run four experiments without changing the task:

  1. No project context: Ask from an empty window.
  2. Repository context: Open the Storefront API with copilot-instructions.md.
  3. Space or context packet: Ask with the selected project sources.
  4. Prompt file: Use a structured repository prompt for the task.

Record:

  • import style;
  • file placement;
  • response and error conventions;
  • added assumptions;
  • number of corrections;
  • claims that cite or clearly follow a source.

Score the response against the project requirements rather than how well it reads. Keep extra context only when it removes wrong assumptions.

docs.title: Checkpoint 3: comparison uses evidence
docs.text:
• All four experiments use the same task text.
  • Each score cites a concrete output difference.
  • The comparison identifies one useful source and one source that added no value.
  • The final choice states the smallest context set that supports the task.

docs.title: Stage 4: Build and test a prompt library (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Create these files in storefront-api/.github/prompts/:

  1. investigate-bug.prompt.md
  2. generate-api-docs.prompt.md
  3. migration-checklist.prompt.md

Each prompt needs front matter with a short description. Name the inputs it accepts, the sections it should return, and a check to run.

docs.title: Test the prompts on the same project
docs.text:
• Run investigate-bug against an invalid minPrice query scenario.
  • Run generate-api-docs against the low-stock endpoint.
  • Run migration-checklist for a proposed Express major-version update. Do not install it.

Review each result:

  • Did it stay inside the selected Storefront API sources?
  • Did it separate known facts from assumptions?
  • Did it name a check another engineer can run?
  • Did it avoid changing code when the prompt only requested analysis?

Compare with lab/solution/ecommerce-project/.github/prompts/.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4: prompts define their inputs and checks
docs.text:
• All three prompt files appear in .github/prompts/.
  • Each prompt was tested on the Storefront API.
  • Each output includes a check to run.
  • The migration prompt stops before package changes.
  • Stale or duplicate instructions were removed.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit the storefront-api/ workspace with:

  1. context-notes.md and either the Space source list or context-packet.md.
  2. .github/copilot-instructions.md.
  3. The completed context-comparison.md.
  4. Three tested prompt files under .github/prompts/.
  5. Low-stock endpoint check results and the final context choice.

Done: Another engineer can see which sources were selected, how each context layer changed the result, and how to check the project-specific output.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text: Checked October 15, 2026: Copilot CLI environment and instruction commands.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m2-03: Context workflows
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery baseline
docs.text: Read the course safety baseline. Before the demo, check the current GitHub docs and your organization's rules. Product behavior and availability can change.

docs.title: Access and cost preflight
docs.text:
1. Choose the training repository and synthetic data.
  2. Check which sources learners may add or share.
  3. Choose a small question and the files needed to answer it.
  4. Set a usage limit if the work is metered.
  5. Check Spaces and GitHub Copilot access before the lab.
  6. Check standalone CLI /env and /instructions in the copied Storefront project.

docs.title: Access failure
docs.text: Stop the learner lab. A printed context packet may support the trainer demonstration, but it does not count as learner completion.

docs.title: Session objective
docs.text: Teach learners to select the few files needed for a task and check the answer against those files.

docs.title: Suggested agenda
docs.text: Segment Activity Preflight Check data, sources, usage limits, and access. Source selection Select only relevant repository instructions, code, tests, and docs. Context packet Explain why every included source is necessary. Small task Use the packet to plan a small change. Review Check the output against the source files and tests. Access gate Stop when required Spaces or Copilot access is missing.

docs.title: Context packet pattern
docs.text:
Task: make one API behavior change

Include:
- route or service file
- focused tests
- relevant API contract
- repository conventions

Exclude:
- unrelated repositories
- sensitive data
- broad documentation that does not affect the task

docs.title: Trainer talking points
docs.text:
"Select the fewest files needed to explain and check the result."

"If you are unsure whether you may use a source or how the product handles it, stop and resolve the access or policy question before the lab."

"For metered work, stop at the usage limit."

docs.title: Review rubric
docs.text:
• Does every source have a clear relationship to the task?
  • Is all included data allowed for the lab?
  • Does the result follow the source files and acceptance criteria?
  • Are assumptions identified for human review?
  • Can the task be completed manually from the packet?

docs.title: Close
docs.text: Ask learners to identify a task that would be easier to review with fewer files.

docs.title: Minute-mapped delivery plan (60 minutes)
docs.text: Time Segment Trainer outcome 0:00 to 0:08 Diagnose the context problem Learners distinguish missing information from excess noise. 0:08 to 0:18 Context hierarchy Learners rank task, instructions, curated sources, and local references. 0:18 to 0:30 Curated context workflows The group creates a purpose, audience, source list, and owner. 0:30 to 0:42 Instructions and reusable prompts Learners separate project-wide rules from repeatable tasks. 0:42 to 0:50 Source governance and maintenance Each source receives scope and freshness checks. 0:50 to 0:58 Scripted before/after demo The group compares two responses with the source files. 0:58 to 1:00 Close and lab handoff Learners begin with the context packet.

docs.title: Time-pressure cutpoints
docs.text:
• At 0:08, use one missing-context and one excess-context example.
  • At 0:18, keep the hierarchy diagram and omit secondary surface examples.
  • At 0:30, describe sharing rather than navigating a changing UI.
  • At 0:42, create one instruction excerpt and one prompt file, not a library.
  • At 0:50, mention memory only after noting that learners must check its availability.
  • At 0:55, compare plans rather than waiting for generated code.
  • Never cut source approval, maintenance ownership, access checks, or lab boundaries.

docs.title: Trainer talking points
docs.text:
• Context is an engineering input. It does not authorize collecting everything available.
  • Missing contracts cause invented assumptions.
  • Broad, stale, or conflicting sources can obscure the decisive rule.
  • Restricted data must not be added merely because it seems relevant.
  • A confident answer does not show that the right source was used.
  • Teach learners to select the fewest files needed for review.

docs.title: Opening exercise
docs.text:
Display this request:

Add validation to the checkout endpoint.

Ask learners what is missing.

Expected answers include endpoint location, input contract, error shape, repository conventions, focused tests, and allowed data.

Then ask what should not be added.

Expected answers include unrelated repositories, production records, secrets, and ownerless stale documents.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "We can organize those choices as a hierarchy, starting with the task itself."

docs.title: Detailed talking points
docs.text:
1. Task intent and acceptance criteria define the immediate outcome.
  2. Repository instructions provide reviewed project-wide conventions.
  3. Reusable prompt files encode repeatable workflows.
  4. Curated collections can bring code, docs, issues, and specifications together.
  5. Current files and named references supply local context.
  6. Retained memory needs a source, scope, and review date.
  7. Specific task requirements override generic guidance.
  8. Conflicts require clarification; they are not resolved by adding more context.

docs.title: Source-ranking exercise
docs.text:
For a fictional quantity-validation change, rank:

  • current API contract;
  • focused route tests;
  • owned architecture note;
  • unrelated product roadmap;
  • production request log.

Include the contract, tests, and the relevant owned note.

Exclude the unrelated roadmap and production log.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "Record why each source is included and who will maintain it."

docs.title: Access and governance check
docs.text:
1. Revisit the Delivery baseline.
  2. Check the current GitHub docs for Spaces.
  3. Check repository access and use only synthetic data.
  4. Check the rules for adding and sharing sources.
  5. Set a usage limit and name who can approve more.
  6. Stop if the required sources are missing.

docs.title: Trainer-created context card
docs.text:
Purpose: answer questions about the fictional Checkout API validation behavior.
Audience: workshop participants.
Owner: training repository maintainer.
Review date: before the next cohort.

Include:
- docs/api-contract.md
- src/routes/checkout.ts
- src/services/checkout.ts
- tests/checkout.test.ts
- .github/copilot-instructions.md

Exclude:
- production data
- secrets and credentials
- unrelated services
- abandoned proposals

docs.title: Talking points
docs.text:
• A curated Space may support this workflow when it is available and approved.
  • Do not infer sharing, access, retention, or entitlement behavior.
  • Check those facts in current official documentation and organizational policy.
  • Source-level access does not automatically authorize a new audience or use.
  • Assign an owner and review trigger before sharing.
  • Test the packet with a known question whose answer exists in the sources.

docs.title: Observable outcome
docs.text: Ask learners to explain why they need each included source and why they excluded the others.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "Use the selected sources to understand the project. Repository instructions tell you how to work in it."

docs.title: Segment 4: Instructions and reusable prompts (0:30 to 0:42)
Repository instruction example
docs.text:
# Repository guidance

- Validate request input at the route boundary.
- Keep business logic in src/services/.
- Preserve the documented error response shape.
- Run the focused test before proposing completion.
- Do not add dependencies without reviewer approval.

docs.title: Trainer talking points
docs.text:
• Write instructions a reviewer can check rather than "write high-quality code."
  • Show /env and /instructions in the CLI. Inspect the source and file scope; discovery alone does not prove an instruction was applied.
  • Use the supplied stale CommonJS note in the copied project only. Compare it with the current ES-module contract, correct that note, restart, and inspect again. Do not disable personal, managed, or security rules.
  • Keep project-wide conventions separate from one feature's requirements.
  • Review instruction files through the repository's normal process.
  • Instructions guide proposals; they are not enforcement or proof.
  • Check current supported paths, names, and settings before demonstrating.
  • Stop the runtime-inspection exercise if a required command or source cannot be inspected. A manual checklist does not prove loading.

docs.title: Reusable prompt example
docs.text:
---
description: Review a low-stock endpoint change
---

Read the selected contract, route, service, tests, and repository guidance.
List mismatches before proposing changes.
Do not edit files outside the selected feature.
End with assumptions, cited evidence, and the focused validation command.

docs.title: Pair exercise
docs.text:
Ask pairs to label each sentence as:

  • project-wide instruction;
  • task-specific prompt;
  • acceptance criterion;
  • unsuitable vague guidance.

Debrief disagreements and move feature-specific behavior out of repository-wide rules.

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "Context is useful only while its source, scope, and freshness remain trustworthy."

docs.title: Segment 5: Source governance and maintenance (0:42 to 0:50)
Three-question check
docs.text:
For every source or remembered fact, ask:

  1. Source: Where did this fact come from?
  2. Scope: Which repository, audience, and task does it apply to?
  3. Freshness: When, or after which change, should you check it again?

docs.title: Maintenance table
docs.text: Trigger Required action API contract changes Update packet sources and retest a known question. Repository convention changes Review instruction and prompt files. Source owner changes Assign a new accountable maintainer. Output conflicts with source files Remove stale sources and identify which source governs the task. Product behavior changes Recheck current official documentation. Policy or audience changes Get approval again for using and sharing the sources.

docs.title: Safe delivery wording
docs.text: "Check that memory or context features are available before use. Never store secrets, restricted material, or guesses. The manual source log remains authoritative for this exercise."

docs.title: Transition
docs.text: "Now compare the plans with and without the selected source files."

docs.title: Scripted demo: Low-stock reporting with and without grounding (0:50 to 0:58)
Purpose
docs.text: Compare the responses against clear criteria. Do not claim that a product surface always cites or follows context.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Use four excerpts from the Storefront API lab:

docs/api-spec.md:

Product list responses use the existing data envelope.
Invalid query values use the existing VALIDATION_ERROR response.

src/routes/products.js:

router.get('/:id', async (req, res) => {
  // Existing dynamic route.
});

src/models/product.js defines product stock as a non-negative integer.

The lab task requires GET /api/products/reports/low-stock, an optional non-negative integer threshold, and a default threshold of 10.

Use synthetic data only.

docs.title: Pass A: Minimal prompt
docs.text:
Exact prompt:

Add a low-stock report endpoint.

docs.title: Trainer actions for Pass A
docs.text:
1. If approved access exists, submit the prompt without project context.
  2. Otherwise reveal a prepared generic proposal.
  3. Record assumptions about the route, threshold, error shape, and test command.
  4. Do not score writing style or confidence.

docs.title: Expected observation for Pass A
docs.text:
Look for a route placed after /:id, invalid thresholds accepted, invented errors, or missing checks.

Results may vary. The request lacks the source files needed to judge the proposal.

docs.title: Exact trainer prompt
docs.text:
Exact prompt:

Using only the API specification, product route, product model, and
repository instructions, propose the smallest low-stock endpoint change.
First list acceptance criteria and assumptions.
Do not add dependencies. Reject negative or non-integer thresholds.
End with the source files used and two checks to run.

docs.title: Exact trainer actions for Pass B
docs.text:
1. Check that each source is current and allowed for the lab.
  2. Submit through the context workflow.
  3. Require acceptance criteria before code.
  4. Compare the plan with the API specification and route order.
  5. Ask whether Number.isInteger(Number(value)) would wrongly accept "2".
  6. Check the default and invalid threshold paths.
  7. Record any unsupported assumption.

docs.title: Expected outcome
docs.text:
The grounded response should state the threshold rules, place the static route before /:id, avoid new dependencies, name its source files, and list two checks.

It may then include a code proposal such as:

function parseThreshold(value) {
  if (value === undefined) return 10;
  if (!/^\d+$/.test(value)) {
    throw new Error('threshold must be a non-negative integer');
  }
  return Number(value);
}

Check the existing project before choosing the error type and message.

docs.title: Verification rubric
docs.text: Dimension Pass question Correctness Are the default, valid, and invalid threshold paths represented? Scope Is the proposal limited to the selected feature? Assumptions Are unresolved decisions named? Sources Can each behavior be traced to a source file? Testability Are valid and invalid cases clear? Data Was only synthetic data used?

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
Give half the room only the minimal request.

Give the other half the four-source packet and grounded prompt.

Each group writes a plan, not code.

Swap plans and score them with the rubric.

Reveal the code proposal only during debrief. Use this to recover the trainer demonstration, not as a learner substitute.

docs.title: Demo recovery
docs.text:
• If the surface is unavailable during the demonstration, use the printed responses and fix access before the lab.
  • If it ignores an instruction, mark the mismatch; do not claim enforcement.
  • If sources conflict, stop and assign clarification to the source owner.
  • If the packet is noisy, remove one source and explain the decision.
  • If time expires, compare acceptance criteria and skip code generation.

docs.title: "Should we add the whole repository?"
docs.text: No. Start with the fewest files that support the task, then add a file only when the answer is missing specific information.

docs.title: "Do instructions guarantee compliance?"
docs.text: No. They guide output. Tests, repository checks, and human review enforce the rules.

docs.title: "Which source wins when docs and code disagree?"
docs.text: Do not guess. Find the source owner, record the conflict, and ask them to clarify it before implementation.

docs.title: "Can we include issue comments or meeting notes?"
docs.text: Only when the lab permits them and they are relevant, owned, and current. Separate decisions from unverified discussion.

docs.title: "Does a Space change repository permissions?"
docs.text: Do not guess how access works. Check the current docs and organization rules before adding or sharing a source.

docs.title: "Can we store team conventions in memory?"
docs.text: Keep long-lived team rules in reviewed repository files. Before using a memory feature, check current support, data rules, sources, scope, and review dates.

docs.title: "Why did the grounded response still miss a rule?"
docs.text: Context supplies more information. It does not guarantee correct use. State the rule, test it, and review the result.

docs.title: "What does this cost?"
docs.text: Check current metering information and use the organization's usage limit.

docs.title: Pitfalls, anti-patterns, and recoveries
docs.text: Anti-pattern Recovery "More context is always better" Remove sources that do not affect a criterion. Adding restricted records Stop, remove them, notify the appropriate owner, and use synthetic data. Mixing stale and current contracts Identify authority and update or exclude the stale source. Vague instructions Rewrite them as behavior a test or reviewer can check. Treating citations as correctness Open the source and check the claim. No source owner Assign one or do not share the packet. No review date Add event-based and scheduled maintenance triggers. Assuming instructions loaded Test the expected behavior. Teaching fixed paths or UI Check current docs before delivery. Context changes without review Manage shared artifacts through normal repository review.

docs.title: Closing script
docs.text: "Keep only the sources the task needs. Check that you may share them, and name who will keep them current."

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Open lab/README.md.

Explain that learners will use the same Storefront API to select sources, add repository instructions, compare context, and test reusable prompts.

Check current support before using a changing UI, path, setting, sharing control, or memory feature.

docs.title: Readiness checklist
docs.text:
• Purpose, audience, and owner are written.
  • Every source is allowed for the lab and uses synthetic data.
  • Exclusions are clear.
  • One known-answer question is ready.
  • Maintenance triggers are assigned.
  • Required Spaces and GitHub Copilot access is checked.
  • A usage limit is recorded when it applies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m2-04: Copilot for code review & pull requests
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Copilot in Practice Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-03 Duration: 3 hours (1 hr trainer content + 2 hr lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Follow one pull request from change brief to final human decision. Inspect a flawed change, run /review and /security-review on its local diff, and compare those findings with Copilot PR review. Then correct the code and resolve a conflict. Record the diff, test output, and reviewer decision.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Use Copilot to generate PR summaries and review comments
  • Configure automatic Copilot reviews at repository or organization level
  • Evaluate Copilot review quality and blind spots
  • Run general and security review before committing a local patch
  • Triage unsupported claims and check fixes with regression tests
  • Resolve merge conflicts using the cloud agent
  • Add Copilot to a team code-review workflow
  • Support every blocking comment and accepted fix with a code reference or reproducible check

docs.title: Session materials
docs.text: Resource Location Lab exercises lab/ Lab starter files lab/starter/ Lab solution files lab/solution/

docs.title: Key topics
docs.text:
• PR summaries and commit message generation
  • Copilot code review, manual and automatic
  • Local /review and /security-review, followed by review of the correction diff
  • Security-review scope and its limits alongside repository scanning
  • Review comments with one-click fixes
  • Merge conflict resolution via cloud agent
  • Quality gates and team adoption

docs.title: Diffs, test results, and human judgment
Access and cost preflight
docs.text:
Follow the course safety baseline.

  1. Check the current GitHub docs and your organization's rules.
  2. Check the repository, data, and review permissions.
  3. Use a small pull request with clear acceptance criteria.
  4. Set a usage limit for metered work.

docs.title: Review is a human responsibility
docs.text:
Automation may raise questions. A reviewer decides whether a change is correct, safe, maintainable, and within scope.

Issue and acceptance criteria
        ↓
Proposed change and checks
        ↓
Human review
        ↓
Accept, request revision, or implement manually

docs.title: Review rubric
docs.text:
• Correctness against acceptance criteria
  • Tests and check results
  • Security, dependency, and permission implications
  • Scope and maintainability
  • Repository conventions and human approval

docs.title: Conflict-resolution exercise
docs.text:
1. Read both branch intentions.
  2. Write the merged behavior and tests before editing.
  3. Resolve the conflict manually in the repository sandbox.
  4. Run checks and request review.
  5. Demonstrate an approved assisted workflow only after checking current documentation and policy.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
Check CLI /review and /security-review, Copilot PR review, Git, Node.js, and npm. Use a private training remote with the baseline branch already present.

Stop if a command or review access is missing. A worksheet does not replace the required runs.

docs.title: Review the same diff through separate passes
docs.text:
1. Record the human verdict before assisted review.
  2. Leave the patch uncommitted and run /review.
  3. Run /security-review against that same local patch.
  4. Triage both outputs, then commit and request Copilot PR review.
  5. Repeat the local commands on the correction diff before committing fixes.

Keep the original verdict. Record no-findings results honestly.

docs.title: A finding needs support
docs.text:
Claim Check Exposed password field Inspect the actual response and add a regression test Database compromise The mock route never executes SQL; reject that claim Leaked credential The strings are fake and unused; do not claim a live leak Pagination defect Check page-one behavior separately from security review

Record: review source, file/line, impact, check, and triage decision.

docs.title: Security review has a narrow scope
docs.text:
/security-review examines current local changes. It is read-only and does not replace repository security scanning.

A clean result does not prove that a change is secure. The human reviewer still decides.

docs.title: Agenda and time plan
docs.text:
Time Topic Trainer move 0:00 Review workflow and roles Define accountability 0:08 Summaries and descriptions Separate draft from evidence 0:18 Local commands and PR review Keep the patch uncommitted 0:28 Defect and triage demo Check behavior and reject unsupported claims 0:43 Suggestions and conflicts Preserve author intent 0:51 Limits and adoption Design human gates 0:58 Lab handoff and Q&A Assign reviewer roles

Transition: "Copilot can increase review coverage; it cannot own the decision."

docs.title: Copilot across a PR lifecycle
docs.text:
Issue and acceptance criteria
          ↓
Branch and bounded commits
          ↓
Draft summary and PR description
          ↓
Automated checks + Copilot first pass
          ↓
Human review and author response
          ↓
Approval, revision, or close

At each stage, save the output the reviewer needs to check the change.

docs.title: Commit messages and PR descriptions
docs.text:
Copilot can draft text from the visible change, but authors must check:

  • the user-visible behavior is accurate;
  • tests and results are not invented;
  • breaking changes and migrations are named;
  • security and dependency implications are named;
  • issue links and acceptance criteria match the work;
  • no sensitive details appear in generated prose.

A polished summary can still be wrong.

docs.title: A reviewable PR template
docs.text:
## Problem
What user-visible problem does this solve?

## Change
List the bounded implementation choices.

## Validation
- [ ] Focused tests
- [ ] Existing checks
- [ ] Manual edge case

## Risk and rollback
Name data, dependency, security, and recovery considerations.

docs.title: Requesting Copilot review
docs.text:
For a manual request:

  1. Check that the PR is ready for a first pass.
  2. Check current availability, permissions, and repository policy.
  3. Request the Copilot review through the supported PR control.
  4. Wait for comments and review them as hypotheses.
  5. Resolve them, reject them with a reason, or implement a checked fix.
  6. Request human review with the diff, findings, and check results.

Do not use Copilot review to bypass required reviewers.

docs.title: Automatic review configuration
docs.text:
Automatic review can be configured at repository or organization scope when supported.

Before enabling:

  • identify eligible repositories and excluded data;
  • define when reviews run and who owns triage;
  • preserve branch protection and required human approvals;
  • monitor noise, missed findings, and review delay;
  • document an off switch and escalation owner.

Trainer cue: Demonstrate navigation, not fixed UI labels that may change.

docs.title: Quality gates
docs.text:
