Module: Agentic Workflows

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Design a canvas extension for one synthetic delivery-readiness board. Start with the contract, then create the canvas in the GitHub Copilot app with the required access. Test direct and agent-requested updates, including a rejected update and recovery. Compare the final canvas with the contract.

A canvas is a shared interactive surface. People use visible controls while an agent uses named capabilities against the same state. The canvas does not replace the system that owns the work.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Choose a canvas only when visible shared state improves the workflow.
  • Separate canvas state, human actions, and agent-callable capabilities.
  • Write validation rules that reject unsafe or incomplete state changes.
  • Create and review a project-scoped or user-scoped canvas.
  • Recover from a rejected action without weakening the contract.
  • Record ownership, review, failure handling, and retirement decisions.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. a completed canvas contract;
  2. a canvas created in a sandbox you have approval to use;
  3. checkpoint records for direct, agent-requested, rejected, and recovered changes;
  4. a final state that matches the contract.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
The lab requires GitHub Copilot app access and the built-in /create-canvas skill. Project scope also requires approval to create files under .github/extensions.

If app access or /create-canvas is unavailable, stop the lab. If project scope is unavailable, use user scope. Do not bypass policy or install a replacement.

The default lab remains the delivery-readiness board. An optional Feature Workbench variant uses synthetic CI results to practice a test-gate decision:

docs.title: Define the contract, state, and allowed actions
Today's outcome
docs.text:
Build or simulate one delivery-readiness canvas.

Record these in the demo:

  • the approved contract;
  • one direct update;
  • one agent-requested update;
  • one rejected update and recovery;
  • one human review decision.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
The lab requires:

  • GitHub Copilot app access;
  • the built-in /create-canvas skill;
  • approval for the chosen extension scope.

If app access or the skill is missing, stop the lab. If project scope is unavailable, use user scope. Do not install a replacement or move data to an unapproved surface.

docs.title: Pick the smallest fit
docs.text:
Need Use Repository convention Instructions Repeatable procedure Skill Specialist behavior Custom agent External tool or data MCP server Shared interactive artifact Canvas Packaged customizations Plugin

A canvas is useful when people and an agent need to inspect or change the same visible state.

docs.title: Canvas anatomy
docs.text:
shared state
  ├─ human actions in the interface
  ├─ agent-callable capabilities
  └─ validation before every change

The contract names all four parts before implementation starts.

docs.title: Worked contract
docs.text: Part Delivery-readiness rule State item, status, review flag, evidence Status planned, in-progress, review, ready Human actions add item, set status, flag review, add evidence Agent capabilities read board, update one named item, list flagged items Validation known item, accepted status, evidence before ready

docs.title: Authority stays narrow
docs.text:
Safe:

  • read the current board;
  • update one named item;
  • list items flagged for review.

Out of scope:

  • deployment;
  • external writes;
  • credentials;
  • hidden data imports;
  • broad actions such as "manage the project."

docs.title: Prepared demo inputs
docs.text:
ID Item Start state Evidence DOC-101 Draft operator guide planned none API-204 Add retry metric in-progress test log WEB-318 Check empty state review preview

All names and evidence are synthetic.

docs.title: Prepared demo sequence
docs.text:
1. Run the local contract tests.
  2. Create the canvas from the worked prompt.
  3. Move WEB-318 to ready with a visible control.
  4. Ask the agent to move API-204 to review.
  5. Ask for DOC-101 to move to ready.
  6. Show the rejection, add evidence, and retry.

docs.title: Creation prompt
docs.text:
/create-canvas

Create a delivery-readiness canvas from @prepared-items.json.
Use the contract in @canvas-contract.md.
People can add evidence and update one item.
Copilot can read the board, update one named item, and list review flags.
Reject unknown items or statuses. Require evidence before ready.
Do not connect external systems.

Choose project scope only when .github/extensions is allowed. Otherwise use user scope.

docs.title: Visible and agent-requested changes
docs.text:
The same state must change through both paths:

Path Evidence Human control The item visibly changes in the canvas Agent capability The named item changes and the response matches the canvas

If the response and visible state disagree, stop and inspect the artifact.

docs.title: Rejection is part of the design
docs.text:
Request:

Move DOC-101 to ready.

Expected:

Rejected: evidence is required before ready.

A safe canvas keeps the state unchanged and explains the rule.

docs.title: Recovery keeps the rule
docs.text:
1. Add synthetic evidence to DOC-101.
  2. Retry the same transition.
  3. Check that ready is now accepted.
  4. Record before, rejection, correction, and after state.

Keep validation in place when you fix the demo.

docs.title: Review the generated extension
docs.text:
Check:

  • state fields and defaults;
  • visible actions;
  • agent-callable capabilities;
  • dependencies and persisted data;
  • owner and reviewer;
  • retirement trigger.

Remove anything the contract did not request.

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text:
The canvas is a working artifact, not an automatic system of record.

If another system owns the data:

  • label the canvas as a projection;
  • record refresh or reconciliation rules;
  • keep external writes outside this lab.

docs.title: Peer decision
docs.text:
The reviewer chooses:

  • approve when the recorded results match the contract;
  • revise when the correction fits the contract;
  • pause when access, ownership, data, or behavior is unresolved.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text: Use one contract and one prepared data set for the full two hours.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-01 lab: Build and review a canvas contract
docs.text: Duration: 2 hours Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 Deliverable: A tested canvas and its final state

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Use one synthetic delivery-readiness contract from setup through handoff. Test the contract locally, then create or simulate the canvas. Make visible and agent-requested changes to the same state. Check that an invalid change is rejected, then recover without changing the rule.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. your completed canvas-contract.md;
  2. the generated extension location;
  3. final state that matches the accepted transitions.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
The lab requires GitHub Copilot app access and the built-in /create-canvas skill. Project scope requires approval to create files under .github/extensions.

If app access or the skill is unavailable, stop the lab. If project scope is not available, use user scope. Do not install a replacement or copy the synthetic workflow into another external service.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
From the repository root:

cd sessions/session-m3-01-copilot-app-canvases/lab/starter
npm test

Expected result:

tests 4
pass 4
fail 0

Open these files:

  • canvas-contract.md
  • prepared-items.json
  • demo-runbook.md

Copy the record files to a writable working folder if you do not want to edit the starter assets.

docs.title: Time plan
docs.text: Part Work Time 1 Check access and contract 20 min 2 Run the prepared contract tests 15 min 3 Create the canvas 25 min 4 Make two visible state changes 20 min 5 Check rejection and recovery 20 min 6 Inspect and hand off 20 min

docs.title: Part 1: Check access and contract (20 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Select project or user scope.
  2. Check that all data comes from prepared-items.json.
  3. Review every state field, human action, agent capability, and validation rule in canvas-contract.md.
  4. Replace the owner and reviewer placeholders.
  5. Check the retirement trigger.

The contract must retain these rules:

  • statuses are planned, in-progress, review, and ready;
  • only one named item changes per update;
  • ready requires non-empty evidence;
  • unknown items and statuses are rejected;
  • no external system is connected.

Checkpoint 1: A peer can explain the contract without adding verbal requirements.

docs.title: Part 2: Run the prepared contract tests (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Run:

npm test

Read test/canvas-contract.test.mjs and map each test to a contract rule.

Record:

  • the command;
  • pass or fail;
  • the four rules tested;
  • any mismatch between code and contract.

Do not continue with a failing harness. Fix only a mismatch caused by your edits, or reset your working copy from lab/starter/.

Checkpoint 2: Your local harness passes, and your group can identify the planned rejection.

docs.title: Part 3: Create the canvas (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open a GitHub Copilot app session with the required access. Run:

/create-canvas

Create a delivery-readiness canvas from @prepared-items.json.
Use the contract in @canvas-contract.md.
People can add evidence and update one item.
Copilot can read the board, update one named item, and list review flags.
Reject unknown items or statuses. Require evidence before ready.
Do not connect external systems.

Choose:

  • project scope only when .github/extensions is approved for the training repository;
  • user scope when a personal local extension is approved.

Inspect the generated directory, metadata, dependencies, state, visible controls, and agent-callable capabilities. Ask Copilot to remove anything outside the contract.

Checkpoint 3: The canvas shows all three prepared items and no extra capability.

docs.title: Part 4: Make two visible state changes (20 minutes)
docs.text: Use the same state for both paths.

docs.title: Change A: direct human action
docs.text:
Move WEB-318 from review to ready.

This should succeed because the item already has evidence.

docs.title: Change B: agent-requested action
docs.text:
Ask Copilot:

Move API-204 from in-progress to review. Change only that item.

Check:

  • WEB-318 is ready;
  • API-204 is review;
  • DOC-101 is still planned;
  • the visible state and response agree.

Compare the before and after values in the canvas state.

Checkpoint 4: One human action and one agent-requested capability changed the same state model without breaking the contract.

docs.title: Part 5: Check rejection and recovery (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Request:

Move DOC-101 to ready.

Expected result:

Rejected: evidence is required before ready.

Check that DOC-101 remains planned.

Now add this synthetic evidence:

docs://operator-guide-review

Retry the same status change. It should succeed.

Record:

  1. state before the request;
  2. rejection text;
  3. evidence added;
  4. final accepted state.

If the first request succeeds, stop. Restore the validation rule and repeat the case. Do not approve a canvas that reaches ready without evidence.

Checkpoint 5: Recovery corrected the data and kept the rule.

docs.title: Part 6: Inspect and hand off (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Exchange canvases with another group. Inspect:

  • artifact location and scope;
  • state and defaults;
  • visible human actions;
  • agent-callable capabilities;
  • rejection and recovery records;
  • dependencies and persisted data;
  • owner and retirement trigger.

Fix contract mismatches. Pause if access, behavior, data, or ownership remains unresolved. Then compare the final state with ../solution/final-state.json.

Checkpoint 6: The canvas matches the contract and is safe to hand off.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Your work is complete when another person can identify:

  • the selected extension scope;
  • the fixed canvas contract;
  • the prepared starting state;
  • both accepted changes;
  • the rejected change and recovery.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Response /create-canvas is unavailable Stop the lab. Project scope is blocked Use user scope. Generated actions exceed the contract Remove them before testing. State and agent response disagree Stop and inspect the shared artifact. Local tests fail before edits Record the failure and restore the supplied starter files. ready accepts empty evidence Fix the rule before review.

Use this variant only after the default delivery-readiness lab, or when the trainer assigns it as follow-up practice. It does not replace the required deliverable.

  1. Open starter/feature-workbench-contract.md.

  4. Record the required check that blocks the decision.

The canvas may propose pass, hold, or rerun. A named human reviewer owns the final decision. Do not connect a live CI system, merge code, or trigger deployment.

docs.title: Teaching goal
docs.text: Teach learners to define a canvas contract and explain each action. Demonstrate a safe rejection, then show how to check whether the final state is safe to share.

docs.title: Required preparation
docs.text:
Before class:

  1. Check GitHub Copilot app access and the built-in /create-canvas skill.
  2. Decide whether project scope under .github/extensions is allowed. Use user scope when it is not.
  3. Use only the synthetic files in ../lab/starter/.
  4. Run:
cd sessions/session-m3-01-copilot-app-canvases/lab/starter
npm test
  1. Open prepared-items.json, canvas-contract.md, and demo-runbook.md.
  2. Name the demo owner and reviewer.
  3. Keep ../lab/solution/demo-evidence.md ready for a delayed or unavailable live run.

The delivery-readiness board is the default. For an early-finisher, follow-up, or CI-focused audience, prepare the optional Feature Workbench files:

  • ../lab/starter/feature-workbench-contract.md
  • ../lab/starter/feature-workbench-sample.json
  • ../lab/solution/feature-workbench-solution.md
  • ../lab/solution/feature-workbench-final-state.json

Do not replace the main demo or change the one-hour plan. The variant reuses the same contract-first method with a narrower decision: whether synthetic feature work may pass a test gate.

docs.title: Access decision
docs.text:
The live demo requires all of these:

  • GitHub Copilot app access;
  • /create-canvas is present;
  • the chosen extension scope is approved;
  • the trainer can inspect generated files and capabilities;
  • synthetic data is used.

If any condition fails, use the prepared manual demo. Do not bypass a policy, install a community replacement, or claim that a generated extension ran when it did not.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment What learners show 0:00 to 0:05 Outcome and access check Required access checked 0:05 to 0:13 Choose the right customization Canvas decision explained 0:13 to 0:23 Build the contract State, actions, capabilities, validation 0:23 to 0:30 Inspect prepared inputs and harness Passing local contract tests 0:30 to 0:43 Prepared or live canvas demo Two visible state changes 0:43 to 0:50 Rejection and recovery Rule preserved through recovery 0:50 to 0:56 Generated extension review Keep, revise, or remove decisions 0:56 to 1:00 Lab handoff Roles, deliverables, and checkpoints clear

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:05: Set the outcome and access gate
docs.text:
Say:

"We are designing one shared artifact. Judge it by its visible behavior, not by a polished chat response."

Show the required deliverables. Tell the class whether you will use the live or prepared demo.

Ask one learner to name a condition that should stop the canvas from being shared.

docs.title: 0:05 to 0:13: Choose the right customization
docs.text:
Use the decision table from the slides.

Make the distinction concrete:

  • instructions state conventions;
  • a skill describes a repeatable procedure;
  • a custom agent supplies specialist behavior;
  • an MCP server connects tools or data;
  • a canvas gives people and an agent one interactive artifact;
  • a plugin can package a canvas with other customizations.

Use a canvas when the state must stay visible across several actions or a handoff. Stay in chat for a short answer or one draft.

Checkpoint: Ask, "What breaks if this remains only in chat?" A valid answer names lost visibility, direct control, or saved state for handoff.

docs.title: 0:13 to 0:23: Build the worked contract
docs.text:
Open ../lab/starter/canvas-contract.md.

Walk through each section:

  1. State: id, item, status, reviewFlag, and evidence.
  2. Human actions: add evidence, set a status, and set the review flag.
  3. Agent capabilities: read the board, update one named item, and list flagged items.
  4. Validation: reject unknown IDs, unknown statuses, and ready without evidence.
  5. Boundary: synthetic data and no external systems.

Ask who can retire the artifact. Record an owner rather than saying "the team."

Teaching test: Every action must fit in one sentence. A broad verb such as "manage" needs a smaller action.

docs.title: 0:23 to 0:30: Inspect prepared inputs and contract harness
docs.text:
Open prepared-items.json. Point out the three starting states and which item lacks evidence.

Run:

cd sessions/session-m3-01-copilot-app-canvases/lab/starter
npm test

Explain that the harness does not imitate the GitHub Copilot app. It checks the state rules that the generated canvas must preserve.

Show these results:

  • an item with evidence can move to ready;
  • an agent-requested named update changes the same state model;
  • DOC-101 cannot move to ready without evidence;
  • adding evidence allows the retry.

docs.title: Live route
docs.text:
Start an app session with the required access and use:

/create-canvas

Create a delivery-readiness canvas from @prepared-items.json.
Use the contract in @canvas-contract.md.
People can add evidence and update one item.
Copilot can read the board, update one named item, and list review flags.
Reject unknown items or statuses. Require evidence before ready.
Do not connect external systems.

Choose project scope only when repository sharing is approved. Otherwise use user scope.

After generation:

  1. inspect the files and declared capabilities;
  2. remove fields or actions outside the contract;
  3. use a visible control to move WEB-318 from review to ready;
  4. ask Copilot to move API-204 from in-progress to review;
  5. compare the visible board with the agent response.

docs.title: Prepared route
docs.text:
Open ../lab/solution/demo-evidence.md and ../lab/solution/final-state.json.

Trace the same two changes. Label each statement as an observed result or a prepared example. Do not imply that a live app call occurred.

docs.title: Time guard
docs.text: If the canvas is not ready for review by 0:38, switch to the prepared demo record. Keep the rejection, recovery, and review segments.

docs.title: 0:43 to 0:50: Show rejection and recovery
docs.text:
Request:

Move DOC-101 to ready.

Expected behavior:

  • the update is rejected;
  • the message names the missing evidence rule;
  • DOC-101 remains planned.

Add the synthetic evidence value docs://operator-guide-review, then retry.

Expected behavior:

  • the same transition now succeeds;
  • the rule did not change;
  • the change record shows the state before the request, the rejection, the correction, and the state afterward.

If the generated canvas accepts the first request, pause the demo. Restore the rule before continuing. A successful unsafe update is a failed demo.

docs.title: 0:50 to 0:56: Inspect the extension
docs.text:
Inspect:

  • generated files and dependencies;
  • state fields and persisted data;
  • visible human actions;
  • agent-callable capabilities;
  • validation messages;
  • owner, failure handling, and retirement trigger.

Remove generated features that the contract did not request. Pause if the canvas still violates the contract.

docs.title: 0:56 to 1:00: Hand off to the lab
docs.text:
Assign four roles. One person may hold two roles in a small group:

  • contract owner;
  • app operator or manual simulator;
  • contract tester;
  • handoff owner.

Point learners to the six lab checkpoints. Remind them that the same three prepared items stay in use for the full lab.

End with:

"Keep the contract fixed while you test the implementation. If the implementation needs broader authority, stop and review the contract first."

docs.title: Common failures and recovery
docs.text: Failure Recovery /create-canvas is missing Stop the lab. Do not install a replacement. Project scope is not allowed Use user scope. Generation takes too long Stop the run and show the prepared demo record. Extra capabilities appear Remove them and record the review decision. Agent response and visible state differ Stop, inspect the artifact, and record the mismatch. ready succeeds without evidence Treat it as a failed rule, fix it, and rerun the rejection. A learner proposes real work data Replace it with the supplied synthetic input.

docs.title: Optional Feature Workbench guidance
docs.text:
Use this variant after the default flow or as a separate practice task. Learners review three synthetic CI checks, reject a gate decision when a required check fails, then record the evidence that allows a retry.

Keep the authority narrow:

  • people may acknowledge a result and request a gate evaluation;
  • the agent may read checks and propose pass, hold, or rerun;
  • only a named human reviewer records the final gate decision;
  • the workbench must not trigger deployment, merge a pull request, or call a live CI service.

The worked solution holds FEAT-204 because integration-tests failed. A retry is valid only after the sample state contains a passing required check.

docs.title: Product notes checked October 5, 2026
docs.text: Official GitHub documentation describes canvas extensions as shared interactive surfaces in the GitHub Copilot app. It documents /create-canvas, project scope at .github/extensions, user scope at ~/.copilot/extensions, visible canvas controls, and agent-callable capabilities. Availability and policy can still differ, so complete the required preparation before class.

docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-02: Copilot cloud agent
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Agentic Workflows

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Take one synthetic issue from its contract to a human review decision. Prepare the repository and start a Copilot cloud agent session. Then inspect the proposed change and run the required tests before deciding whether to approve, request changes, or pause.

Keep the issue fixed throughout the work: reject blank or whitespace-only task titles while preserving valid task creation.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Write an issue with testable acceptance criteria, allowed files, and non-goals.
  • Review repository instructions and Copilot setup steps before assignment.
  • Monitor an agent session without expanding the issue or its repository access.
  • Compare a proposed change with the issue and allowed file scope.
  • Run and record focused tests.
  • Name the human reviewer and record their decision.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. the fixed issue contract;
  2. the proposed change;
  3. focused test output;
  4. the review outcome.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
Learners need Copilot cloud agent access to the training repository, synthetic data, and a human reviewer.

If anything is missing, do not assign the issue. Stop the lab.

docs.title: Session materials
docs.text: Resource Purpose trainer-content/README.md Minute-mapped teaching and demo plan slides.md Trainer-facing teaching deck lab/README.md Two-hour issue-to-review lab lab/starter/ Issue, setup, sample project, and review guide lab/solution/ Completed issue journey and runnable solution

docs.title: Current product references
docs.text:
Product notes were checked against official GitHub documentation on October 5, 2026. Trainers must recheck access and policy before delivery:

  • Get started with Copilot agents on GitHub
  • Managing agent sessions
  • Configure the development environment
  • Add repository custom instructions

docs.title: Keep the Copilot cloud agent within the issue
Today's journey
docs.text:
issue contract
    ↓
repository setup
    ↓
proposed change
    ↓
test evidence
    ↓
human decision

Keep the same issue and acceptance criteria at every step.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
The live route requires:

  • approved Copilot cloud agent access;
  • a training repository with synthetic data;
  • a named reviewer;
  • an issue with a file scope and stop condition.

If any requirement is missing, stop the lab. Do not bypass policy.

docs.title: The fixed issue
docs.text:
Reject blank task titles

Allowed files:

  • src/app.js
  • tests/app.test.js

Required command:

npm test

No dependency changes. No unrelated refactor.

docs.title: Checkpoint 1: Issue contract
docs.text:
The reviewer must answer:

  • Which behavior changes?
  • Which behavior stays the same?
  • Which files may change?
  • What proves completion?
  • What is out of scope?

Do not assign the issue until every answer is clear.

docs.title: Repository instructions
docs.text:
Tell the agent how to work in this repository:

  • project shape;
  • coding conventions;
  • allowed file scope;
  • test command;
  • prohibited changes.

Instructions support the issue. They do not repair a vague issue.

docs.title: Copilot setup steps
docs.text:
The workflow file belongs at:

.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml

It uses one job named:

copilot-setup-steps

Review permissions, commands, and secrets before merging it to the default branch.

docs.title: Checkpoint 2: Setup
docs.text:
Record:

  • baseline test result;
  • repository instructions location;
  • setup workflow location;
  • allowed files;
  • reviewer and stop condition.

Stop when the baseline is unexplained or setup requires unapproved access.

docs.title: Start the session
docs.text:
• assign the fixed issue through an entry point allowed by repository policy;
  • watch the session log;
  • steer only within the issue;
  • stop on scope drift.

docs.title: Checkpoint 3: Proposed change
docs.text:
Inspect before running tests:

  • changed files;
  • validation behavior;
  • response shape;
  • valid request behavior;
  • dependency and configuration changes.

A small diff can still be wrong.

docs.title: The expected behavior
docs.text:
if (typeof title !== "string" || title.trim() === "") {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: "title is required" });
}

The code may differ, but it must preserve the required behavior and constraints.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4: Tests
docs.text:
Required cases:

Case Expected "" HTTP 400 " " HTTP 400 " Weekly plan " HTTP 201 with preserved response shape

Run the full supplied suite and record the command output.

docs.title: Keep review feedback within the issue
docs.text:
Good:

The whitespace case is missing. Add a focused test in tests/app.test.js.
Keep the current response shape and do not change other endpoints.
Run npm test and report the result.

Bad:

Clean up the API while you are there.

docs.title: Checkpoint 5: Human decision
docs.text:
Choose:

  • approve when criteria, scope, and tests pass;
  • request changes when a correction within the issue remains;
  • pause when access, test output, or ownership is unresolved.

The agent does not make this decision.

docs.title: Stop conditions
docs.text:
Stop the live route when:

  • the requested files expand;
  • a new dependency appears;
  • credentials or unapproved data are requested;
  • repeated test failures have no recovery plan;
  • the issue changes during implementation;
  • the reviewer is no longer available.

docs.title: Trainer demo recovery
docs.text:
The solution folder contains:

  • the final issue contract;
  • reviewed setup workflow;
  • proposed diff;
  • runnable solution project;
  • test output;
  • completed human decision.

Use it only when the trainer demo is delayed. Learners still need a live cloud-agent run for lab completion.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text: Keep the same issue through all five checkpoints. Record the reviewer's decision.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-02 lab: One issue from contract to review
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04

Deliverable: One reviewed change with passing focused tests

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Take one synthetic issue from its fixed contract through setup and implementation, then test and review the change. Use Copilot cloud agent only when you have approval to use it. Otherwise complete the same work manually.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. the fixed issue.md;
  2. the proposed diff or pull request reference;
  3. test output;
  4. the review outcome in the pull request or local review.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text:
You need Copilot cloud agent access to the training repository, synthetic data, and a reviewer.

If access, policy approval, or reviewer ownership is missing, do not assign the issue. Stop the lab. Do not add credentials to issues, instructions, setup workflows, or comments.

docs.title: The one issue
docs.text:
Use starter/issue.md for the entire lab.

The request is:

Reject blank or whitespace-only task titles.

Do not replace it with another issue, add another endpoint, or expand it into API cleanup.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
From the repository root:

cd sessions/session-m3-02-cloud-agent/lab
npm --prefix starter/sample-project install
npm --prefix starter/sample-project test

Expected result: the starter suite passes before the new validation is added.

Open:

  • ../issue.md
  • ../copilot-instructions.md
  • ../copilot-setup-steps.yml
  • ../pr-review-checklist.md

The setup workflow belongs at .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml in a live training repository.

docs.title: Time plan
docs.text: Checkpoint Work Time 1 Approve the issue contract 20 min 2 Check repository setup 20 min 3 Produce and inspect the proposed change 35 min 4 Run and review tests 25 min 5 Make the human decision 20 min

docs.title: Checkpoint 1: Issue contract (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Read starter/issue.md.

Have a peer answer:

  • Which request is invalid?
  • What exact response is required?
  • Which valid behavior must remain?
  • Which files may change?
  • Which command proves completion?
  • What is out of scope?

Clarify any ambiguous issue text before implementation.

Result: The issue has fixed acceptance criteria, allowed files, non-goals, and a stop condition.

docs.title: Checkpoint 2: Setup (20 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Review starter/copilot-instructions.md.
  2. Review starter/copilot-setup-steps.yml.
  3. Check that the workflow content targets .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml.
  4. Check that the single job is named copilot-setup-steps.
  5. Run the starter baseline:
npm --prefix starter/sample-project test
  1. Record the command and result.
  2. Record the allowed file list: src/app.js and tests/app.test.js.

Stop if the baseline failure is unexplained, setup needs a credential, or any required command is not approved.

Checkpoint record: Passing test output, reviewed setup files, named reviewer, and stop condition.

docs.title: Checkpoint 3: Proposed change (35 minutes)
docs.text:
Place the sample project in an approved training repository. Add the reviewed instructions and setup workflow if policy permits. Copy the contents of starter/sample-project/ to the repository root. The setup workflow expects package.json, package-lock.json, src/, and tests/ at that root.

Create or reuse the one issue from starter/issue.md. Assign it through a currently supported Copilot cloud agent entry point allowed by repository policy.

Monitor the session. Record:

  • files the agent plans to change;
  • commands it reports;
  • questions or steering;
  • the final proposed files.

Use this message only if the work drifts:

Keep the existing issue contract. Change only src/app.js and tests/app.test.js.
Add no dependency. Stop and ask for clarification if broader work is required.

docs.title: Review the proposal
docs.text:
Before tests, inspect the diff with starter/pr-review-checklist.md.

Check:

  • only the two allowed files changed;
  • blank and whitespace-only titles return HTTP 400;
  • the error body is { "error": "title is required" };
  • valid task creation keeps its existing response shape;
  • no dependency or unrelated endpoint changed.

If no proposal is ready after 25 minutes, stop the run.

Checkpoint record: A pull request or agent-produced diff tied to the same issue.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4: Tests (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Run:

npm test

The test output must cover:

Case Expected result Empty title "" HTTP 400 and required error body Whitespace title " " HTTP 400 and required error body Valid title " Weekly plan " HTTP 201 with the existing response fields Existing endpoints Existing tests still pass

If a required case is missing, request a test for that case. Do not add a new issue or unrelated cleanup.

Result: The reviewed proposal has focused test output.

docs.title: Checkpoint 5: Human decision (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Use starter/pr-review-checklist.md to inspect the change.

Choose:

  • approve when the issue, diff, and tests agree;
  • request changes when a correction within the issue remains;
  • pause when access, test output, policy, or ownership is unresolved.

Compare the result with solution/issue-journey.md after the review.

Result: The pull request or local review shows the outcome. Do not merge as part of this lab unless the training repository policy explicitly requires it.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Your work is complete when another reviewer can trace:

same issue → reviewed setup → proposed change → tests → review outcome

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Response Copilot cloud agent access is missing Stop the lab. Setup workflow is not active on the default branch Stop the lab. Session edits extra files Stop or ask the agent to change only the allowed files. Test output is missing Run the required test command before deciding. A test passes but response shape changed Request changes and cite the criterion for preserving the response shape. Review suggests a second feature Record it as future work, outside this issue.

docs.title: Solution reference
docs.text: solution/ contains the completed issue journey and final review decision. It also includes the prepared diff, setup workflow, runnable solution project, and test output.

docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-02: Trainer guide
docs.text:
00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide Enable timer shortcut (T)

Teaching time: 60 minutes

Lab handoff: ../lab/README.md

docs.title: Teaching goal
docs.text: Demonstrate one issue from assignment through review. At each checkpoint, ask learners to show the relevant files or test output and name the human who decides what happens next.

docs.title: Required preparation
docs.text:
Before class:

  1. Check whether Copilot cloud agent is approved for the training repository.
  2. Use only the synthetic task API in ../lab/starter/sample-project/.
  3. Name the reviewer and define the stop condition.
  4. Run:
cd sessions/session-m3-02-cloud-agent/lab/starter/sample-project
npm install
npm test
  1. Review ../lab/starter/issue.md.
  2. Review ../lab/starter/copilot-instructions.md.
  3. Review ../lab/starter/copilot-setup-steps.yml as content intended for .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml.
  4. Keep ../lab/solution/issue-journey.md and ../lab/solution/proposed-change.diff ready.

docs.title: Access decision
docs.text:
The live route requires:

  • Copilot cloud agent is enabled for the repository;
  • the repository and synthetic data are approved;
  • the issue and setup are reviewed;
  • a human reviewer is named;
  • the stop condition is visible.

If any condition is missing, stop and resolve it. Do not assign the issue, broaden access, or paste credentials into an issue or instruction file.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment What to check 0:00 to 0:05 Frame and access decision Live route confirmed 0:05 to 0:16 Checkpoint 1: issue contract Approved issue 0:16 to 0:27 Checkpoint 2: setup Passing baseline and reviewed setup 0:27 to 0:39 Start or simulate one session Planned files, commands, and edits stay within the issue 0:39 to 0:47 Checkpoint 3: proposed change Scoped diff review 0:47 to 0:54 Checkpoint 4: tests Recorded test result 0:54 to 0:58 Checkpoint 5: human decision Approve, request changes, or pause 0:58 to 1:00 Lab handoff Roles and records ready

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:05: Frame the journey
docs.text:
Show the five-checkpoint sequence.

Say:

"We will keep one issue fixed from assignment through review. If the work needs a different issue, we stop and write one."

State how the class will access the agent. Ask the reviewer to accept responsibility for the final decision.

docs.title: 0:05 to 0:16: Checkpoint 1: issue contract
docs.text:
Start with this weak request:

Fix title validation.

Open ../lab/starter/issue.md. Show how the same request gains testable criteria and a file scope:

  • blank and whitespace-only titles return HTTP 400;
  • the error body is { "error": "title is required" };
  • valid creation keeps its response shape;
  • only src/app.js and tests/app.test.js may change;
  • npm test must pass;
  • no dependency or unrelated endpoint change is allowed.

Ask a learner to map each criterion to a test or diff check.

Gate: Do not assign the issue until a peer can name changed behavior, preserved behavior, allowed files, required checks, and non-goals.

docs.title: 0:16 to 0:27: Checkpoint 2: setup
docs.text:
Open ../lab/starter/copilot-instructions.md.

Check that it describes:

  • Node.js and the supplied Express app;
  • file scope;
  • response format;
  • no new dependencies;
  • npm test.

Open ../lab/starter/copilot-setup-steps.yml.

Explain that the asset is intended for:

.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml

Point out the single job named copilot-setup-steps, minimum required permissions, dependency install, and baseline test.

Run the local baseline:

cd sessions/session-m3-02-cloud-agent/lab/starter/sample-project
npm test

Gate: Stop when the baseline fails without an explanation, setup requests a credential, or the reviewer cannot identify the allowed files.

docs.title: 0:27 to 0:39: Start or simulate one session
Live route
docs.text:
Assign only ../lab/starter/issue.md through a currently supported entry point allowed by repository policy.

Watch the session and record what it shows:

  • planned files;
  • commands;
  • edits;
  • test reports;
  • questions or scope changes.

Use this steering message only if needed:

Keep the current issue contract. Change only src/app.js and tests/app.test.js.
Add no dependency. Stop and ask for clarification if broader work is required.

Stop on scope drift. Do not edit the issue during the run.

docs.title: Time guard
docs.text: At 0:35, use ../lab/solution/proposed-change.diff only to finish the trainer demonstration if no reviewable proposal exists. Fix access or runtime problems before the learner lab.

docs.title: 0:39 to 0:47: Checkpoint 3: proposed change
docs.text:
Review the live or prepared diff before running tests.

Check:

  1. Only src/app.js and tests/app.test.js changed.
  2. Blank and whitespace-only strings are rejected.
  3. The response body matches the issue.
  4. Valid task creation preserves its response shape.
  5. No dependency, configuration, or unrelated endpoint changed.

Use ../lab/starter/pr-review-checklist.md.

Model one review comment that stays within the issue:

The blank-title test passes, but the whitespace case is missing.
Add that focused test in tests/app.test.js. Keep the current file scope,
then run npm test and report the result.

docs.title: 0:47 to 0:54: Checkpoint 4: tests
docs.text:
Run:

npm test

Require test results for:

  • empty string;
  • whitespace-only string;
  • valid title with surrounding whitespace;
  • all existing endpoints.

Passing tests are necessary, but they do not replace diff review.

If a test fails, decide whether the correction fits the issue. Request that change or pause.

docs.title: 0:54 to 0:58: Checkpoint 5: human decision
docs.text:
The named reviewer chooses:

  • approve when scope, behavior, and tests match the issue;
  • request changes when the required correction stays within the issue;
  • pause when access, test output, policy, or ownership is unresolved.

Do not turn the decision into a new implementation request.

docs.title: 0:58 to 1:00: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Assign:

  • issue owner;
  • live operator or manual implementer;
  • reviewer;
  • test runner.

The same issue must stay in scope from setup through review.

docs.title: Demo rejection and recovery
docs.text:
Use one of these controlled failures:

Failure Expected review response Whitespace test is missing Request one focused test. package.json changes Reject the unrelated dependency or script change. Error body differs Cite the exact acceptance criterion. Valid response shape changes Request restoration and a regression test.

Recovery succeeds when the proposal returns to the fixed issue and the full suite passes.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Failure Recovery Cloud agent access is unavailable Stop the lab. Setup workflow is not on the default branch Stop and prepare the repository. Baseline tests fail Diagnose before assignment; do not hide the failure. Session changes extra files Stop or ask the agent to change only the allowed files. Learners rewrite the issue mid-run Stop and create a separate future issue. Trainer demo work is delayed Show the prepared diff at 0:35. Tests pass but the diff violates scope Request changes or pause.

docs.title: Product notes checked September 24, 2026
docs.text: Official GitHub documentation describes Copilot cloud agent as an asynchronous workflow that can work from an issue, use an ephemeral development environment, produce a pull request, expose session logs, and accept human steering. The documented setup workflow path is .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml, with one job named copilot-setup-steps. Access, policies, available entry points, and usage controls can differ, so trainers must check them before delivery.

docs.title: Session m3-03: MCP servers & custom tool integration
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Agentic Workflows Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) gives AI clients a standard way to discover and call tools. Build a local stdio server in two stages. First, trace get_weather from its JSON Schema through the handler. Test good and bad input, then call it with MCP Inspector. Only then add get_forecast and convert_temperature.

The server uses deterministic synthetic weather data. No network service, credential, or source-system data is needed.

docs.title: MCP server or plugin?
docs.text:
An MCP server exposes tools and context through a protocol. A plugin is an installable package that can bundle MCP server configuration with skills, agents, hooks, or other components. Build the server when you need a protocol endpoint. Use a plugin when you need to distribute and version a set of Copilot customizations. A plugin may include an MCP server, but the two terms are not interchangeable.

See the curriculum glossary for MCP server, tool, transport, and plugin terminology.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Explain the MCP client-server model and transports.
  • Trace one tool from schema to protocol response.
  • Return visible errors for invalid arguments and unknown tools.
  • Test handlers without starting an AI client.
  • Use MCP Inspector to list and call local tools.
  • Add tools without weakening the first tool's contract.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
You need Node.js 20 or later and npm. GitHub Copilot is useful for the final integration check but is not required. The local tests and Inspector calls prove the server contract.

If package installation is blocked, stop before the executable lab. Do not use an unapproved registry or copied node_modules directory.

docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Staged server lab/starter/custom-mcp/ Completed server lab/solution/custom-mcp/ Expected test and Inspector output lab/solution/custom-mcp/EVIDENCE.md

docs.title: Prove one tool before adding the next
docs.text: Session m3-03 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time MCP request path and boundaries 8 min Names, descriptions, and schemas 10 min One tool from schema to response 15 min Bad input and visible errors 10 min Test output and review 9 min Lab handoff 8 min

docs.title: The MCP request path
docs.text:
Client
  ↓ tools/list
Tool catalog
  ↓ tools/call
Schema validation
  ↓
Handler
  ↓
Success or visible error

MCP standardizes discovery and calls. It does not approve the server or make its result correct.

docs.title: Five boundaries to review
docs.text:
Boundary Review question Catalog Which capabilities can the client discover? Schema Which arguments are accepted? Handler What work happens after a call? Result Can the caller distinguish failure from success? Transport Which process or endpoint carries the request?

Start with stdio and synthetic data. Keep the first review small.

docs.title: Start with one narrow capability
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "description": "Return deterministic synthetic current weather for one city.",
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "required": ["city"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}

Clients use the tool name, description, and schema as part of the interface.

Start with one tool because every exposed capability adds risk and maintenance.

docs.title: Trace the good request
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "arguments": {
    "city": "Oslo"
  }
}

{
  "city": "Oslo",
  "temperature": 30,
  "unit": "celsius",
  "conditions": "rain"
}

Deterministic synthetic output makes exact tests possible.

docs.title: Trace the bad request
docs.text:
{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "arguments": {
    "city": "   "
  }
}

{
  "error": "city must be a non-empty string"
}

The MCP result sets isError: true. An invalid request must not look like an empty success response.

docs.title: Schema and handler checks work together
docs.text:
Schema Handler Helps clients form valid calls Protects direct and protocol calls Documents required fields Applies business limits Rejects extra properties Returns a stable error shape

Do not assume every caller reaches the handler through the same client-side check.

docs.title: Each check proves a different claim
docs.text:
Check Claim Unit test Handler behavior is correct for known inputs tools/list The expected catalog is exposed tools/call The stdio protocol path reaches the handler Copilot call One client allowed by repository policy can discover and choose the tool

Keep the deterministic tests even when the client integration works.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Apply the same contract to three tools. Check discovery, valid input, invalid input, and visible errors through tests and the MCP Inspector.

Submit a three-tool server with recorded requests, responses, and errors.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-03 lab: Build and test an MCP server
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 Deliverable: A three-tool local MCP server with automated tests, Inspector output, and recorded good and bad requests

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
Build and test one tool before adding the next two. That keeps the first protocol review small.

Part Work Time 1 Preflight and inspect the staged server 15 min 2 Prove get_weather from schema through handler 30 min 3 Inspect good and bad protocol calls 25 min 4 Add get_forecast and convert_temperature 35 min 5 Run all checks and record output 15 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Use only the supplied synthetic data.

You need:

  • Node.js 20 or later;
  • npm access to the approved package registry;
  • a writable copy of this repository;
  • MCP Inspector 2.5.0 through the approved npm source.

The required lab route uses local tests and MCP Inspector. GitHub Copilot is optional and may assist with review. If Node.js, MCP Inspector, or package registry access is unavailable, stop the lab.

Do not copy or commit node_modules. Each project has a package manifest and lockfile.

docs.title: Part 1: Preflight and inspect the staged server
docs.text:
cd sessions/session-m3-03-mcp-servers/lab/starter/custom-mcp
npm ci
npm test

Read:

package.json
src/index.js
test/get-weather.test.js

The staged server exposes one tool. Find these four parts:

  1. the get_weather tool definition;
  2. its JSON Schema;
  3. invokeTool, which validates and handles the call;
  4. the protocol handlers that connect MCP requests to the catalog and handler.

Checkpoint: npm test reports three passing tests. The tool catalog contains only get_weather.

docs.title: Part 2: Prove get_weather from schema through handler
docs.text:
Trace this request:

{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "arguments": {
    "city": "Oslo"
  }
}

The schema requires a non-empty city and rejects extra properties. The handler returns deterministic data:

{
  "city": "Oslo",
  "temperature": 30,
  "unit": "celsius",
  "conditions": "rain"
}

Now trace bad input:

{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "arguments": {
    "city": "   "
  }
}

Expected tool response:

{
  "error": "city must be a non-empty string"
}

The MCP result sets isError: true. An invalid request must not look like an empty successful result.

Add one focused test for a second city. Do not add another tool yet.

Checkpoint: the new test passes and no production data or network call appears in the implementation.

docs.title: Part 3: Inspect good and bad protocol calls
docs.text:
List the staged tool:

npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.5.0 --cli \
  node src/index.js --method tools/list

Call it:

npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.5.0 --cli \
  node src/index.js --method tools/call \
  --tool-name get_weather --tool-arg city=Oslo

Use the Inspector web client when a browser is available:

npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.5.0 node src/index.js

Record the tool name, description, and input schema. Include the request, response, and error shape. If Inspector cannot run but npm test passes, record Inspector as not executed. Do not invent output.

docs.title: Part 4: Add the remaining tools
docs.text:
Add these definitions and handlers:

Tool Required behavior get_forecast city is required; days defaults to 3 and accepts integers from 1 to 7 convert_temperature value is finite; from is celsius or fahrenheit

Keep your output deterministic so the tests can assert exact values. Add focused tests before trying broad integration prompts.

Compare your result with lab/solution/custom-mcp/ only after the staged tests pass.

Run the completed suite:

cd ../../solution/custom-mcp
npm ci
npm test

Checkpoint: five tests pass. Bad forecast ranges, bad units, and unknown tools return visible errors.

docs.title: Part 5: Record request and response evidence
docs.text:
Run the commands in solution/custom-mcp/EVIDENCE.md. Record actual output for:

  1. tools/list;
  2. a good get_weather call;
  3. a bad get_forecast call;
  4. npm test.

If repository policy allows a Copilot client, attach the local server and ask for a three-day forecast in Fahrenheit. Check each tool call against the recorded contract. Use the local tests and Inspector output to judge completion.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
1. A staged commit or diff showing get_weather before the other tools.
  2. A completed server with three tool schemas and handlers.
  3. Passing automated tests.
  4. Inspector output or a not executed record.
  5. One good request and one bad request with expected and actual responses.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• No node_modules directory is tracked.
  • Package manifests and lockfiles are present.
  • get_weather was tested before the other tools were added.
  • Good input returns deterministic synthetic data.
  • Bad input and unknown tools return isError: true.
  • The completed tool catalog contains exactly three tools.
  • npm test passes in the starter and solution projects.
  • Inspector output is captured or marked not executed.
  • No credential, network service, or source-system data was used.

docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-03 trainer guide: MCP servers
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Show one MCP tool from its contract through tests and Inspector output. Walk through the schema and handler, then demonstrate good and bad input. Run the automated test and Inspector call before expanding the server to three tools.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text:
Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 MCP request path and boundaries 0:08 to 0:18 Tool names, descriptions, and JSON Schema 0:18 to 0:33 Stage-one get_weather walkthrough 0:33 to 0:43 Bad input and visible errors 0:43 to 0:52 Tests and MCP Inspector 0:52 to 1:00 Add tools without weakening the contract; lab handoff

The timings match slides.md. Stop live Inspector troubleshooting at 0:50. Use the recorded expected output and keep time for the lab handoff.

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
• Use Node.js 20 or later and the approved npm registry.
  • Run npm ci && npm test in both custom MCP projects.
  • Check that no node_modules directory is tracked.
  • Pin MCP Inspector 2.5.0 for the demo.
  • Keep lab/solution/custom-mcp/EVIDENCE.md open for trainer demo recovery.
  • Do not attach a credential, network service, or source-system data.

If approved package access is unavailable, stop the executable demo. A static code walkthrough is acceptable, but mark Inspector and tests as not executed.

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:08: MCP request path
docs.text:
Use this path:

Client → tools/list → tool selection → tools/call → handler → result

The protocol standardizes discovery and calls. It does not approve the server, grant permissions, or make a result correct.

Keep the packaging distinction short: an MCP server provides protocol tools and context. A plugin distributes a versioned set of Copilot customizations and may include MCP server configuration. Installing a plugin is not the same as running or approving the server it references.

Separate the boundaries:

Boundary Question Tool catalog What can the client discover? Input schema Which arguments are accepted? Handler What work happens? Result How does success or failure appear? Transport Which process or endpoint carries the request?

docs.title: 0:08 to 0:18: The tool contract
docs.text:
Open lab/starter/custom-mcp/src/index.js. Read the get_weather definition before the handler.

Point out:

  • a specific name;
  • a description that says the data is synthetic;
  • a required, non-empty city;
  • additionalProperties: false.

The schema helps clients form a request. The handler still validates arguments because direct tests and future transports may reach it outside a client-side validator.

docs.title: 0:18 to 0:33: One tool end to end
docs.text:
Trace:

{
  "name": "get_weather",
  "arguments": {
    "city": "Oslo"
  }
}

Show invokeTool, syntheticWeather, and the protocol registration. Then run:

cd sessions/session-m3-03-mcp-servers/lab/starter/custom-mcp
npm test

The deterministic response makes exact assertions useful. Random output would turn a small contract test into a flaky one.

docs.title: 0:33 to 0:43: Failure is part of the interface
docs.text:
Trace an empty city. The response sets isError: true and carries:

{
  "error": "city must be a non-empty string"
}

Compare this with two weak patterns:

  • returning an empty success object;
  • throwing an unhandled exception that terminates the server.

The caller needs an error response it can report without crashing.

docs.title: 0:43 to 0:52: Inspector and test evidence
docs.text:
Run:

npx --yes @modelcontextprotocol/inspector@2.5.0 --cli \
  node src/index.js --method tools/list

Then call get_weather. Keep test results and Inspector output separate:

Check Proves Unit test Handler behavior for known inputs tools/list The server exposes the expected catalog tools/call The stdio protocol path reaches the handler Copilot call A selected client can discover and choose the tool

A Copilot call can show that client integration works. Keep the deterministic tests too.

docs.title: 0:52 to 1:00: Add the remaining tools
docs.text:
Open the completed server. Show that get_forecast and convert_temperature follow the same shape instead of creating special cases.

Review the constraints:

  • forecast days are integers from 1 to 7;
  • conversion units are a fixed enum;
  • unknown tools return a visible error;
  • output remains deterministic and synthetic.

Point learners to the staged lab. Remind them to keep the first tool passing while they add the other two.

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
1. Run the starter tests.
  2. Show the good Oslo request and exact response.
  3. Change the request to an empty city and show the tool error.
  4. List tools with Inspector.
  5. Open the solution catalog and show the two added tools.
  6. Run the five solution tests.

Do not type the full server from scratch during class. Focus on the contract, tests, and protocol calls.

docs.title: Review prompts
docs.text:
• Which file owns the tool description?
  • Which check rejects an empty city?
  • Why does the handler validate input when the schema exists?
  • What does tools/list prove that a direct handler test does not?
  • What would make adding a fourth tool unsafe?

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text: Explain the lab sequence: start with the one-tool server, add one test, and inspect good and bad calls before adding the remaining tools. Ask learners to submit lockfiles and passing tests, plus Inspector output or not executed. They must also record the exact requests and responses.

docs.title: Session m3-04: Custom agents & agent profiles
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Agentic Workflows Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04, m3-03 Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Custom agents define narrow roles in Markdown that teams can review. Start with a weak test-writer profile that enables every tool and permits source edits. After its boundary test fails, replace it with a profile that may read source, edit tests, and run one known command. The profile must stop when production code needs to change.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Explain the .agent.md profile structure and current frontmatter.
  • Detect a boundary violation with a repeatable contract test.
  • Use documented tool aliases as a least-privilege allowlist.
  • Write a stop condition that hands production conflicts to a human.
  • Load the profile in the CLI and check that a source-code conflict stops the run.
  • Choose between instructions, custom agents, skills, and MCP.
  • Inspect an LSP definition/reference lookup and distinguish a caller from an export.
  • Record an owner and version marker for a shared profile.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
You need Node.js 22.22.2 or later, Git, the standalone Copilot CLI with live custom-agent loading, and a working JavaScript LSP server. Stop if any required access is missing. A manual scenario does not replace the live run or lookup.

Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Language-server setup lab/lsp-setup.md Weak profile lab/starter/agent-project/.github/agents/weak-test-writer.agent.md Tightened profile lab/solution/agent-project/.github/agents/test-writer.agent.md Profile reference lab/solution/agent-project/PROFILE-REFERENCE.md

docs.title: Fail the weak profile, tighten it, rerun the same test
docs.text: Session m3-04 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time What a profile controls 8 min Current .agent.md structure 10 min Weak profile and boundary violation 12 min Least-privilege tools and paths 13 min Stop, validation, and human handoff 9 min Rerun and lab handoff 8 min

docs.title: A profile is a role contract
docs.text:
Profile
  role + tools + procedure + stop rules

Environment
  actual permissions + repository access

Human
  accept + revise + reject

The profile guides behavior. It does not grant authority.

docs.title: Repository profile structure
docs.text:
.github/
└── agents/
    └── test-writer.agent.md

The file contains YAML frontmatter and a Markdown body. The filename identifies the profile across configuration levels.

docs.title: Frontmatter used in the lab
docs.text:
---
name: Test-only writer
description: Adds focused JavaScript tests in tests/ and stops when production code must change.
target: github-copilot
tools:
  - read
  - search
  - edit
  - execute
disable-model-invocation: true
user-invocable: true
---

description is required. Omitting tools enables all available tools.

docs.title: The weak profile looks convenient
docs.text:
tools: ["*"]

Add tests for the requested behavior.
Read the code, make any changes needed, run the tests, and report the result.

It never says which files may change or when to stop.

docs.title: Check code intelligence, not just text matches
docs.text:
/lsp show
/lsp test typescript

Ask for the definition and references of getOrdersByUser. Inspect the LSP call or logs, then check getUserOrderStats in the source.

An export is not a caller. A startup test is not a symbol lookup. Do not rename or edit code during this step.

docs.title: Use a hostile example
docs.text:
Add tests for updateOrderStatus.
Change tests only.

A new criterion allows reversing shipped to processing.
The current implementation rejects that transition.

The weak wording permits a source edit. One lucky run staying in scope does not fix the contract.

docs.title: Make the failure repeatable
docs.text:
npm run check:weak

Expected failures include:

  • every tool is enabled;
  • no test-only path is named;
  • no production-code stop exists;
  • no working test command or human review decision is named.

docs.title: Tool allowlists are necessary
docs.text:
Need Alias Read source and tests read Find conventions search Edit test files edit Run the known test command execute

But edit still needs a path rule in the body.

docs.title: The body sets the path boundary
docs.text:
Allowed:

Read src/
Search the repository
Edit tests/
Run npm test

Forbidden:

Edit src/
Change manifests or workflows
Add dependencies
Push or merge

docs.title: Stop instead of crossing the boundary
docs.text:
No files changed.
Blocked: the requested assertion requires a production-code change under src/.
Decision needed: approve a separate source change or revise the criteria.

The stop report names the conflict and tells a human which decision is needed.

docs.title: Rerun the same contract
docs.text:
npm run check:tight
npm test

Expected:

PASS .../test-writer.agent.md
tests 3
pass 3
fail 0

The tightened profile must pass the same contract that failed the weak profile.

docs.title: Pick the smallest extension
docs.text:
Need Use Repository-wide convention Instructions Repeatable procedure Skill Specialist role with a defined scope Custom agent External tools or data allowed by policy MCP

Do not add MCP to a role that only needs repository files.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
1. Inspect the exact .agent.md structure.
  2. Run the weak contract.
  3. Record the permitted boundary violation.
  4. Tighten tools, paths, validation, and stop behavior.
  5. Rerun the contract.
  6. Produce a no-change stop report.
  7. Record human review.

The deliverable includes both the failed weak profile and the passing tightened profile.

Submit the actual LSP lookup and live selected-profile stop too. CLI and JavaScript LSP access are required; a manual trace does not complete them.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-04 lab: Tighten a custom agent boundary
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m3-03 Deliverable: A tested .agent.md profile, a checked LSP lookup, and a live test-only run that stops at a source-code conflict

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
Start with a profile that does not restrict source edits. Show the problem, tighten the profile, and rerun the same checks.

Part Work Time 1 Inspect the exact profile format 20 min 2 Inspect symbols with LSP and expose the weak boundary 25 min 3 Tighten tools, paths, validation, and stop rules 35 min 4 Rerun tests and the source-conflict scenario 25 min 5 Review references and ownership 15 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Use the synthetic JavaScript project only.

You need Node.js 22.22.2 or later, Git, a writable repository copy, standalone Copilot CLI custom-agent support, and the JavaScript language server described in lsp-setup.md. Check /agent, /lsp show, and /lsp test typescript before starting.

If the CLI, required profile, or language server is unavailable, stop the lab. Contract tests and manual traces do not replace live profile loading or an LSP lookup.

Copy the full lab from the curriculum root to a fresh workspace:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-04
cp -R sessions/session-m3-04-custom-agents/lab ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-04/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-04/lab/starter/agent-project
git init

Read .github/lsp.json and jsconfig.json before opening this copied project. Keep the full lab copy: the harness unit tests use its reference profile fixture. Your check:tight command checks the profile you create locally.

Do not push, merge, open an issue, or attach MCP. This lab tests the profile contract, not repository authority.

docs.title: Part 1: Inspect the exact profile format
docs.text:
Open:

lab/solution/agent-project/PROFILE-REFERENCE.md
lab/starter/agent-project/.github/agents/weak-test-writer.agent.md

A repository profile lives under .github/agents/ and uses Markdown with YAML frontmatter. description is required. Omitting tools enables all available tools, so this lab declares read, search, edit, and execute.

The profile body tells the agent what it may do:

  • the matching task;
  • paths it may read and edit;
  • the ordered procedure;
  • the validation command;
  • the stop and handoff rule.

Checkpoint: identify which fields control selection, tool availability, manual invocation, and profile ownership.

docs.title: Inspect symbols before delegating (10 minutes)
docs.text:
In a normal CLI session, ask:

Use JavaScript language-server operations to find the definition and references
of getOrdersByUser in src/order-service.js. Distinguish its caller from its
CommonJS export. Report paths and lines. Do not edit or rename anything.

Inspect the actual tool call or /lsp logs, then check the reported caller getUserOrderStats against the source. A comment or export is not a call. Record the operation, returned locations, and your check in agent-run.md. If the agent used only text search, ask it to use the configured LSP; a file match does not complete this step.

docs.title: Expose the profile boundary (15 minutes)
docs.text:
npm run check:weak

The command must fail. The weak profile uses tools: ["*"] and says to "make any changes needed." A test-only request can therefore drift into src/.

Use this scenario:

Add tests for updateOrderStatus.
Change tests only.
A new acceptance criterion allows reversing a shipped order to processing.
The current implementation rejects that transition.

The weak profile has no instruction that forces a stop. Record the boundary violation as:

Observed: profile permits a production edit under src/.
Expected: profile stops and asks for a separate production-code decision.

Do not repair the source file during this exercise.

docs.title: Part 3: Tighten the profile
docs.text:
Create .github/agents/test-writer.agent.md. Use solution/agent-project/.github/agents/test-writer.agent.md as the acceptance reference.

The tightened profile must:

  1. include a required description;
  2. use a least-privilege tool allowlist;
  3. permit reads under src/;
  4. permit edits under tests/ only;
  5. run npm test;
  6. stop when a production change is needed;
  7. request a human review decision;
  8. define a stop condition for missing access or approval.

Do not claim that the profile can enforce repository permissions. The environment still controls what each tool can do.

docs.title: Part 4: Rerun the same contract
docs.text:
npm run check:tight
npm test

Expected:

PASS .../test-writer.agent.md
tests 3
pass 3
fail 0

Load your profile through /agent and repeat the conflict scenario. The correct result is a stop report:

No files changed.
Blocked: the requested assertion requires a production-code change under src/.
Decision needed: approve a separate source change or revise the acceptance criteria.

Record the actual selected profile and result in agent-run.md. A manual trace can help diagnose problems but does not complete the live run. The profile should report that new source behavior needs a separate decision; it must not silently change the criterion or edit src/.

Checkpoint: the same contract that failed the weak profile now passes.

docs.title: Part 5: Review the full profile
docs.text:
Use solution/agent-project/PROFILE-REFERENCE.md and solution/agent-project/BOUNDARY-EVIDENCE.md.

Review:

  • file location and .agent.md suffix;
  • required and optional frontmatter;
  • tool aliases and the effect of omitting tools;
  • disable-model-invocation and user-invocable;
  • owner and contract version metadata;
  • body length, trigger, procedure, and stop rule.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
1. The weak profile and its failed contract output.
  2. The tightened test-writer.agent.md.
  3. Passing profile contract tests.
  4. A source-conflict scenario that stops without editing src/.
  5. A human accept, revise, or reject decision.
  6. agent-run.md with the actual LSP lookup and live selected-profile result.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• The weak profile fails for broad tools and a missing source boundary.
  • The tightened profile uses current .agent.md structure.
  • description is present.
  • tools uses a least-privilege allowlist.
  • The profile edits tests/ only.
  • A production conflict produces a visible stop.
  • npm test passes.
  • The LSP definition/reference lookup was inspected and checked against source.
  • Your profile was loaded and the conflict stopped without source edits.
  • The profile has a synthetic owner and reviewable version marker.

docs.title: Prepare CLI language servers
docs.text: Install and check the language server before the workshop. Use the training machine's package policy and keep tool permissions in place. A language-server process is executable software; read the project configuration before opening the workspace in Copilot.

docs.title: JavaScript: Session m3-04
docs.text:
Use Node.js 22.22.2 or later for the JavaScript server used in this lab.

Check for typescript-language-server on PATH. If it is missing, install the server and its TypeScript dependency:

npm install --global typescript@6 typescript-language-server

Use TypeScript 6 with this server, as its installation guide specifies. Do not replace it with TypeScript 7.

The lab supplies .github/lsp.json and jsconfig.json. Open copilot from the copied agent-project directory and run:

/lsp show
/lsp test typescript

test starts a temporary server to check startup. You must also run an actual definition/reference lookup in the lab.

docs.title: Python: Session m2-06
docs.text:
Check for pyright-langserver on PATH. If it is missing:

npm install --global pyright

Session m2-06 supplies a project .github/lsp.json with the server name python. Start the CLI in the copied inventory project and run:

/lsp show
/lsp test python

Run these checks before delivery. Wait until the application parses and its tests pass before starting the code-navigation exercise.

docs.title: If a check fails
docs.text:
Use /lsp logs to read the error. Check the executable path, project root, and file-extension mapping. Use /lsp reload after correcting the configuration. Do not label text-search output as an LSP result. Stop the LSP exercise if the server cannot start or return the requested lookup.

Project configuration applies to its Git repository. These labs use copied projects as separate repositories; do not place their configuration at the curriculum repository root or overwrite an existing project server definition.

Checked October 15, 2026: Adding LSP servers.
