docs.title: Session m3-04 trainer guide: Custom agent boundaries
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Make the boundary failure visible. Start with a profile that enables every tool and permits any needed change. Run the contract, show why a test-only task can drift into production code, tighten the profile, and rerun the same test.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 What a custom agent profile controls 0:08 to 0:18 Current .agent.md structure 0:18 to 0:30 Weak profile and boundary violation 0:30 to 0:43 Least-privilege tools and path rules 0:43 to 0:52 Stop, validation, and human handoff 0:52 to 1:00 Rerun checks and lab handoff

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
• Open the weak and tightened profiles side by side.
  • Run npm test from lab/starter/agent-project.
  • Keep PROFILE-REFERENCE.md and BOUNDARY-EVIDENCE.md open.
  • Check profile support in the Copilot client.
  • Prepare the JavaScript LSP server using lab/lsp-setup.md; check its startup and an actual getOrdersByUser reference lookup.
  • Stop the learner lab if live profile loading is unavailable.

Do not push, merge, open issues, or attach MCP during the core demo.

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:08: What the profile controls
docs.text:
A profile supplies instructions and filters the tools presented to the agent. It does not create repository authority.

Profile: role, available tools, procedure, stop rules
Environment: actual tool permissions and repository access
Human: accepts, revises, or rejects the result

The profile must not imply that a tool call is approved simply because the tool is listed.

docs.title: 0:08 to 0:18: Exact structure
docs.text:
Show:

.github/
└── agents/
    └── test-writer.agent.md

Read the frontmatter from PROFILE-REFERENCE.md.

Explain:

  • description is required;
  • name is optional but useful;
  • target can limit the environment;
  • omitting tools enables all available tools;
  • disable-model-invocation requires deliberate use;
  • user-invocable keeps the profile selectable;
  • metadata can record a synthetic owner and contract version.

Show where the Markdown body tells the agent what it may do and when to stop.

Use five minutes of this segment to distinguish tools from code intelligence. /lsp show reports configured servers; /lsp test typescript checks startup. Neither proves a lookup. Ask for getOrdersByUser references and inspect the LSP call or logs. Check that getUserOrderStats is a caller and the export is not. Keep this lookup read-only and separate from the test-writing role.

docs.title: 0:18 to 0:30: Weak profile
docs.text:
Open weak-test-writer.agent.md:

tools: ["*"]

Its body says to make any changes needed. Run:

npm run check:weak

Use this conflict:

Add tests for updateOrderStatus. Change tests only.
A new criterion allows reversing shipped to processing; the implementation
rejects it.

The profile has no reason to stop before editing src/. The failure is in the contract, even if one model run happens to stay inside the boundary.

docs.title: 0:30 to 0:43: Tighten tools and paths
docs.text:
Open test-writer.agent.md.

The profile uses:

tools:
  - read
  - search
  - edit
  - execute

Explain why the allowlist is not enough: edit can still affect the wrong file. Show how the body limits edits to tests/ and names forbidden paths.

Ask learners to distinguish:

Rule Where it lives Tool is available Frontmatter Only tests may change Profile body Repository blocks a write Environment or repository policy Change is accepted Human review

docs.title: 0:43 to 0:52: Stop and handoff
docs.text:
Read the production-conflict rule aloud. The correct output names:

  • no files changed;
  • the behavior that conflicts with the criteria;
  • the forbidden production path;
  • the decision a human must make.

Then show that npm test runs in the project. If the command does not run, the profile reports not run. It must not claim success instead.

docs.title: 0:52 to 1:00: Rerun
docs.text:
Run:

npm run check:tight
npm test

The same contract now passes. Load the learner's profile through CLI /agent and run the conflict scenario. Require the actual stop report and unchanged source; a manual trace does not count as live invocation.

Finish with the extension choice:

Need Use Repository-wide rule Instructions Repeatable procedure Skill Role with a defined scope Custom agent External tools or data allowed by policy MCP

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
1. Show the weak profile.
  2. Run check:weak and read the failed checks.
  3. Trace the production edit the weak wording permits.
  4. Show the tightened frontmatter and body.
  5. Run check:tight and the full tests.
  6. Produce the stop report for the same conflict.
  7. Keep the LSP operation and actual selected profile in agent-run.md.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Treating tools: ["*"] as harmless convenience.
  • Naming a role without naming paths.
  • Writing "do not edit source" without a stop and handoff result.
  • Claiming validation passed when the command did not run.
  • Assuming the profile grants permission.
  • Adding MCP to a role that does not need external data.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text: Explain the sequence: inspect the current structure, run the failing weak profile, then tighten it and rerun the contract. Learners must record a stop report with no source edits. They then review the documentation and read-only data analyst examples using the same structure. Allow ten minutes for the LSP lookup within the 25-minute weak-profile block. Keep the lab at 120 minutes.

docs.title: Session m3-05: Agent Skills and repository guidance
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Agentic Workflows Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m3-04 Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Skills capture reusable procedures owned by the repository. Build one skill under .github/skills/. Test when it should run, when it should stay out of scope, and when a missing reviewer should stop it. Then check live loading and compare the local decision-interview skill with a pinned copy of Matt Pocock's grill-me and its grilling dependency. The accepted interview decisions become inputs to /plan. Finish by reviewing scoped /chronicle improve suggestions. Use actual session corrections to decide whether a rule belongs in instructions, a skill, or neither.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Create a valid skill directory and SKILL.md.
  • Write a description that states when to use the skill and when not to use it.
  • Test matching, non-matching, and failed-precondition behavior.
  • Stop visibly when required evidence or approval is missing.
  • Run the named API scenario and inspect its result.
  • Assign an owner and review skill changes in the repository.
  • Inspect community skill dependencies and license before loading them.
  • Compare two live interviews, then trace owner decisions into an implementation plan.
  • Review repository-scoped session suggestions without applying them automatically.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
You need Node.js 22 or later and the standalone Copilot CLI with project skill loading, /plan, and /chronicle improve. Stop if required access is unavailable. The deterministic runner checks its own contract; it does not replace live skill invocation. Session m7-02 supplies reusable interview assets but is not a prerequisite.

Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Completed skill lab/solution/skills-project/.github/skills/api-design/SKILL.md Expected output lab/solution/skills-project/EXPECTED-OUTPUT.md Pinned community snapshot lab/starter/community-interview/README.md Interview comparison reference lab/solution/interview-comparison-reference.md

docs.title: Test selection, non-selection, and visible failure
docs.text: Session m3-05 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time Skill directory and loading model 8 min Required frontmatter and description 8 min Selection and visible failure 10 min Validation versus live invocation 10 min Pinned interview comparison and plan handoff 18 min Access check and lab handoff 6 min

docs.title: A skill has two jobs
docs.text:
1. Select the right task.
  2. Guide the work after selection.

A broad description can select the wrong task even when the procedure is good. The procedure also needs failure rules so it does not claim success after a required check fails.

docs.title: Repository skill structure
docs.text:
.github/
└── skills/
    └── api-design/
        └── SKILL.md

The directory uses lowercase words and hyphens. The instruction file is named exactly SKILL.md.

docs.title: Required frontmatter
docs.text:
---
name: api-design
description: Use for creating or reviewing REST routes under src/api/ when acceptance criteria, a reviewer, and a verified focused test command are available. Do not use for documentation, UI, deployment, or generated clients.
---

Match name to the directory. Use description to tell Copilot when to select the skill.

docs.title: Test the positive trigger
docs.text:
Review GET /api/tasks/:id under src/api/.
Check identifier handling and the existing not-found response.

Required context:

  • acceptance criteria;
  • named paths;
  • reviewer;
  • focused test command that runs in this project.

Expected status: applied.

docs.title: Test a non-trigger
docs.text:
Rewrite the installation section in README.md.

Expected:

{
  "status": "not_applicable",
  "skill": "api-design",
  "reason": "Task is outside REST route work under src/api/."
}

A skill should not run on tasks outside its scope.

docs.title: Matching work can still be blocked
docs.text:
Add POST /api/tasks under src/api/.
Acceptance criteria exist.
No reviewer is assigned.

The trigger matches. The precondition does not.

docs.title: Make the failure visible
docs.text:
{
  "status": "blocked",
  "skill": "api-design",
  "reason": "Missing precondition: human reviewer."
}

Do not invent a reviewer, skip the check, or return success.

docs.title: A reviewable skill body
docs.text:
Preconditions
Procedure
Validation
Failure behavior
Maintenance

Each section answers a different question. Keep the procedure short enough that a human can apply it as a checklist.

docs.title: Validate the files
docs.text:
npm run validate:skill

The validator checks:

  • SKILL.md exists;
  • frontmatter has name and description;
  • name matches the directory;
  • required sections are present.

docs.title: Test all three outcomes
docs.text:
npm test

The suite proves:

  • a route task applies the skill;
  • a documentation task does not;
  • a missing reviewer blocks;
  • valid and invalid directories are distinguishable.

docs.title: Run the two demo scenarios
docs.text:
npm run demo

The output shows:

  1. correct application to named API files;
  2. a visible missing-reviewer failure.

The local runner is a teaching harness, not a replacement skill platform.

docs.title: Local tests and live skills prove different things
docs.text:
Check What it shows Local directory validator Your file has the required structure Harness unit tests The fixed scenario contract behaves as expected /skills info and actual invocation Copilot discovered and used the skill

Live CLI access is required. Stop if a required skill cannot load.

docs.title: Inspect the pinned interview skill
docs.text:
Matt Pocock's grill-me is a community entry point that invokes grilling.

  • Check the recorded revision and SHA-256 hashes.
  • Read both files and the retained MIT license.
  • Load only the reviewed project-local copy.
  • Keep permissions and the agreed usage limit in place.

No marketplace installer or live download is needed for this lab.

docs.title: Compare the same request twice
docs.text:
Use separate fresh Interactive sessions:

Run Skill Local /decision-interview from Session m7-02 Community /grill-me with its grilling dependency

Use the same request, owner decisions, and late visibility constraint. Record actual loading and changes to the decisions.

docs.title: Interview first, plan second
docs.text:
Keep Plan mode off while decisions are unsettled.

  1. Finish the interview and review the decisions.
  2. Save the accepted brief with open questions.
  3. Start a fresh /plan session from that brief.
  4. Name two decisions that change plan steps or acceptance checks.

Do not implement or create live work items during this comparison.

docs.title: Review candidates before adaptation
docs.text:
Check:

  • source and license;
  • files and scripts;
  • dependencies and network use;
  • data flow;
  • repository fit;
  • owner and retirement condition.

Do not run an unfamiliar script just to inspect it.

docs.title: Learn from actual session friction
docs.text:
/chronicle improve

This subcommand scopes history to the current repository or working directory. Check a recommendation against an actual correction.

Choose instructions, a skill, or neither. Cancel the apply step; suggestions may start selected. Do not reindex or inspect unrelated history for this lab.

Too little history is a valid result. This uses the last five minutes of the 45-minute comparison block.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
1. Create api-design/SKILL.md.
  2. Validate the directory and frontmatter.
  3. Run the trigger scenario.
  4. Run the non-trigger scenario.
  5. Run the missing-reviewer scenario.
  6. Finish with the two-scenario demo.
  7. Check live API-skill invocation and the missing-reviewer stop.
  8. Compare both live interviews and trace decisions into /plan.
  9. Check scoped Chronicle suggestions without auto-applying them.

Submit actual outputs. The harness or prepared transcripts cannot replace live loading, either interview, or the plan handoff.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m3-05 lab: Test skills and compare live interviews
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m3-04 Deliverable: A validated repository skill, live trigger and failure results, and a local-versus-community interview comparison that feeds /plan

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
Test both parts of a skill: how its description selects work and how its procedure handles that work. Check that missing preconditions stop the run.

Part Work Time 1 Build and validate the skill directory 25 min 2 Test a matching task 15 min 3 Test a non-matching task 10 min 4 Test visible precondition failure 10 min 5 Check the local harness and live loading 15 min 6 Compare interviews, plan, and review session friction 45 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Use the synthetic repository sandbox.

You need Node.js 22 or later, a writable training workspace, and the standalone Copilot CLI from Session m2-01. Check /skills, /plan, and loading of project skills before starting. If CLI access, a required skill, or package access is unavailable, stop the lab. A local contract runner does not replace live loading. Check /chronicle improve too. Use only the synthetic training repository's history; do not run account-wide history analysis during this exercise.

Do not connect the static MCP configuration in integrated-workflow/. Do not run unreviewed community scripts.

From the curriculum root, copy the complete lab and the reused Session m7-02 inputs:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-05
cp -R sessions/session-m3-05-agent-skills-ecosystem/lab \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-05/
cp sessions/session-m7-02-interview-and-shape-work/lab/starter/vague-request.md \
  sessions/session-m7-02-interview-and-shape-work/lab/starter/late-constraint.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-05/lab/starter/
mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-05/lab/starter/skills-project/.github/skills/decision-interview
cp sessions/session-m7-02-interview-and-shape-work/lab/starter/.github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-05/lab/starter/skills-project/.github/skills/decision-interview/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m3-05/lab/starter/skills-project

Use a fresh destination if that folder exists. Keep the curriculum files unchanged.

docs.title: Part 1: Build and validate the skill directory
docs.text:
Create this exact structure:

.github/
└── skills/
    └── api-design/
        └── SKILL.md

SKILL.md must start with:

---
name: api-design
description: Use for creating or reviewing REST routes under src/api/ when acceptance criteria, a reviewer, and a verified focused test command are available. Do not use for documentation, UI, deployment, or generated clients.
---

The body must define preconditions, procedure, validation, failure behavior, and maintenance.

Run:

npm install
npm run validate:skill

The validator checks the directory name, exact SKILL.md file name, required frontmatter, and body sections.

Checkpoint: the validator passes. A mismatched directory and frontmatter name fails visibly in the automated suite.

docs.title: Part 2: Test the trigger
docs.text:
Open scenarios/trigger.json. It names a REST route under src/api/, acceptance criteria, a reviewer, and npm test.

Run all contract tests:

npm test

The matching scenario must return:

{
  "status": "applied",
  "skill": "api-design"
}

The full result also lists the allowed paths and ordered checks. The skill may not expand the task to deployment, documentation, or unrelated refactoring.

docs.title: Part 3: Test the non-trigger
docs.text:
Open scenarios/non-trigger.json. The request changes README.md.

Expected result:

{
  "status": "not_applicable",
  "skill": "api-design",
  "reason": "Task is outside REST route work under src/api/."
}

Keep the skill out of tasks beyond its scope. Do not rewrite the description to match every software task.

Checkpoint: the documentation scenario does not apply the API procedure.

docs.title: Part 4: Test a missing precondition
docs.text:
Open scenarios/failure.json. The task matches the API trigger but has no reviewer.

Expected result:

{
  "status": "blocked",
  "skill": "api-design",
  "reason": "Missing precondition: human reviewer."
}

This result shows that your failure check works. Do not replace the missing reviewer, skip the condition, or return an applied result.

docs.title: Part 5: Check the local harness and live loading
docs.text:
npm run demo

The command runs two scenarios:

  1. a matching route review that applies the skill to named files;
  2. the same class of work without a reviewer, which stops.

Compare the output with solution/skills-project/EXPECTED-OUTPUT.md.

Start copilot in the working skills-project directory. Run /skills reload and /skills info api-design. Submit the same matching and missing-reviewer prompts without changing the files. Record actual skill selection and the missing-reviewer stop. The local harness tests its own deterministic contract; these live outputs show what Copilot actually did.

If the skill does not load or does not stop correctly, fix the skill and repeat the check. Do not mark live loading as complete from the harness output.

docs.title: Part 6: Compare live interviews, then plan
Inspect and load the pinned skills
docs.text:
Read ../community-interview/README.md, both upstream SKILL.md files, and the license. The snapshot pins Matt Pocock's grill-me entry point and its grilling dependency. It is a community skill, not a Copilot built-in.

From your working skills-project:

cd ../community-interview
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
cd ../skills-project
cp -R ../community-interview/grill-me ../community-interview/grilling .github/skills/
cp ../community-interview/LICENSE .github/skills/MATT-POCOCK-LICENSE

Use shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS on macOS. Stop on a checksum mismatch. Review both files, including any delegated fact-finding, against the agreed usage limit. There are no bundled scripts or downloads to run during the lab.

In Copilot, run:

/skills reload
/skills info decision-interview
/skills info grill-me
/skills info grilling

If any skill is missing, stop and correct its project path or client support. Do not install a global copy or drop the dependency.

docs.title: Run the same interview twice
docs.text:
Attach ../vague-request.md. In a fresh Interactive session, run:

/decision-interview
Use the attached synthetic request. I am the request owner. Ask the first
dependency-ordered question round, then wait. Do not draft or implement yet.

Answer the questions as the owner. Record decisions and reasons in a copy of ../interview-comparison.md. Continue until the main scope decisions are settled. Add ../late-constraint.md and ask the skill to reopen only affected decisions.

Start another fresh Interactive session with the same request and run:

/grill-me
Use the attached synthetic request and only the supplied local inputs. I am the
request owner. Ask the first question round, then wait. Do not edit, use the
network, or implement. Stay within the agreed usage limit.

Use the same owner decisions. Add the same late constraint and record the effect. Check that Copilot actually invokes grilling through the entry point. It may request a fact-finding subagent; inspect its scope and usage if that happens. Do not require a subagent when no fact lookup is needed.

Keep Plan mode off during both interviews. The pinned upstream guidance recommends a fresh conversation without Plan mode so the interview can finish before the agent starts drafting an implementation plan.

docs.title: Turn decisions into an implementation plan
docs.text:
Save an accepted decision-brief.md with the outcome, non-goals, decisions, and remaining questions. Start a fresh planning session, attach that brief, and run:

/plan Use decision-brief.md to plan the smallest request-status change. Map each
step and acceptance check to an owner decision. Mark open questions as blockers
instead of guessing. Do not implement or create a live work item.

Name at least two decisions that changed a plan step or acceptance check. Compare the skills' actual behavior and choose which fits this task. Different phrasing or one model run does not prove a universal winner.

docs.title: Review repeated friction with /chronicle (last 5 minutes)
docs.text:
After the interviews and plan, run:

/chronicle improve

This subcommand uses history for the current repository or working directory. Inspect any suggestion before its apply step; suggestions may be selected by default. Cancel without applying changes during this comparison. Check Git status afterward. Do not run reindex, broad tips, or account-wide history searches to make a short lab produce more recommendations.

Check one suggestion against an actual correction in your training sessions. Decide whether it belongs in repository instructions, a reusable skill, or neither. Record the source correction and decision in interview-comparison.md. If there is too little indexed history or no useful recommendation, record that result. Do not invent a pattern from one run or claim a generated instruction has already improved the workflow.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
1. .github/skills/api-design/SKILL.md.
  2. Passing directory and file validation.
  3. Trigger and non-trigger results.
  4. A visible missing-precondition result.
  5. Live API-skill loading and missing-reviewer stop results.
  6. interview-comparison.md, the accepted decision brief, and /plan output.
  7. The scoped /chronicle improve result and a human decision, without applying suggestions automatically.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• The directory is lowercase and uses hyphens.
  • The file is named exactly SKILL.md.
  • name matches the directory.
  • description states when to use and when not to use the skill.
  • The trigger scenario applies the skill.
  • The documentation scenario does not apply it.
  • The missing-reviewer scenario returns blocked.
  • Invalid skill structure fails validation.
  • npm test passes.
  • The demo run shows both correct application and visible failure.
  • Copilot loaded and used the API skill in both live scenarios.
  • The community snapshot passed checksums and both dependency skills loaded.
  • Both interviews ran live in separate Interactive sessions.
  • The same request, owner decisions, and late constraint were used.
  • At least two decisions changed the resulting /plan steps or checks.
  • No implementation or live work-item creation occurred during comparison.
  • Chronicle suggestions were checked against actual corrections, or insufficient history was recorded.
  • No instruction suggestion was applied automatically.

docs.title: Session m3-05 trainer guide: Skill selection and failure
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Show how a skill selects a task and then guides the work. Demonstrate a matching task and a task that stays out of scope. Then show a matching task that stops because a precondition is missing. Have learners load skills live and compare two decision interviews before moving into /plan.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 Skill directory and loading model 0:08 to 0:16 Required frontmatter and description 0:16 to 0:26 Trigger, non-trigger, and visible failure 0:26 to 0:36 Directory validation versus live invocation 0:36 to 0:54 Pinned interview comparison and plan handoff 0:54 to 1:00 Access check and lab handoff

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
• In a scratch copy of the full lab, place the reference API skill at the learner's .github/skills/api-design path. Run npm test, npm run validate:skill, and npm run demo there.
  • Open the completed api-design/SKILL.md.
  • Keep the three JSON scenarios visible.
  • Do not connect the static MCP configuration.
  • Check CLI /skills reload, /skills info, and /plan.
  • Check the pinned community snapshot's checksums and retained MIT license.
  • Load decision-interview, grill-me, and grilling in the scratch project.
  • Agree a usage limit, including any fact-finding subagent.
  • Check /chronicle improve against this copied repository's training history.

If CLI access or a required skill is unavailable, stop the learner lab. The local harness is useful for teaching deterministic checks, but does not prove that Copilot discovered or invoked a skill.

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:08: Directory model
docs.text:
Show:

.github/
└── skills/
    └── api-design/
        └── SKILL.md

The directory name is lowercase with hyphens. The instruction file is named exactly SKILL.md. Supporting scripts or references may sit beside it when they are reviewed and necessary.

docs.title: 0:08 to 0:16: Frontmatter
docs.text:
The minimum frontmatter has name and description.

---
name: api-design
description: Use for creating or reviewing REST routes under src/api/ when acceptance criteria, a reviewer, and a verified focused test command are available. Do not use for documentation, UI, deployment, or generated clients.
---

The name matches the directory. The description does more than summarize the body: it tells Copilot when to select the skill.

docs.title: 0:16 to 0:26: Selection and visible failure
docs.text:
Compare:

Review GET /api/tasks/:id under src/api/.

with:

Rewrite the installation section in README.md.

The first task matches the work and path. The second does not. A skill that triggers for both is noisy and unsafe.

Open trigger.json and non-trigger.json. Ask learners which fields make the decision visible in the output.

docs.title: Missing precondition
docs.text:
The API skill requires:

  • named acceptance criteria;
  • a human reviewer;
  • a focused test command that runs in this project.

Open failure.json. It matches the trigger but has no reviewer. The expected result is:

{
  "status": "blocked",
  "skill": "api-design",
  "reason": "Missing precondition: human reviewer."
}

Explain why this is the correct result: the skill matched the task, checked its preconditions, and stopped.

docs.title: 0:26 to 0:36: Validate and invoke
docs.text:
Run:

npm run validate:skill
npm test
npm run demo

Separate the claims:

Check Proves Directory validator Required file, frontmatter, and sections exist Scenario tests The local harness behaves as its fixed contract specifies Two-scenario demo A reviewer can see the applied and blocked outputs Live invocation The selected product discovers and uses the skill

The local runner only handles the supplied scenarios. It is a teaching harness.

The learner validator and demo read the project-local API skill. The harness unit tests retain a fixed reference fixture. Neither claims that an LLM followed the Markdown procedure. Show actual /skills info and live invocation separately.

docs.title: 0:36 to 0:54: Live interview comparison
docs.text:
Open community-interview/README.md. The snapshot pins upstream revision 49dd158d1076134a641b33efb035946536778336 and contains unchanged, MIT-licensed grill-me and grilling files. Read both; the entry point needs the dependency.

Use the Session m7-02 synthetic request and late constraint. Compare local decision-interview with /grill-me in separate fresh Interactive sessions. Use the same owner decisions and inspect actual skill loading. Keep the interview out of Plan mode, as the pinned upstream guide recommends.

grilling may delegate fact-finding. That does not authorize a network call or broader repository access. Keep permissions and the usage limit in place.

Write a short accepted decision brief, then start /plan in a fresh session. Require two decisions that change a plan step or acceptance check. Do not implement. Question wording can vary; the comparison is not a benchmark or universal ranking.

Use the last five minutes of the comparison for /chronicle improve. This subcommand scopes history to the current repository or working directory. Inspect a recommendation against an actual learner correction, then cancel the apply step: suggestions may start selected. Decide whether the recurring rule belongs in instructions, a skill, or neither. Insufficient history is a valid result; do not reindex or query unrelated work to manufacture a pattern.

docs.title: 0:54 to 1:00: Handoff
docs.text: Show interview-comparison.md. The final record must contain actual skill invocations, owner decisions, the late constraint's effect, and the plan handoff. Stop on a missing dependency or checksum mismatch; do not download a new version during delivery.

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
1. Validate the completed directory.
  2. Run the six automated tests.
  3. Run the trigger scenario and point to the allowed paths.
  4. Run the documentation non-trigger.
  5. Run the missing-reviewer failure.
  6. Show the same outputs in EXPECTED-OUTPUT.md.
  7. Show live loading and the matching and missing-reviewer prompts.
  8. Compare a question round from each interview and trace decisions into /plan.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text:
• Missing YAML frontmatter.
  • A name that differs from the directory.
  • A description that says what the skill is but not when to use it.
  • No negative trigger.
  • Preconditions hidden inside a long procedure.
  • Returning success after a command failed or did not run.
  • Assuming popularity means a community skill has approval for use.
  • Installing only grill-me without grilling.
  • Keeping Plan mode on while the interview is still settling decisions.
  • Calling the author's second answer an independent interview run.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Keep the lab at 120 minutes. Allow 25/15/10/10/15 minutes for the API skill checks. Use the remaining 45 minutes for the live interview comparison, plan handoff, and five-minute retrospective. If the first half runs long, shorten discussion rather than the live comparison.

Require correct skill application, visible missing-reviewer failure, actual live loading, and the decision-to-plan comparison. A manual checklist or copied model transcript does not complete the session.

docs.text:

Module: DevOps & Infrastructure with Copilot Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
You will use one Node.js application for four workflow tasks: create CI, design a staged deployment, repair broken workflow files, and validate a local JavaScript action. Every task uses copilot-webapp, so you can trace each decision back to the same scripts, tests, build output, and health endpoint.

Submit your workflow files. At each checkpoint, record the command and result, which file changed, and the review decision.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Generate CI from repository facts and check it with local commands.
  • Design staging and production jobs without performing a live deployment.
  • Repair workflow syntax and behavior from exact failures.
  • Validate a JavaScript action against the application with pass and fail cases.
  • Review triggers, permissions, secrets, artifacts, and deployment gates.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
You need Node.js 20 or later and GitHub Copilot in the selected coding environment. Repository and GitHub Actions access are optional. Complete the lab with local tests, YAML parsing, and peer review.

Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Application starter lab/starter/webapp/ Reference workflows and action lab/solution/

docs.title: DevOps & infrastructure | Intermediate
docs.text: Session m4-01 | 3 hours

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Time Topic 0:00 to 0:08 Baseline and Actions model 0:08 to 0:18 Generate CI 0:18 to 0:28 Design deployment 0:28 to 0:40 Repair workflow failures 0:40 to 0:52 Validate a JavaScript action 0:52 to 1:00 Review and lab handoff

docs.title: Start with repository facts
docs.text:
copilot-webapp already defines the contract:

npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
test -f dist/app.js

The workflow should call these commands. It should not invent another build, artifact path, or runtime.

docs.title: A workflow is code with an execution boundary
docs.text: Review Question Trigger Who can cause this code to run? Runner Which tools and trust boundary apply? Permissions What can the token read or change? Commands Do they exist in the repository? Artifacts Which files leave the job? Environment Which approval gate applies?

docs.title: Generate CI from the application
docs.text:
Read package.json, tests, and scripts/build.js. Create ci.yml for pull requests
and pushes to main. Use Node.js 20, npm ci, existing lint, test, and build scripts,
npm caching, contents: read, and a seven-day dist artifact.

Then check both YAML syntax and application behavior:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' ci.yml
npm test && npm run lint && npm run build

docs.title: Deployment stays a design exercise
docs.text:
The same application moves through:

build → staging → production

The workflow references environments and secrets. Production reviewers are configured in repository settings. Placeholder commands must not imply that a deployment ran.

docs.title: Syntax and behavior fail differently
docs.text:
broken-ci.yml does not parse.

broken-deploy.yml parses but contains a stale runner, a bad Git ref, a wrong secret name, and no checkout.

Ask for the failed-step output before the repair.

docs.title: A repair is a claim plus proof
docs.text:
Observation: the parser fails near Setup Node.js.
Change: align the step indentation.
Proof: parse the file again.

For behavior faults, cite the deployment specification or repository facts.

docs.title: Validate both action outcomes
docs.text:
env INPUT_THRESHOLD=0 ... node src/main.js
env INPUT_THRESHOLD=101 ... node src/main.js

The first run must pass and write a summary. The second must exit with code 1.

One successful run does not show that the action enforces the threshold.

docs.title: Access and checks
docs.text:
GitHub Copilot access is required. Repository access and Actions are optional.

For each case, inspect:

  • command or review;
  • result;
  • changed files;
  • the next action.

docs.text: Create CI, design deployment, repair failures, and validate the action against copilot-webapp.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m4-01 lab: One application, four workflow tasks
docs.text: Duration: 2 hours Difficulty: Intermediate Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 Deliverable: Reviewed workflows, command output, and review notes for copilot-webapp

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will use the same application for every part of the lab.

Part Work Time 1 Prove the application baseline and create CI 30 min 2 Design staged deployment jobs 25 min 3 Repair two supplied workflow failures 30 min 4 Validate a JavaScript action 25 min 5 Collect command results and review notes 10 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. You must have GitHub Copilot access in the selected coding environment and Node.js 20 or later.

GitHub repository access is optional. Do not push, run Actions, install an external action, or use a deployment target unless the instructor confirms that route. When repository access or Actions is unavailable, complete all the work locally as described below. If GitHub Copilot access is unavailable, stop and do not continue the lab.

Do not use real credentials or deployment endpoints. The supplied deployment work is a reviewed design exercise.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Run all commands from this session directory unless a command changes directory.

node --version
cd lab/starter/webapp
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
test -f dist/app.js
cd ../../..

Expected result: Node reports version 20 or later, seven tests pass, lint succeeds, the build succeeds, and dist/app.js exists.

Create lab/evidence.md from this table:

Checkpoint Command or review Result Changed files Reviewer Baseline CI Deployment design Workflow repair Custom action

docs.title: Part 1: Create CI
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to read lab/starter/webapp/package.json, the tests, and the build script. Create lab/starter/webapp/.github/workflows/ci.yml with:

  • pushes to main and pull requests;
  • ubuntu-latest and Node.js 20;
  • npm ci, lint, tests, and build;
  • npm caching;
  • permissions: contents: read;
  • the dist/ build artifact with seven-day retention.

Validate the application again:

cd lab/starter/webapp
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
test -f dist/app.js
cd ../../..

Validate the workflow syntax:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/starter/webapp/.github/workflows/ci.yml

Review the generated commands against package.json. Compare the result with lab/solution/webapp/.github/workflows/ci.yml.

Checkpoint: Record both command results and explain why the workflow uploads dist/ rather than a path invented by the assistant.

docs.title: Part 2: Design deployment
docs.text:
Read lab/starter/deployment-spec.md. Create lab/starter/webapp/.github/workflows/cd.yml. It must build the same application, deploy to staging before production, reference GitHub Environments and secrets, run two health checks, and describe rollback without calling a real endpoint.

Run:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/starter/webapp/.github/workflows/cd.yml
grep -nE 'environment: (staging|production)|needs:|permissions:' \
  lab/starter/webapp/.github/workflows/cd.yml

Expected result: YAML parsing succeeds. The output shows both environments, job ordering, and a permissions block.

Compare your design with lab/solution/workflows/cd.yml. Production reviewers are configured in repository settings. The workflow only references the production environment.

Checkpoint: Record the secret names, the production gate, the health-check behavior, and the rollback steps. Do not claim that a deployment occurred.

docs.title: Part 3: Repair workflow failures
docs.text:
The two broken workflows both target copilot-webapp.

First, run the parser to see the CI file's syntax failure:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/starter/broken-workflows/broken-ci.yml

Expected failure: the parser reports an indentation error near Setup Node.js. Fix the indentation, update the checkout action, add least-privilege permissions, and use the package command intended for CI. Run the parser again and compare with lab/solution/fixed-workflows/fixed-ci.yml.

The deployment workflow parses, but its behavior is wrong:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/starter/broken-workflows/broken-deploy.yml
grep -nE 'ubuntu-18.04|refs/head/main|DEPLOY_KEY|checkout' \
  lab/starter/broken-workflows/broken-deploy.yml

Expected result: parsing succeeds. The second command exposes the stale runner, bad ref, wrong secret name, and missing checkout step. Repair those items, parse the file again, and compare with the solution.

Checkpoint: For each change, cite the observed failure or repository fact. Do not accept a broad rewrite unless each change addresses a recorded failure.

docs.title: Part 4: Validate the custom action
docs.text:
Complete the metadata and implementation in lab/starter/custom-action/. The action scans the same application used by the workflows.

Use the reference implementation to check both pass and fail outcomes:

npm ci --prefix lab/solution/custom-action
cd lab/starter/webapp
env INPUT_THRESHOLD=0 'INPUT_REPORT-FORMAT=markdown' \
  GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/session-m4-01-summary.md \
  node ../../solution/custom-action/src/main.js
test -s /tmp/session-m4-01-summary.md
cd ../../..

Expected result: the action reports passed: true, exits with code 0, and writes the summary.

Now run the intentional failure:

cd lab/starter/webapp
env INPUT_THRESHOLD=101 'INPUT_REPORT-FORMAT=json' \
  node ../../solution/custom-action/src/main.js
cd ../../..

Expected failure: the action reports a score below 101 and exits with code 1. This proves that the threshold changes the job result.

If act is already installed and local runner use is approved, you may also run:

act -W lab/solution/custom-action/.github/workflows/quality-check.yml -j quality-check

Checkpoint: Record the pass and fail exit codes, score, scanned path, outputs, and summary location.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. CI and deployment workflow files for copilot-webapp.
  2. Both repaired workflow files with explanations tied to the recorded failures.
  3. The completed JavaScript action.
  4. lab/evidence.md with commands, results, changed files, and reviewer decisions.

Keep credentials and real deployment endpoints out of your deliverable. Do not claim that local syntax checks prove a production deployment is safe.

docs.text: Use copilot-webapp from start to finish. First, show that the application works locally. Then demonstrate CI creation and deployment design, followed by workflow repairs and JavaScript action validation against the same codebase.

docs.text:
Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 Application baseline and Actions model 0:08 to 0:18 Generate CI from repository facts 0:18 to 0:28 Design staging and production jobs 0:28 to 0:40 Diagnose workflow failures 0:40 to 0:52 Validate a JavaScript action 0:52 to 1:00 Security review and lab handoff

The timings match slides.md. Stop a live tool response at the end of its segment and use the prepared solution.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Run the application tests, lint, and build before delivery.
  • Keep the supplied broken workflows unchanged for the investigation.
  • Install the solution action dependencies.
  • Prepare one passing threshold and the intentional threshold-101 failure.
  • Do not configure a live deployment target.

docs.title: 0:00 to 0:08: Baseline and model
docs.text:
Run:

cd lab/starter/webapp
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
test -f dist/app.js

Tie each workflow step to a repository fact. npm test, npm run lint, and npm run build exist because package.json defines them. dist/ is valid because the build command creates it.

docs.title: 0:08 to 0:18: Generate CI
docs.text:
Use this request with a fixed scope:

Read package.json, tests, and scripts/build.js in copilot-webapp. Create ci.yml
for pull requests and pushes to main. Use Node.js 20, npm ci, the existing lint,
test, and build scripts, npm caching, contents: read, and a seven-day dist artifact.
Do not add dependencies or deployment steps.

Parse the YAML, then rerun the local application checks. A valid workflow can still call a missing script or upload a path that never exists.

docs.title: 0:18 to 0:28: Deployment design
docs.text:
Open lab/starter/deployment-spec.md. Ask learners to find the required trigger, environments, secret names, health checks, and rollback rule before generating YAML.

Review the design without deploying it. Repository settings enforce production reviewers, and the supplied endpoints are placeholders. No live deployment occurs.

docs.title: 0:28 to 0:40: Diagnose failures
docs.text:
Run the YAML parser against broken-ci.yml and let the parser reveal the first fault. After learners repair it, inspect action versions, permissions, and package commands.

For broken-deploy.yml, parsing succeeds. Use the grep command from the lab to separate syntax from behavior. Each repair needs a source: platform support, the deployment specification, the Git ref format, or the application checkout requirement.

docs.title: 0:40 to 0:52: Validate the action
docs.text:
Explain why custom action validation needs two outcomes. A passing run proves the action can scan the application and emit outputs. The threshold-101 run proves the action can fail the job.

Run the exact commands in the lab. Show the generated step summary and exit code. Do not use a repository workflow run as the only proof.

docs.title: 0:52 to 1:00: Review and handoff
docs.text:
Review:

  • triggers and token permissions;
  • approved action references;
  • secret references and environment gates;
  • artifact contents and retention;
  • the local command output that supports each claim.

Point learners to lab/evidence.md. Ask them to check that their workflow files and action agree with the command results and reviewer decisions before submitting.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text: GitHub Copilot access is required. Stop if it is unavailable. Repository access, Actions, and act are optional. Learners must complete the local work, which uses no credentials or deployment target.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Valid YAML only proves that the file parses. Run the application commands and review what the workflow does.

Use one application throughout. Learners can use the same repository facts for each decision instead of reconstructing a new project for every exercise.

Test an action failure too. A custom action that always exits successfully has not shown that it enforces the threshold.

docs.title: Session m4-02: Infrastructure as code with Copilot
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: DevOps & Infrastructure with Copilot Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02, m4-01 Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes (1 hour trainer content + 1 hour 30 minutes lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
You will use Terraform to build and review one modular infrastructure project. Connect the network, compute, and database modules, then validate each stage. Finally, repair a supplied configuration that fails the local security gate.

Bicep is a trainer comparison and optional extension. It is not part of the required learner deliverable.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Generate Terraform modules from fixed architecture constraints.
  • Connect module inputs and outputs without copying values between layers.
  • Run formatting, initialization, validation, and a local security gate in order.
  • Explain what local validation proves and what still needs a reviewed plan.
  • Review the equivalent Bicep structure without requiring a second implementation.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
You need GitHub Copilot, Terraform 1.5 or later, and network access to the approved Terraform provider source. No cloud account or credentials are required. Stop if the approved provider source is unavailable.

Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Terraform starter lab/starter/terraform/ Terraform solution lab/solution/terraform/ Optional Bicep extension lab/starter/bicep/

docs.title: Terraform from modules to security gate
DevOps & infrastructure | Advanced
docs.text: Session m4-02 | 2 hours 30 minutes

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Time Topic 0:00 to 0:08 Architecture and project model 0:08 to 0:20 Module contracts 0:20 to 0:32 Root composition 0:32 to 0:44 Staged validation 0:44 to 0:54 Security failure 0:54 to 1:00 Bicep comparison and lab handoff

docs.title: One required path
docs.text:
The learner path is Terraform:

architecture → modules → root composition → format → init → validate → security gate

Bicep appears as a prepared comparison. Learners do not build both projects.

docs.title: Modules define contracts
docs.text:
Module Consumes Exposes Network CIDR and names VPC and subnet IDs Compute VPC and subnet IDs Load balancer DNS and app security group Database Private subnets and app security group Database endpoint

Keep secrets in sensitive inputs. Do not copy values between layers.

docs.title: Prompt from fixed constraints
docs.text:
Complete the network, compute, and database module contracts. Pass values through
typed variables and outputs. Keep the database password sensitive. Do not add
credentials, a backend, plan, or apply command.

Use the architecture to set the boundaries before Copilot drafts the files.

docs.title: Validate in stages
docs.text:
terraform fmt -check -recursive
terraform init -backend=false
terraform validate

Fix the first failure before moving on. Each stage answers a different question.

docs.title: What local validation does not prove
docs.text:
It does not check:

  • the current cloud state;
  • organization policy;
  • quota or regional availability;
  • the effect of an apply.

A reviewed plan needs an approved identity and target environment.

docs.title: One intentional security failure
docs.text:
bash lab/starter/check-security.sh lab/starter/insecure-iac/main.tf

The gate must fail. Inspect the cited lines, repair the file, and check that the rerun passes.

docs.title: Bicep is a comparison
docs.text:
Show:

  • module inputs and outputs;
  • @secure() parameters;
  • az bicep build;
  • the same human review boundary.

Six minutes. No second required build.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Complete Terraform, validate each stage, and repair the security-gate failure.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m4-02 lab: Terraform from modules to security gate
docs.text: Duration: 1 hour 30 minutes Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 and m4-01 Deliverable: Validated Terraform modules, a repaired security case, and command output

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will connect Terraform modules, validate the project locally, and repair an intentional security failure.

Part Work Time 1 Inspect and format the Terraform project 10 min 2 Build and connect the modules 35 min 3 Initialize and validate 15 min 4 Investigate the intentional security failure 20 min 5 Record command output and review limits 10 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. You must have GitHub Copilot access, Terraform 1.5 or later, and the approved provider source. This lab does not need a cloud account, credentials, state backend, plan, or apply.

If GitHub Copilot access or the approved provider source is unavailable, stop and do not continue the required lab. The instructor may still show the prepared files.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Run:

terraform version
terraform fmt -check -recursive lab/starter/terraform

Expected result: Terraform reports version 1.5 or later and the supplied files are formatted.

docs.title: Part 1: Read the module contract
docs.text:
Open lab/starter/terraform/. Keep the supplied architecture:

  • VPC 10.0.0.0/16;
  • two public, two private application, and two private database subnets;
  • an internet-facing load balancer;
  • private application instances;
  • an encrypted, private PostgreSQL database;
  • database ingress only from the application security group.

Do not add credentials, a remote backend, a plan, or an apply command.

Checkpoint: List the root inputs and the outputs that connect network to compute and compute to database.

docs.title: Part 2: Build and connect the modules
docs.text:
Create the missing module files under:

modules/network/
modules/compute/
modules/database/

Use typed variables and narrow outputs. Keep the database password sensitive. Compare with lab/solution/terraform/ only after your first draft.

Run the formatting stage:

terraform fmt -check -recursive lab/starter/terraform

Expected result: the supplied files pass. If your generated files fail, run terraform fmt -recursive lab/starter/terraform, then rerun the check.

Checkpoint: Record the format result and any files Terraform changed.

docs.title: Part 3: Initialize and validate
docs.text:
Run these stages in order:

terraform -chdir=lab/starter/terraform init -backend=false
terraform -chdir=lab/starter/terraform validate

Expected result: initialization downloads the approved provider and validation reports Success! The configuration is valid.

If validation fails, fix the first reported module contract error before running it again. Do not add provider credentials to make validation pass.

Checkpoint: Record the provider version, validation result, and any contract error you repaired.

docs.title: Part 4: Investigate the intentional security failure
docs.text:
Run the local policy gate against the supplied insecure file:

bash lab/starter/check-security.sh lab/starter/insecure-iac/main.tf

Expected failure: the command exits with code 1 and reports prohibited public access, a hardcoded password, wildcard IAM access, missing database encryption, or missing load-balancer logging.

Inspect the file before opening the solution. Use the stated architecture to decide which reported findings to repair, then run:

bash lab/starter/check-security.sh lab/solution/secure-iac/main.tf
terraform fmt -check lab/solution/secure-iac/main.tf
terraform -chdir=lab/solution/secure-iac init -backend=false
terraform -chdir=lab/solution/secure-iac validate

Expected result: the security gate and Terraform validation pass.

Checkpoint: Record the failing exit code, each cited line, the repaired file, and the passing rerun. Passing this gate does not give you approval to deploy.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. The completed Terraform root module and three modules.
  2. Clean formatting and validation output.
  3. Output from the failing security check and passing rerun after repair.
  4. A short review note that states what requires a plan, cloud policy review, and human approval before deployment.

docs.title: Optional extension: Bicep comparison
docs.text:
The trainer may show lab/solution/bicep/. If time remains and Azure CLI with Bicep is already approved, build the prepared template:

az bicep build --file lab/solution/bicep/main.bicep

Compare module inputs, outputs, secure parameters, and local compilation with the Terraform project. Do not make Bicep a second required implementation.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m4-02 trainer guide: Terraform as the required path
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Demonstrate one complete IaC workflow. Show how to build and connect Terraform modules, validate them locally, and investigate a security-gate failure. Keep Bicep as a short trainer comparison or optional extension.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 Architecture and Terraform project model 0:08 to 0:20 Module contracts 0:20 to 0:32 Root composition 0:32 to 0:44 Staged validation 0:44 to 0:54 Intentional security failure 0:54 to 1:00 Bicep comparison and lab handoff

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Run terraform fmt -check -recursive on the solution.
  • Initialize the solution with -backend=false and run terraform validate.
  • Run the security gate once against the insecure file and once against the fix.
  • Keep cloud credentials unset.
  • Prepare the Bicep solution for a six-minute comparison. Do not assign it as required learner work.

docs.title: Architecture and module contracts
docs.text:
Use the supplied three-tier design. Trace address space and subnets through the network module. Show how compute uses subnet IDs and exposes the application security group, then how database uses that group and its private subnets.

Ask learners to state each boundary before generating code. A module is useful when its callers depend on a small, stable interface.

docs.title: Root composition
docs.text:
Use this request:

Read the Terraform root module and architecture constraints. Complete the network,
compute, and database module contracts. Pass values through typed variables and
outputs. Keep the database password sensitive. Do not add credentials, a backend,
plan, or apply command.

Inspect every added input and output. Reject duplicated CIDRs or values copied between modules when an output should carry them.

docs.title: Staged validation
docs.text:
Run checks in this order:

terraform fmt -check -recursive
terraform init -backend=false
terraform validate

Formatting catches style drift. Initialization resolves providers and modules. Validation checks the configuration against the installed provider schema. None of these commands compares the configuration with a cloud environment.

Do not run a plan during the required session. A plan needs an approved identity, target environment, backend decision, and review boundary.

docs.title: Intentional security failure
docs.text:
Run:

bash lab/starter/check-security.sh lab/starter/insecure-iac/main.tf

Let learners inspect the output before showing the solution. The gate should fail. Each repair must connect a reported pattern to the architecture or security rule.

Then show the passing command against lab/solution/secure-iac/main.tf.

docs.title: Bicep comparison
docs.text: Use the final six minutes to show the prepared Bicep module calls, @secure() parameter, and outputs. The comparison helps learners transfer the design ideas. It does not create another required lab.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text: GitHub Copilot, Terraform, and the approved provider source are required. Stop if any is unavailable. No cloud account or credentials are needed.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text: Give learners 90 minutes to complete the Terraform modules, run staged checks, and investigate the security failure. Ask them to submit command output. Explain that the session lasts 2 hours 30 minutes because learners no longer need to build the Bicep project as well.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Do not run a plan. The required exercise has no approved cloud target or identity. Local validation is enough for the learning goal.

Keep Bicep as a comparison. It shows that the module and validation ideas transfer without doubling the required implementation.

Keep policy tooling separate. The security script is a deterministic training gate for the supplied failure. It does not replace policy tooling.

Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: DevOps & Infrastructure with Copilot Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 and m4-01 Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
You will debug CI/CD failures using workflow files, failed-step output, and local checks. Record an observation and hypothesis before opening a reference fix. One case has a second failure that appears only after the first repair.

The security exercise uses a deliberately vulnerable training app. Review the smallest patch through a route you have approval to use, or work locally.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Separate observations, hypotheses, repairs, and proof.
  • Reproduce relevant pipeline commands locally.
  • Handle a second-stage failure without stacking speculative fixes.
  • Review a security patch for scope and focused protection.
  • Keep remediation behind human approval.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
You need GitHub Copilot and Node.js 20.x. Repository Actions, code scanning, and remote remediation are optional. Complete the lab with the supplied files and local commands.

Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Pipeline application lab/starter/pipeline-app/ Failure cases lab/starter/failing-pipelines/ Reference fixes lab/solution/fixed-pipelines/

docs.text:
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
test -f dist/index.js

If these commands pass locally, the workflow may still use the wrong runtime, directory, environment, or job order.

Read this workflow and failed-step output. Separate observations from hypotheses.
Use the local command as additional evidence. Propose the smallest repair and one
proof command. Do not change unrelated jobs.

Check every claim against the files.

docs.title: Do not reveal the answer early
docs.text:
1. Read the failed step.
  2. Record the exact log output.
  3. Reproduce the relevant command.
  4. State one hypothesis.
  5. Repair one cause.
  6. Prove the rerun.
  7. Open the reference fix.

docs.title: One failure can hide another
docs.text:
first failed stage
        ↓ repair
next workflow run
        ↓
new failed stage

Use the new log to diagnose the next failure. Keep the repair you already checked and avoid speculative changes.

docs.title: Security findings need path evidence
docs.text:
For each finding, identify:

  • input source;
  • dangerous sink;
  • expected protection;
  • focused proof;
  • approval decision.

An absence of scanner findings is not enough.

Actions, code scanning, and remote remediation are optional. The local path uses the supplied application, logs, workflows, and syntax checks.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m4-03 lab: Evidence-led pipeline debugging
docs.text: Duration: 2 hours Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-02 and m4-01 Deliverable: Three investigation records, fixed workflows, and a reviewed security patch

docs.title: Lab overview
docs.text:
You will investigate three pipeline failures, review a security repair, and improve feedback speed without removing checks.

Part Work Time 1 Prove the local application baseline 10 min 2 Investigate three pipeline cases 50 min 3 Review a security remediation 30 min 4 Improve feedback speed 20 min 5 Collect investigation records 10 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. You must have GitHub Copilot access and Node.js 20.x. Use only the supplied application, logs, and workflow files.

Remote workflow runs and security products are optional. Use them only when the instructor confirms access and policy. You must complete the local work. If GitHub Copilot access is unavailable, stop.

Do not open lab/solution/fixed-pipelines/ until a checkpoint tells you to compare. For Case 3, do not open error-log-3-stage-2.txt until the first repair is complete.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Run all commands from this session directory unless a command changes directory.

Check that the application works before you inspect the pipeline:

cd lab/starter/pipeline-app
npm ci
npm test
npm run lint
npm run build
test -f dist/index.js
cd ../../..

Expected result: install, tests, lint, and build pass.

Create one investigation record per case:

Field Record Failed job and step Exact observation Local proof command Hypothesis Smallest repair Proof after repair

docs.title: Part 1: Investigate the pipeline cases
docs.text:
For every case:

  1. Read the workflow and failed-step output.
  2. Record observations without naming a root cause.
  3. Run the local proof command.
  4. State one hypothesis.
  5. Ask Copilot to challenge the hypothesis and propose the smallest repair.
  6. Validate the repaired YAML.
  7. Compare with the solution only after the checkpoint.

Use this prompt:

Read this workflow and failed-step output. Separate observations from hypotheses.
Use the supplied local command as additional evidence. Propose the smallest repair
and one proof command. Do not change unrelated jobs.

docs.title: Case 1
docs.text:
Open pipeline-1.yml and error-log-1.txt.

Run:

node --version
cd lab/starter/pipeline-app
npm pkg get engines.node
npm test
cd ../../..

Record what the log and package metadata say. Edit only after your hypothesis explains both.

After the repair:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/starter/failing-pipelines/pipeline-1.yml

Checkpoint: Record the proof, then compare with lab/solution/fixed-pipelines/pipeline-1.yml.

docs.title: Case 2
docs.text:
Open pipeline-2.yml and error-log-2.txt.

Run the failing command from the workflow location:

npm ci

Expected failure: npm cannot find the project package metadata in the session root. Now check the same command in the application directory:

npm --prefix lab/starter/pipeline-app ci
npm --prefix lab/starter/pipeline-app test

After the repair, parse the YAML and compare with the solution.

Checkpoint: The repair must explain why changing dependency resolution would not address the observed path failure.

docs.title: Case 3: multi-stage failure
docs.text:
Open pipeline-3.yml and error-log-3.txt. Investigate only the first failed stage.

Run:

cd lab/starter/pipeline-app
npm pkg get engines.node
npm ci
npm test
cd ../../..

Repair the first failure and parse the workflow. Then open error-log-3-stage-2.txt. The second log represents the next run after the first repair.

Use the new log. Do not restore the first change or add unrelated fixes. After the second repair, run:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/starter/failing-pipelines/pipeline-3.yml
npm --prefix lab/starter/pipeline-app run build
test -f lab/starter/pipeline-app/dist/index.js

Checkpoint: Record two observations, two repairs, and separate proof for each stage. Then compare with lab/solution/fixed-pipelines/pipeline-3.yml.

docs.title: Part 2: Review a security remediation
docs.text:
Open lab/starter/vulnerable-app/src/app.js. Check its syntax locally:

node --check lab/starter/vulnerable-app/src/app.js

Complete the CodeQL workflow template. If an approved remote scan is available, inspect its findings. Otherwise use the supplied source as the finding context.

Investigate these sinks without opening the secure solution:

  • SQL query construction;
  • HTML response construction;
  • file path resolution.

Ask for one repair at a time. Review the diff, then compare with lab/solution/secure-app/src/app.js. Run the focused checks:

node --check lab/solution/secure-app/src/app.js
npm ci --prefix lab/solution/secure-app
npm test --prefix lab/solution/secure-app

Explain how each repair protects its code path: parameterized queries for SQL, output encoding for HTML, and resolved-path containment for file access. The three tests must pass. Do not rely only on an absence of scanner findings.

docs.title: Part 3: Improve feedback speed
docs.text:
Review lab/starter/slow-pipeline/workflow.yml. Preserve its checks while adding lockfile caching, parallel lint and test jobs, shallow checkout, and a main-push deployment condition.

Validate:

ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Psych.parse_stream(File.read(ARGV[0]))' \
  lab/solution/optimized-pipeline/workflow.yml
grep -nE "cache: 'npm'|needs: \\[lint, test\\]|fetch-depth: 1|github.event_name" \
  lab/solution/optimized-pipeline/workflow.yml

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. Three fixed workflows.
  2. Three investigation records, with two stages for Case 3.
  3. A reviewed security patch and local syntax-check output.
  4. The optimized workflow review.

Write the root-cause statement after the observation and local proof. Keep the original logs unchanged with the investigation records.

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Demonstrate a repeatable debugging sequence. Observe and reproduce the failure before forming a hypothesis. Make the repair, then run the check that proves it worked. Keep the reference answer hidden until learners record their investigation. Case 3 adds a second failure after the first repair.

docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 Observation, hypothesis, and proof 0:08 to 0:18 Local application baseline 0:18 to 0:34 Prepared pipeline investigation 0:34 to 0:44 Multi-stage failure 0:44 to 0:54 Security remediation review 0:54 to 1:00 Lab handoff

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
• Run the pipeline application tests, lint, and build.
  • Keep the solution directory closed during the first investigation.
  • Hold error-log-3-stage-2.txt until the first Case 3 repair.
  • Prepare the vulnerable and secure source side by side.
  • Do not depend on a remote workflow run or security product.

docs.title: Debugging sequence
docs.text:
Use this record:

Observation:
Local proof:
Hypothesis:
Smallest repair:
Proof after repair:

An observation quotes a file, command, or log. A hypothesis explains those facts. Do not let learners write the root cause before they have checked the files and logs.

docs.title: Prepared investigation
docs.text:
Start with Case 2 because the tempting dependency fix is wrong. Show the failed npm ci step and workflow. Run npm ci from the session root, then run the same operation with --prefix lab/starter/pipeline-app.

Pause for learner hypotheses. Reveal the reference fix only after the room explains why the project location matters.

docs.title: Multi-stage failure
docs.text:
For Case 3:

  1. Show error-log-3.txt.
  2. Record the first observation and local package metadata.
  3. Apply only the first repair.
  4. Announce that the next run reached another stage.
  5. Reveal error-log-3-stage-2.txt.
  6. Repeat the investigation sequence.
  7. Compare with the solution after both proofs pass.

The first failure can hide another fault. Use the new log to update the diagnosis. Keep each repair focused on the observed failure.

docs.title: Security review
docs.text:
Open one vulnerable route at a time. Ask learners to identify the source, sink, and expected protection before showing the secure file.

At minimum, run the local syntax checks. If an approved scan is available, include its findings. A clean scan alone does not prove that the repair preserves behavior or covers the intended path.

docs.title: Access policy
docs.text: GitHub Copilot and Node.js 20.x are required. Stop if either is unavailable. Actions, code scanning, and remote remediation are optional. Use the supplied files and local commands when those tools are unavailable.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text: Tell learners to keep solutions closed until each checkpoint. Case 3 requires two investigation records in sequence. Ask them to submit their investigation records and fixed files.

docs.title: Facilitator answer key
docs.text:
Reveal this section only after the matching investigation:

  • Case 1 uses a runtime below the application's declared engine.
  • Case 2 runs npm from the wrong directory.
  • Case 3 first includes an unsupported runtime, then reaches a build job that runs outside the application directory.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Can Copilot name the cause first? Ask it to separate observations from hypotheses. Learners still need local proof before changing the workflow.

Why keep the second log hidden? The first failed job prevents the later stage from running. Showing both logs early gives away the sequence.

Accept a different repair when it explains the observed output and keeps the change small. It must pass the same checks.

docs.title: Session m5-01: Brady's Squad: Human-led AI teams
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Specification-Driven Frameworks

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m3-02 to m3-05 Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content, 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Use Brady's Squad to assign roles, route work, and keep a shared decision record. In this elective, you carry one input-validation issue from assignment through tests and lead review.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Define a coordinator, specialized roles, and clear charters.
  • Design shared decision records and role-specific history.
  • Route independent work without overlapping ownership.
  • Use GitHub Issues as reviewable work contracts.
  • Decide when orchestration is worth its cost.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Learners need Node.js 20 or later, Git, a GitHub training repository, GitHub Copilot, and Squad. If a requirement is unavailable, stop and resolve it before the lab.

docs.title: Deliverable
docs.text: Submit one review packet for the input-validation issue. Include the assignment, implementation within the issue scope, test results, lead decision, and decision record. The reference solution includes both a .squad/ result and a tabletop equivalent.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/ Lab lab/ Starter files lab/starter/ Reference solution lab/solution/

docs.title: Module 5: Specification-driven frameworks | Advanced
docs.text:
Session m5-01 | 3 hours | Optional

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m3-02 to m3-05

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time Coordination trade-offs 7 min Roles, routing, and memory 20 min Issues and monitored work 8 min Prepared team demonstration 12 min Decision framework and lab handoff 13 min Lab 2 hours

docs.title: Coordination has a cost
docs.text:
Use a team when work has separate owners, clear interfaces, and a decision record to share. An individual agent is better for a small, well-understood change.

More agents create more state, review work, and cost.

docs.title: Parallelism only helps with real independence
docs.text:
Work can run in parallel when each stream has its own inputs, a clear output, and no hidden dependency on another stream's decision.

Work item Parallel? Reason Review separate test files Often Each reviewer can return findings Choose a shared domain model No Every implementation depends on the decision Update unrelated documentation Often Output boundaries are clear

Splitting an ambiguous task across agents spreads the ambiguity.

docs.title: The coordinator owns the integration risk
docs.text:
A coordinator does more than hand out tasks. It needs to know:

  1. Which decision makes the workstreams compatible.
  2. Which files or systems only one role may change.
  3. Which results each role must return.
  4. When a conflict should stop the workflow rather than be merged automatically.

The coordinator stays human-led even when agents do the initial work.

docs.title: Return a result summary
docs.text:
Each workstream should return a short result summary:

Scope completed:
Evidence:
Files or records changed:
Checks run:
Open questions:
Recommendation:

The parent can compare these summaries without reading each agent's full conversation. Report missing results. Do not guess.

docs.title: Coordinator pattern
docs.text:
Issue with acceptance criteria
        ↓
Coordinator selects a bounded role
        ↓
Role writes a proposal or change
        ↓
Focused checks and human review
        ↓
Decision record, merge, follow-up, or pause

The coordinator assigns work with a defined scope. Clarify an ambiguous request before implementation.

docs.title: Team boundaries
docs.text:
Role Responsibility Lead Scope, decisions, review gate Implementer A defined product area or file set Tester Focused checks and reported gaps Scribe Shared decisions and history Work monitor Flag ready, approved work

Agents need charters that state inputs, outputs, and limits. Avoid concurrent writes to the same files.

docs.title: Shared memory
docs.text:
Commit decision records: the choice, supporting results, owner, and date. Keep temporary drafts separate.

Agents can write individual proposals. A designated owner reviews and merges the shared record. Git history keeps the trail.

docs.title: Issues and monitored work
docs.text:
An issue is a work contract. It needs acceptance criteria, non-goals, constraints, checks, and a reviewer.

Ready issue → assignment → bounded change → focused checks →
human review → merge or follow-up issue

Treat Ralph as a monitored queue. Stop when approval, ownership, policy, test status, scope, or usage limits are unclear.

docs.title: When orchestration helps
docs.text: Situation Path One small repair Individual agent or manual work Separate work with defined interfaces Coordinated team Overlapping ownership or unclear design Plan before implementation Restricted path or unapproved tool Manual workflow

docs.title: One issue, one review trail
docs.text:
The worked issue adds validation to POST /api/users.

Issue contract
  → lead assignment
  → backend implementation
  → tester evidence
  → lead review
  → durable decision

Keep the same acceptance criteria through every step. A role may add supporting results, but it must not quietly expand the issue.

docs.title: Reference .squad/ result
docs.text:
.squad/
├── team.md
├── routing.md
├── decisions.md
├── agents/{lead,backend,tester,scribe}/
├── decisions/inbox/issue-001-proposal.md
├── orchestration-log/issue-001.md
└── reviews/issue-001-review.md

The reference project also includes the implemented route and passing tests.

docs.title: Required access
docs.text: Check GitHub Copilot, Squad, repository integration, and the network path before the lab. If a requirement is unavailable, stop and resolve it. A tabletop simulation does not demonstrate orchestration.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Copy the starter project and check Squad access before work begins.

Submit:

  • one issue assignment;
  • the input-validation implementation;
  • passing focused tests;
  • a lead review and decision record.

Use lab/solution/squad-project/ to check the expected result.
