docs.title: Build reliable agent applications with the GitHub Copilot SDK
docs.text:
Own the lifecycle, policy, run records, and failure path

Session m6-01 | Module 6 | Advanced

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time The application reliability boundary 8 min Client, session, and streaming lifecycle 12 min Tools, permissions, and hooks 17 min Tests and trace evidence 10 min Prepared demo and lab handoff 13 min

docs.title: The application owns the control path
docs.text:
The SDK provides an agent session. Your application still owns:

  • startup and shutdown;
  • the data boundary;
  • which tools exist;
  • which calls may run;
  • what the user sees when work fails;
  • the records kept after the session ends.

A useful answer with an unsafe control path is still a broken application.

docs.title: The scenario is deliberately small
docs.text:
Synthetic change record
        ↓
TypeScript CLI
        ↓
Copilot session
        ↓
Change request lookup tool
        ↓
ready or needs-review

The data is fixed. You build the controls around the model.

docs.title: Start with an explicit lifecycle
docs.text:
import { CopilotClient } from "@github/copilot-sdk";

const client = new CopilotClient({
  telemetry: { otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4318" },
});

await client.start();
let session;

try {
  session = await client.createSession(config);
  await session.sendAndWait({ prompt });
} finally {
  await session?.disconnect();
  await client.stop();
}

Cleanup belongs in finally. A successful response is not proof that resources were released.

docs.title: One client can own several sessions
docs.text:
Object Owns Close when CopilotClient Runtime connection and client options The application exits Session Conversation state, tools, hooks, and events The task is complete Event subscription UI updates from that session The session is no longer observed Collector connection Trace export path The local trace stack stops

Keep session state scoped by session ID. Remove it in the session-end path.

docs.title: Streaming improves feedback and creates edge cases
docs.text:
session.on("assistant.message_delta", (event) => {
  if (!event.agentId) {
    process.stdout.write(event.data.deltaContent);
  }
});

session.on("session.idle", () => {
  process.stdout.write("\n");
});

The final assistant.message still arrives. Decide whether the CLI renders deltas, the final message, or both in different places. Printing both produces duplicates.

docs.title: Events are evidence, not business truth
docs.text:
Session events can show:

  • text deltas;
  • tool requests and results;
  • permission requests;
  • session state changes;
  • usage records.

The readiness verdict must still come from the application's deterministic data and rules. Do not infer readiness from a fluent answer.

docs.title: A custom tool limits what the agent can do
docs.text:
import { defineTool } from "@github/copilot-sdk";

const lookupTool = defineTool("lookup_change_request", {
  description: "Read one synthetic change and calculate readiness gaps",
  parameters: {
    type: "object",
    properties: { requestId: { type: "string" } },
    required: ["requestId"],
    additionalProperties: false,
  },
  handler: async (args) => lookupChangeRequest(changes, args),
});

The schema narrows the input. The handler still validates the request ID before it reads the fixture.

docs.title: Tool availability and permission answer different questions
docs.text:
Control Question Registered tools Can the model choose this capability? onPermissionRequest May this requested execution proceed? onPreToolUse Does application policy allow these exact arguments now? Tool handler Are the input and data valid at execution time?

Use all four where the risk justifies them. One broad approval does not replace argument-level policy.

docs.title: Deny the action before the handler runs
docs.text:
hooks: {
  onPreToolUse: async (input) => {
    if (
      input.toolName === "lookup_change_request" &&
      input.toolArgs?.requestId?.startsWith("RESTRICTED-")
    ) {
      return {
        permissionDecision: "deny",
        permissionDecisionReason:
          "Restricted change requests cannot be read by this assistant.",
      };
    }

    return { permissionDecision: "allow" };
  },
}

The denial reason should appear in the CLI and trace. Silent denial is hard to debug and easy to misread.

docs.title: Keep permission handling narrow
docs.text:
onPermissionRequest: async (request) => {
  if ("managedApprovalRequired" in request &&
      request.managedApprovalRequired === true) {
    return { kind: "no-result" };
  }

  if ("toolName" in request &&
      request.toolName === "lookup_change_request") {
    return { kind: "approve-once" };
  }

  return {
    kind: "reject",
    feedback: "Only the synthetic readiness tool is allowed.",
  };
},

Deny unknown request kinds. Review new capabilities before approving them so they do not inherit permission by accident.

docs.title: Hooks record and control the lifecycle
docs.text:
Session starts
  → request streams
  → tool call reaches pre-tool policy
  → permission decision
  → handler succeeds or fails
  → failure or error hook records the outcome
  → session ends and state is cleared

Hooks run inline. Keep them fast and deterministic.

docs.title: Failure and error are different paths
docs.text:
Path Example Application response Denied call Restricted synthetic ID violates policy Show the reason, record denial Application result Malformed or missing synthetic ID Return a fixed result without invention Tool execution failure Handler throws or returns a failed execution Record the failed tool event SDK error Runtime or model call fails Notify the user, retry only when safe Session end Complete, abort, timeout, or error Flush state and record reason

Do not turn every failure into a retry. Some failures are policy decisions.

docs.title: Use the failed-tool hook for agent guidance
docs.text:
onPostToolUseFailure: async (input) => {
  audit.failedTools.push({
    toolName: input.toolName,
    result: input.toolResult,
  });

  return {
    additionalContext:
      "Do not invent a change record. Report the failed tool result.",
  };
},

This hook sees tool results marked as failures. It does not replace onErrorOccurred.

docs.title: Use the error hook for SDK recovery policy
docs.text:
onErrorOccurred: async (input) => {
  audit.errors.push(input.error);

  return {
    errorHandling: input.recoverable ? "retry" : "abort",
    retryCount: input.recoverable ? 1 : 0,
    userNotification: "The readiness session could not continue.",
  };
},

Retry once only when the error says recovery is possible. Keep the original error in the audit record.

docs.title: End every session with a record
docs.text:
onSessionEnd: async (input, invocation) => {
  audit.endReason = input.reason;
  audit.endedAt = new Date().toISOString();
  sessionState.delete(invocation.sessionId);

  return {
    sessionSummary: `Readiness session ended: ${input.reason}`,
  };
},

Cleanup should be safe to run more than once. A process crash may skip the hook, so the outer finally block still matters.

docs.title: Test the control path, not model phrasing
docs.text:
Test Stable assertion CR-1042 Tool returns ready with no gaps CR-2087 Tool returns needs-review with fixed gaps Restricted ID Pre-tool hook returns deny with the required reason Failed tool event Failed-tool hook records the failure SDK error Error hook chooses the expected recovery action Session completion End hook clears state and records the reason Streaming Deltas render once and final output is not duplicated

Mock the SDK boundary. Keep synthetic data fixed.

docs.title: Trace the same run outside the terminal
docs.text:
CLI process
   │ OTLP/HTTP :4318
   ▼
OpenTelemetry Collector
   │ OTLP
   ▼
Jaeger :16686

const client = new CopilotClient({
  telemetry: {
    otlpEndpoint: "http://localhost:4318",
  },
});

The trace should show session work, tool activity, the denied action, and the end reason for one run.

docs.title: Traces answer questions logs cannot answer quickly
docs.text:
Use Jaeger to check:

  • which span contained the tool request;
  • whether the denied action reached the handler;
  • how long the model and tool steps took;
  • where a failed run stopped;
  • whether one CLI invocation produced one connected trace.

Trace data can contain prompts and tool details. Keep this lab synthetic.

docs.title: Reliability has tradeoffs
docs.text:
Choice Benefit Cost Stream deltas Faster visible feedback More rendering state Deny by default Smaller execution boundary More permission code Hooks for audit One lifecycle view Inline latency if hooks do too much Deterministic tool data Stable tests and demos Less realism Local tracing stack Traces you can inspect Docker setup and local resource use

Choose controls that show what failed and why. Checks that only make the code look safer do not help.

docs.title: Prepared demonstration
docs.text:
1. Run the passing tests.
  2. Start the Collector and Jaeger.
  3. Assess a known synthetic change.
  4. Watch the response stream.
  5. Request the restricted synthetic record.
  6. Show the denial in the terminal.
  7. Open the same run in Jaeger.
  8. Trigger an unknown ID and show the failure path.

Show one denied tool call in the CLI, then find the same policy decision inside the trace.

docs.title: Keep the boundary tight
docs.text:
This session does not use:

  • dynamic workflows or fleet;
  • cloud or remote sessions;
  • BYOK;
  • plugin packaging;
  • production deployment;
  • external business systems;
  • a second implementation language.

The lab is about one local TypeScript application's control path.

docs.title: Lab handoff
docs.text:
Build the CLI in lab/starter/sdk-readiness-assistant/.

You will complete the lifecycle, streaming, readiness tool, permissions, hooks, tests, and OTLP export. Then you will run the known, denied, and failed paths and inspect the trace in Jaeger.

Stop if authenticated Copilot access, Node.js/npm, or Docker is unavailable.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m6-01 lab: Build a traced change readiness assistant
docs.text: Duration: 120 minutes Difficulty: Advanced Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04, m3-01 to m3-05 and the Session m6-01 trainer content

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Complete a TypeScript CLI that uses the GitHub Copilot SDK to assess deterministic synthetic change records. Your application must stream its response and call one tool limited to readiness lookups. It must also deny a restricted lookup, record failures, pass focused tests, and export traces through an OpenTelemetry Collector to Jaeger.

docs.title: Final deliverables
docs.text:
Submit or demonstrate:

  1. a working CLI under sdk-readiness-assistant/;
  2. client and session cleanup on every exit path;
  3. streamed parent-agent output without duplicate final text;
  4. the typed readiness tool over the supplied synthetic data;
  5. permission handling plus a pre-tool policy that visibly denies RESTRICTED-0001;
  6. failed-tool, error, and session-end hook records;
  7. passing tests and type checks;
  8. one Jaeger trace for a permitted assessment;
  9. one Jaeger trace or trace event showing the denied action;
  10. terminal output for the unknown-change failure path.

docs.title: Time plan
docs.text: Part Work Time 1 Preflight and baseline 15 min 2 Client, session, and streaming 20 min 3 Readiness tool and policy 30 min 4 Failure hooks and cleanup 20 min 5 Tests 15 min 6 Collector, Jaeger, and final verification 20 min

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
Work from:

sessions/session-m6-01-copilot-sdk/lab/starter/sdk-readiness-assistant/

Authenticated GitHub Copilot SDK access is required. You also need:

  • Node.js and npm versions accepted by package.json;
  • Docker Engine;
  • Docker Compose;
  • permission to bind the local ports declared in the Compose file.

Stop if any item is unavailable. Do not switch to BYOK, another model provider, a remote session, or a different language.

Run the local checks:

node --version
npm --version
docker version
docker compose version
npm ci
npm run check
npm test

Some focused tests should fail because you have not completed the reliability controls yet. The project must compile far enough to show those gaps. Use the instructor-provided authentication check in src/live-demo.ts before starting the live exercises. If client.getAuthStatus() reports that the user is not authenticated, stop.

docs.title: Project map
docs.text:
Use the names present in the starter project. The expected layout is:

sdk-readiness-assistant/
├── package.json
├── compose.yaml
├── otel-collector-config.yaml
├── fixtures/
│   └── change-requests.json
├── src/
│   ├── live-demo.ts
│   ├── change-store.ts
│   ├── permission-policy.ts
│   ├── hook-decisions.ts
│   └── types.ts
└── tests/
    ├── change-store.test.ts
    ├── permission-policy.test.ts
    └── hook-decisions.test.ts

Do not add external data sources or new runtime dependencies.

docs.title: Part 1: Establish lifecycle and streaming (20 minutes)
Goal
docs.text: Start the client, create one local session, stream parent-agent output, and close the client on every exit path.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the application entry point and lifecycle module.
  2. Create CopilotClient with the supplied telemetry endpoint.
  3. Start the client before creating the session.
  4. Create one session with streaming enabled.
  5. Subscribe to assistant.message_delta.
  6. Print only parent-agent deltas.
  7. Keep final message events for audit or tests. Do not print the same response again.
  8. Put client shutdown in finally.
  9. Keep per-session state keyed by the session ID.

Use this lifecycle shape:

const client = new CopilotClient(clientOptions);
await client.start();
let session;

try {
  session = await client.createSession(sessionConfig);
  subscribeToOutput(session);
  await session.sendAndWait({ prompt });
} finally {
  await session?.disconnect();
  await client.stop();
}

Run:

npm run check
npm test

docs.title: Checkpoint 1
docs.text:
• The client starts before session creation.
  • The session disconnects after success and thrown errors.
  • The client stops after success and thrown errors.
  • Parent text streams once.
  • Per-session state is not global shared state.

docs.title: Part 2: Complete the readiness tool and policy (30 minutes)
Goal
docs.text: Expose deterministic readiness data through one typed tool. Permit normal lookups and deny the restricted synthetic record before the handler runs.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the supplied change records in fixtures/change-requests.json.
  2. Do not edit the record IDs or expected verdicts.
  3. Complete the lookup_change_request tool with its supplied JSON Schema.
  4. Validate the change ID inside the handler.
  5. Return the matching evidence, gaps, and verdict.
  6. Return the fixed invalid-input or not-found result for bad IDs.
  7. Add onPermissionRequest.
  8. Approve only the supplied readiness tool request.
  9. Reject unknown request kinds and unrelated tools.
  10. Add onPreToolUse.

  11. Deny IDs beginning with RESTRICTED- with this reason:

    Restricted change requests cannot be read by this assistant.

  12. Record whether the handler ran. The denied test must prove that it did not.

Do not use an approve-all helper. You need to show that unrelated requests are rejected while the readiness lookup is permitted.

Run the focused tool and policy tests:

npm test

docs.title: Checkpoint 2
docs.text:
Demonstrate:

  • CR-1042 returns ready with no gaps;
  • CR-2087 returns needs-review with fixed gaps;
  • malformed or unknown IDs return fixed results without invention;
  • a normal lookup is permitted;
  • RESTRICTED-0001 is denied with a visible reason;
  • the denied request never enters the tool handler.

docs.title: Part 3: Add failure, error, and end hooks (20 minutes)
Goal
docs.text: Record the expected failure paths and clear session state at the end.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Complete onPostToolUseFailure.
  2. Record the tool name and failed result.
  3. Add context that tells the agent to report unknown data instead of inventing a change record.
  4. Complete onErrorOccurred.
  5. Store the original error.
  6. Retry once only when the SDK marks the error recoverable.
  7. Abort unrecoverable errors and show a short user notification.
  8. Complete onSessionEnd.
  9. Record the end reason and timestamp.
  10. Delete state for the ended session.
  11. Keep cleanup safe if called more than once.

Do not treat a denied tool call as an SDK error. It is a policy result.

Run:

npm test
npm run check

docs.title: Checkpoint 3
docs.text:
The audit record distinguishes:

  • policy denial;
  • failed tool result;
  • recoverable or unrecoverable SDK error;
  • normal or abnormal session end.

Session state is empty after the end hook.

docs.title: Part 4: Finish the automated tests (15 minutes)
Goal
docs.text:
Prove the control path without depending on model wording or a live trace backend.

Complete or repair tests for:

  • a known ready change;
  • a known blocked change;
  • malformed and unknown change IDs;
  • denied RESTRICTED-0001 lookup;
  • handler non-execution after denial;
  • one retry for a recoverable error;
  • abort for an unrecoverable error;
  • session state cleanup;
  • streamed deltas rendered once;
  • client shutdown after an exception.

Mock the SDK at the boundaries the starter provides. Do not call a live model from unit tests.

Run:

npm test
npm run check

If package.json defines linting, run:

npm run lint

docs.title: Checkpoint 4
docs.text: All tests pass twice without data or snapshot changes.

docs.title: Part 5: Start tracing and run the application (20 minutes)
Goal
docs.text: Export one connected trace through the local Collector and inspect it in Jaeger.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Review compose.yaml and otel-collector-config.yaml.
  2. Check the SDK OTLP HTTP endpoint is:
http://localhost:4318
  1. Start the local stack:
docker compose -f compose.yaml up -d
docker compose -f compose.yaml ps
  1. Wait until the Collector and Jaeger services are healthy.
  2. Run npm run demo.
  3. Check that CR-1042 streams a ready assessment.
  4. Check that bad-id returns the fixed invalid-input result.
  5. Check that RESTRICTED-0001 prints the denial reason.
  6. Check that the session disconnects and the client stops.
  7. Open the Jaeger UI at http://localhost:16686.
  8. Select the service name configured by the project.
  9. Find the three most recent runs.
  10. Open the denied run and check that no lookup handler work follows the policy denial.
  11. Locate the permitted and invalid-input paths.

Stop the local stack when the trainer tells you to:

docker compose -f compose.yaml down

docs.title: Checkpoint 5
docs.text:
Show the trainer:

  • the permitted terminal run;
  • the visible denied action;
  • the invalid-input result;
  • one connected Jaeger trace;
  • the session end reason;
  • passing tests and type checks.

docs.title: Verification checklist
docs.text:
• Authenticated GitHub Copilot SDK preflight passed.
  • Node.js, npm, Docker, and Docker Compose preflight passed.
  • The client starts before session creation and stops on every exit path.
  • The session streams parent output without duplicate final text.
  • The readiness tool reads only deterministic synthetic data.
  • Permission handling rejects unrelated requests.
  • The pre-tool hook denies RESTRICTED-0001 before handler execution.
  • The denial reason is visible.
  • Failed-tool, error, and session-end hooks record distinct outcomes.
  • Per-session state is cleared.
  • Tests pass.
  • Type checks pass.
  • The Collector and Jaeger receive traces.
  • A Jaeger trace shows the denied path.
  • No excluded feature or external business system was added.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Fix client.getAuthStatus() reports unauthenticated Stop. Check the GitHub Copilot sign-in and permitted network path. Do not use BYOK or another provider. CopilotClient starts but session creation fails Check the installed package lock, supported Node.js version, and current GitHub Copilot access. Output is duplicated Print assistant.message_delta as live output and keep the final message for records only. Restricted data reaches the handler Match the exact tool name and inspect parsed toolArgs.requestId in onPreToolUse. Unknown IDs produce an invented answer Return a failed tool result and add failure-hook context that forbids invention. Tests call the live model Mock the SDK session boundary and assert deterministic events or decisions. Collector cannot bind port 4318 Stop the conflicting process only if you may do so, or change the supplied local configuration consistently. Jaeger is empty Check container health, the Collector export pipeline, service name, and Jaeger time range. Session state remains after completion Delete the session ID in onSessionEnd and keep outer cleanup in finally.

docs.title: Solution reference
docs.text:
After completing all checkpoints, compare your work with:

sessions/session-m6-01-copilot-sdk/lab/solution/sdk-readiness-assistant/

Review these areas in order:

  1. src/live-demo.ts for client, session, streaming, and hooks;
  2. src/change-store.ts for the deterministic lookup;
  3. src/permission-policy.ts for permission decisions;
  4. src/hook-decisions.ts for prompt and pre-tool policy;
  5. tests/ for stable control-path assertions;
  6. compose.yaml and otel-collector-config.yaml for trace routing.

Do not copy the solution before the checkpoints. Compare its controls, test results, and traces with yours.

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text:
Show where the model's work ends and application code takes over. The model produces an assessment. TypeScript code manages the lifecycle, limits tools, makes permission decisions, handles failures, and records traces.

Keep the session local and focused. Do not add orchestration, remote sessions, BYOK, packaging, deployment, external systems, or another language.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text:
Time Segment Exit signal 0:00 to 0:08 Application reliability boundary Learners can name what the application owns 0:08 to 0:20 Client, session, and streaming Learners can draw the startup and cleanup path 0:20 to 0:37 Tool, permissions, and hooks Learners can explain where a call is denied 0:37 to 0:47 Tests and trace evidence Learners can name a stable assertion for each path 0:47 to 0:57 Prepared live demo The denied action is visible in the CLI and Jaeger 0:57 to 1:00 Lab transition Every learner has passed preflight

Use slides.md for the teaching sequence.

docs.title: Trainer prerequisites
docs.text:
Prepare the delivery machine before learners arrive:

  1. Check Node.js and npm meet the versions declared in the supplied project.
  2. Check Docker Engine and Docker Compose can start the supplied local stack.
  3. Check authenticated GitHub Copilot SDK access with the same account and network path learners will use.
  4. Run npm ci, the test command, and the type-check command in the reference solution.
  5. Start the OpenTelemetry Collector and Jaeger from the reference solution.
  6. Run one successful readiness assessment and find its trace in Jaeger.
  7. Run the denied action and check that the reason appears in both terminal output and trace data.
  8. Keep the solution project open at the files used in the demo.

Stop if any required access or local tool is unavailable. Do not replace authenticated Copilot access with another model provider.

docs.title: The application owns the boundary
docs.text:
Open with the synthetic change record. Ask which parts need model reasoning and which parts should stay deterministic.

The readiness tool returns fixed lookup results. The model can explain those results, but it cannot create a new record or change the policy. This separation makes the lab testable.

Emphasize these decisions:

  • register only lookup_change_request;
  • inspect exact tool arguments before execution;
  • deny unrecognized permission requests;
  • show policy denial to the user;
  • clean up even when the session fails.

docs.title: Client and session lifecycle
docs.text:
Draw the sequence on the slide:

construct client → start client → create session → subscribe →
send request → await completion → close session state → stop client

The session-end hook records what the agent runtime reports. The outer finally block handles process-level cleanup. Both are needed.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Show assistant.message_delta and the final assistant.message as separate event types. A CLI that prints both as primary output repeats the response.

The supplied application streams parent-agent text deltas. It uses complete events for records and tests. It ignores sub-agent output because sub-agents are outside this session.

docs.title: Tool and permission layers
docs.text:
Use the table from the slides. Registration, permission requests, pre-tool policy, and handler validation are separate controls.

The lookup tool accepts one synthetic request ID. Normal CR-#### values reach the handler. IDs beginning with RESTRICTED- prove the denial path. The pre-tool hook blocks them before the handler runs.

docs.title: Failure and error hooks
docs.text:
Explain the distinction with these prepared cases:

  • malformed input returns a fixed validation result;
  • a failed tool execution enters onPostToolUseFailure;
  • a runtime or model error enters onErrorOccurred.

Do not call a policy denial an error. The application did exactly what it was designed to do.

docs.title: Tests and traces
docs.text:
The tests assert control decisions and deterministic results. They do not assert the model's prose.

Use Jaeger to show the timing and sequence of a run. Check whether the restricted call reached the handler and where a failed run stopped. Remind learners that trace payloads can expose prompts and tool arguments. The lab uses synthetic data for that reason.

docs.title: Demo 1: Trace a denied change request
docs.text: Level: L300 Time: 10 minutes

docs.title: Demo focus
docs.text: Show the denied lookup for RESTRICTED-0001 in the terminal. Seconds later, open Jaeger and point to the same blocked tool call inside the connected trace. Learners can compare what the user sees with what the operator can inspect.

docs.title: Demo prerequisites
docs.text:
• The authenticated GitHub Copilot SDK access check passed.
  • Node.js, npm, Docker, and Docker Compose are working.
  • The reference solution dependencies are installed.
  • The solution tests pass.
  • Ports used by the supplied Collector and Jaeger configuration are free.
  • The deterministic change IDs in the solution have not been edited.

docs.title: Demo steps
docs.text:
1. Show the starting state.

Open lab/solution/sdk-readiness-assistant/. Point to fixtures/change-requests.json, src/live-demo.ts, src/permission-policy.ts, src/hook-decisions.ts, the tests, and the telemetry configuration.

"The model does not own this data or policy. It can reason over one fixed record. TypeScript decides which capability exists and whether the exact call may run."

  1. Prove the baseline.

Run:

npm test
npm run check

"I want the control path green before I involve a live model. These tests check known data, denial, failure handling, streaming, and cleanup. They do not compare natural-language answers."

  1. Start the trace stack.

Run:

docker compose -f compose.yaml up -d
docker compose -f compose.yaml ps

"The SDK exports OTLP data to the Collector on port 4318. The Collector forwards traces to Jaeger. The CLI stays unaware of the Jaeger backend."

  1. Run a permitted assessment.

Run npm run demo. The first request assesses CR-1042. Let the response stream to the terminal.

"You see text as it arrives. The final event is still recorded, but the renderer does not print it a second time."

  1. Watch the restricted lookup.

The third prepared prompt requests RESTRICTED-0001.

"The tool is known to the application, so the request reaches policy. The pre-tool hook checks the request ID and denies this lookup before the handler can run."

  1. Point to the visible denial.

Read the denial reason from the terminal. Show the audit entry produced by the application.

"A denied action is an expected result. The user gets a reason, and the audit path records the decision. Nothing is silently dropped."

  1. Open Jaeger.

Open the local Jaeger UI, select the service name declared by the project, and find the latest trace.

"This is the same run from the operator view. The trace shows the session work and the blocked tool call. There is no handler span after the denial."

  1. Show invalid input and the failed-tool policy.

Point to the bad-id run. Then show the failed-tool hook test and session-end hook test.

"Invalid input is different from denied policy. The tool returns a fixed validation result. A failed tool execution uses its own hook, and the session-end hook records why the session closed."

  1. Close the demo.

Stop the application. Leave the trace stack running for the lab if the training machine is shared and the instructor setup permits it.

"We check reliability through tool limits, permission decisions, visible outcomes, tests, and traces."

docs.title: Demo troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Response SDK authentication fails Stop the demo. Check the GitHub Copilot sign-in and permitted network path. Do not use BYOK or another provider. No streamed text appears Check the session enables streaming and the handler listens for parent assistant.message_delta events. Restricted data reaches the handler Stop. Check the exact tool name and parsed requestId in onPreToolUse, then rerun the denial test. Collector is unreachable Check Docker Compose health and the OTLP HTTP endpoint configured as http://localhost:4318. Jaeger shows no trace Check the Collector exports to Jaeger, select the configured service name, and widen the time range. Output appears twice Check whether both message deltas and the final assistant message are printed as primary output.

docs.title: Transition to the lab
docs.text:
Say:

"You will now add the same controls to the starter project. Finish one layer at a time, run the focused checks at each checkpoint, and do not continue if access or Docker preflight fails."

Point learners to lab/README.md.

docs.title: Lab coaching map
docs.text: Lab checkpoint Coach question Preflight Did every required tool and authenticated SDK call pass? Lifecycle and streaming Where does cleanup run if sendAndWait throws? Tool and denial Can the learner prove the handler did not run? Failure hooks Is unknown data reported without invention or broad retry? Tests Are assertions stable without matching model prose? Traces Can the learner connect terminal output to one Jaeger trace?

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content, 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Implement and review one Bookmark API slice: POST /api/bookmarks. Keep the accepted GitHub issue as the limit on what you change and apply the Session m5-02 specification standards. Finish with test results and a handoff that another engineer can use.

The capstone stays small on purpose. Authentication, persistent storage, deployment, and every other bookmark endpoint remain out of scope.

Implement only the accepted endpoint. Use synthetic data and the existing dependencies. Stop if the work requires another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Keep scope decisions in the accepted GitHub issue.
  • Check a prepared specification for testable behavior and named non-goals.
  • Turn the accepted specification into one implementation-ready issue.
  • Check the Bookmark creation slice with executable tests.
  • Record a review decision, deferred scope, and the next action.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab lab/README.md Starter files lab/starter/ Reference solution lab/solution/

docs.title: Final deliverable

docs.title: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text: Session m6-02 | 3 hours

docs.title: One slice
docs.text:
Implement and review:

POST /api/bookmarks

Everything else is deferred.

docs.title: The result is a handoff
docs.text:
• implementation-ready issue;
  • patch or patch plan;
  • executable test results;
  • review decision;
  • deferred scope and next action.

docs.title: Keep the boundary in the issue
docs.text:
Keep every scope decision in the accepted GitHub issue. Implement only POST /api/bookmarks, use synthetic data, and keep the existing dependencies.

Stop if the work requires another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.

docs.title: Session m5-02 is an input
docs.text:
The accepted specification must separate:

Behavior Implementation constraint Observable request and response rules Node.js, Express, in-memory storage Validation and duplicate behavior Existing dependencies only Acceptance scenarios Exact files and test command

docs.title: Issue trace
docs.text:
Every acceptance criterion maps to:

specification ID -> planned file -> executable test

If the issue adds behavior missing from the specification, revise the issue before implementation.

docs.title: Scope guard
docs.text:
In scope:

  • create one bookmark;
  • validate the accepted fields;
  • reject a duplicate URL;
  • return the documented envelope and status.

Out of scope: authentication, persistence, other endpoints, deployment, and new packages.

Path Use Copilot Implement the single issue Manual Implement the same files and tests Blocked Produce a reviewable patch plan

docs.title: Executable verification
docs.text:
npm test

The suite checks success, defaults, field validation, and duplicate URLs.

docs.title: Review and handover
docs.text:
Trace the change back to the specification. Review the diff, test output, dependency change, and scope decisions in the issue. Record any deviation in the handoff.

Record one decision: approve, request changes, or pause.

docs.title: Session m6-02 lab: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Advanced

Prerequisites: Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04, m3-01 to m3-05 and m5-02; Session m5-01 is optional

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Before the lab, check repository or sandbox permissions, GitHub Copilot access, and Node.js 20 or later. Name a human reviewer. Use only synthetic bookmark data.

If GitHub Copilot, repository access, Node.js, or dependency installation is unavailable, stop the lab. Do not create a public repository, add a package, configure an MCP server, or use production data.

The only implementation slice is POST /api/bookmarks.

Phase Work Time 1 Set the boundary and accept the specification 25 min 2 Write the issue and establish the baseline 25 min 3 Implement the accepted slice 35 min 4 Verify, review, and hand off 35 min

docs.title: Phase 1: Accept the specification and scope (25 min)
docs.text:
Read starter/bookmark-create-spec.md. Check it against the Session m5-02 standard:

  • requirements describe observable behavior;
  • acceptance scenarios are testable;
  • implementation choices appear only under constraints;
  • non-goals are named;
  • every open question has an owner or a safe default.

Record the accepted specification IDs and all scope decisions in the GitHub issue section of starter/capstone-handoff.md. Do not add requirements during implementation.

docs.title: Phase 2: Write the issue and establish the baseline (25 min)
docs.text:
Write the issue in starter/capstone-handoff.md. Include:

  • goal and accepted specification IDs;
  • acceptance criteria and non-goals;
  • expected files;
  • required tests;
  • work stop conditions;
  • human reviewer.

Copy and enter the starter project:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02
cp -R lab/starter/capstone-project ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02/capstone-project
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m6-02/capstone-project
npm install

Run the health-check baseline:

npm test -- --runTestsByPath tests/health.test.js

Then run npm test. The Bookmark tests should fail because the route does not exist. Record that baseline. The missing-route failures are expected at this stage.

docs.title: Phase 3: Implement the accepted slice (35 min)
docs.text:
Use Copilot and treat the issue as the work order. Before editing, list the expected files and map each file to a specification ID.

Implement only:

  • route registration;
  • in-memory creation and duplicate lookup;
  • accepted field validation;
  • documented success and error responses.

Implement only the accepted POST /api/bookmarks endpoint. Use synthetic data and the existing dependencies. Stop if the work requires another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.

When blocked or out of time, stop implementation and record the blocker in starter/capstone-handoff.md. Do not claim completion without test results.

docs.title: Phase 4: Verify, review, and hand off (35 min)
docs.text:
Run:

npm test

Compare the patch with the issue and specification. Check that package.json contains no new dependency. Record any deviation from the accepted issue in the handoff.

Ask your reviewer to record one decision: approve, request changes, or pause. Complete every section in starter/capstone-handoff.md.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text: Time Expected state 25 min Specification and scope review are complete 50 min Issue and executable baseline are recorded 85 min Patch is ready 105 min Tests and specification trace are reviewed 120 min Decision and next action are recorded

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit one capstone-handoff.md containing:

  1. The implementation-ready issue mapped to specification IDs.
  2. The patch summary.
  3. Executable test results.
  4. The human review decision and reviewer.
  5. Deferred scope, deviations, and known risks.
  6. One owned next action.

Your deliverable is incomplete without executable test results or a review decision.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m6-02 trainer guide: End-to-end capstone for one endpoint
docs.text: 00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide      Enable timer shortcut (T)

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Guide learners through one reviewed POST /api/bookmarks change or patch plan. Keep scope decisions in the accepted GitHub issue and require the Session m5-02 specification standards. Do not let the exercise expand into a full API, deployment, or tool tour.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00 to 0:08 Define the one-slice capstone 0:08 to 0:18 Set the issue boundary 0:18 to 0:30 Inspect and tighten the specification 0:30 to 0:40 Write the implementation issue 0:40 to 0:50 Walk through the patch and tests 0:50 to 1:00 Make the review decision and hand off

docs.title: Teach the boundary
docs.text:
The required slice is POST /api/bookmarks. Learners may implement it with Copilot or manually. They may also produce a patch plan when execution is blocked. All paths use the same issue, checks, review gate, and handoff.

Write these non-goals where everyone can see them:

  • no authentication;
  • no persistent storage;
  • no list, read, update, or delete endpoint;
  • no deployment or CI redesign;
  • no new dependency.

docs.title: Keep the boundary in the issue
docs.text: Have learners put every scope decision in the accepted GitHub issue. Do not create a separate form. They must implement only POST /api/bookmarks, use synthetic data, and keep the existing dependencies. They must stop if the work requires another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.

docs.title: Apply Session m5-02
docs.text:
Use lab/starter/bookmark-create-spec.md as the source for accepted behavior. Ask learners to check that each requirement is observable, technology choices stay in the constraints section, and non-goals are named. They must map each issue criterion to a specification ID and a test.

The issue should name the exact route, response shapes, validation rules, duplicate behavior, expected files, required tests, reviewer, and stop conditions. It must not invent behavior absent from the specification.

docs.title: Implementation walkthrough
docs.text:
Use this work order:

Implement only the accepted POST /api/bookmarks issue in the training sandbox.
Use synthetic data and the existing dependencies. Before editing, name the expected
files and map each change to a requirement. Run npm test. Stop if the work requires
another endpoint, live data, deployment, tool configuration, or a new dependency.
Report changed files, test results, deviations, and deferred scope for review.

After 30 minutes of implementation, have learners move unfinished work to a patch plan. They still need to inspect the tests, record a decision, and complete the handoff.

docs.title: Review gate
docs.text:
Review in this order:

  1. Specification and acceptance criteria.
  2. Scope and deferrals.
  3. Validation, response shape, duplicate handling, and tests.
  4. Stop conditions and deviations from the accepted issue.
  5. Handoff owner and next action.

Record one decision: approve, request changes, or pause. Do not approve a serious issue because time ran out.

docs.title: Reference assets
docs.text:
• lab/solution/capstone-project/ contains the creation endpoint and tests.
  • lab/solution/reference-handoff.md shows the full issue-to-handoff record.
  • lab/starter/capstone-handoff.md is the learner template.
  • lab/starter/trainer-delivery-plan-template.md is an optional trainer reflection. It is not a learner deliverable.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Should learners add the other Bookmark endpoints? No. Record them under deferred scope.

What if agent access fails? Stop the lab. Do not count a patch plan as capstone completion.

What if the tests cannot run? Record the command, failure, findings from inspection, and owner for the next action. Do not approve without executable test results.

docs.title: Session m7-01: Work effectively in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: A GitHub account with GitHub Copilot access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Start the Delivery Decision Studio path by comparing answers with and without repository context. Save what you learn in an initiative context brief. You will check context usage, request an independent critique, and test whether a fresh session can use the brief without the original chat.

The fictional Service Request Portal provides the shared scenario. Learners may use approved, sanitized work from their own team.

Important

The GitHub Copilot app is required. Fix access, policy, or client problems before the lab.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
By the end of this session, learners can:

  1. Find and use Chats, Projects, My work, Search, Automations, and Customize.
  2. Choose Interactive, Plan, or Autopilot mode for a task with a defined scope.
  3. Add files with @, reference issues with #, and open commands with /.
  4. Choose repository, issue, file, or uploaded-document context for a question.
  5. Inspect the skills, agents, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases available in their environment.
  6. Explain the difference between an MCP connection and a plugin package.
  7. Check context usage and decide whether to compact or start fresh.
  8. Review and revise a proposed Markdown change.
  9. Update a context brief when the owner approves new source information.
  10. Use independent critique before sharing the brief.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Slides slides.md Starter initiative and brief template lab/starter/ Reference brief and context review lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Use only synthetic or approved, sanitized material.
  • Treat Copilot output as a proposal until the learner checks its source.
  • Keep write actions reviewable and reversible.
  • Do not require programming, Git command-line work, or extension development.
  • Do not use customer data or source organization names.
  • Delivery Decision Studio is the learning path. Service Request Portal is the initiative.

docs.title: Work effectively in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text: Session m7-01 | Product and Delivery Teams | Beginner

docs.title: The app is the classroom
docs.text:
Work in the GitHub Copilot app with repository context. Save work that others can review.

Delivery Decision Studio is the six-session path. Service Request Portal is the initiative.

docs.title: Save work beyond the chat
docs.text:
Use the chat to work through an idea. Keep project context, source references, issues, and saved artifacts available for review after the conversation ends.

Gather evidence → form a proposal → review it → save the decision → verify it

This separates the model's narrative from facts the team can check.

docs.title: Context has a cost
docs.text:
Context choice When it helps One named file The answer depends on a specific rule or API A project or repository The task needs relationships across files An issue or pull request The task needs delivery history and discussion No repository context The work is general and contains no project facts

Tell Copilot why each source matters. Do not make it guess.

docs.title: Separate facts, assumptions, and decisions
docs.text:
Type Example Fact "Issue 42 names a response-time problem." Assumption "The mobile client uses the documented endpoint." Decision "The product owner will confirm the client behavior."

This makes uncertainty visible. A polished paragraph can hide all three.

docs.title: Know the main work areas
docs.text: Area Use it for Chats Exploration and interviews Projects Repository-grounded work My work Issues, pull requests, and sessions Search Finding repository information Automations Recurring or on-demand tasks Customize Skills, agents, MCP servers, and canvases

docs.title: Context comes before the prompt
docs.text:
Use only permitted sources. Attach the smallest set that answers the question.

Name the files, issues, or repository that should support the answer.

docs.title: Choose the session mode
docs.text:
Mode Use in this path Interactive Questions, interviews, and reviewed drafts Plan Review a multi-step approach before changes Autopilot Work with agreed scope and permission to act without review of every action

Session m7-01 uses Interactive, then Plan. The learner reviews every write.

docs.title: Use verified context controls
docs.text:
• @ adds a file.
  • # references an issue.
  • / opens commands.
  • /context shows current context usage.
  • /compact summarizes a long active session.
  • /clear or /reset starts fresh.

docs.title: Ask for sources
docs.text:
Explain the initiative for a product owner.
Cite the supplied source for each factual claim.
Mark missing information as unknown.

A confident answer without a source is still unverified.

docs.title: Inspect what Copilot can use
docs.text:
• Skills provide repeatable procedures.
  • Agents carry role-specific instructions and tools.
  • MCP servers connect Copilot to systems.
  • Plugins install reusable packages that can include MCP servers and other customizations.
  • Canvases provide visible shared state.
  • Automations repeat tasks with a defined scope.

Availability depends on the plan, policy, and installation.

docs.title: Use one repeatable work pattern
docs.text:
Read -> propose -> review -> write -> verify

Every later Module 7 session uses this pattern.

docs.title: Conversation should become an artifact
docs.text:
The lab creates initiative-context-brief.md with:

  • facts and sources;
  • unknowns;
  • useful GitHub artifacts;
  • the next decision and owner.

The brief must make sense without the chat history.

docs.title: Evidence changes the brief
docs.text:
Initial source
  → first brief
  → approved late evidence
  → focused revision
  → fresh-session verification

Keep the brief consistent with source information the owner has approved.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text:
1. Open the repository as a Copilot project.
  2. Inspect the available capabilities.
  3. Compare an unscoped answer with a grounded answer.
  4. Create and commit the initiative context brief.
  5. Apply approved late evidence.
  6. Review and commit the focused revision.
  7. Ask /rubber-duck for independent critique.
  8. Check the brief in a fresh session.

Stop if the app or repository context is unavailable.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-01 lab: Build and check a grounded working brief
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Beginner

Deliverable: initiative-context-brief.md, ready for Session m7-02 without the original chat

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
Compare Copilot's answers with and without project context. Use the sourced information to write a brief, then revise it when new information arrives. Finally, check whether a fresh session can use the brief on its own.

Part Work Time 1 Check the app, mode, and project 15 min 2 Compare weak and grounded context 25 min 3 Create the first working brief 30 min 4 Update the brief with new evidence 25 min 5 Check the brief in a fresh session 25 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

You need:

  • GitHub Copilot app access;
  • read access to the training repository project;
  • permission to create a branch or working copy for the brief.

Check GitHub Copilot access before starting. If GitHub Copilot access or project access is unavailable, stop. Do not continue in a generic chatbot.

docs.title: Part 1: Check the app and project (15 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Open the training repository under Projects.
  2. Start an interactive session.
  3. Select Interactive mode. Type @ and add lab/starter/initiative-overview.md.
  4. Ask Copilot to report the file name and its first heading.
  5. Open Customize → Installed and inspect the visible skills, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases.
  6. Run /context.

Use Interactive for the comparison. Switch to Plan before asking Copilot to propose repository changes. Do not use Autopilot for this lab because you need to review each write.

@ adds files, # references issues, and / opens commands in the app. Type the character and select the item from the picker. A typed file token alone does not show that the app attached the source.

Checkpoint: Copilot can read the supplied file, and you can identify which capabilities are available.

docs.title: Part 2: Compare weak and grounded context (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Start with a deliberately weak prompt without attaching a file:

Explain the Service Request Portal initiative, its users, constraints, and next
decision. Mark anything uncertain.

Identify statements that have no visible source.

Now attach starter/initiative-overview.md and ask:

Use only @initiative-overview.md. Explain the requested outcome, affected users,
known constraints, and next decision. Cite the heading that supports each fact.
Keep missing information as unknown.

Compare the answers:

Check Unscoped answer Grounded answer Unsupported facts Visible unknowns Source references Useful next decision

Checkpoint: Explain which answer is safer and how repository context changed it.

docs.title: Part 3: Create the first working brief (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Copy the templates:

cp sessions/session-m7-01-copilot-app-foundations/lab/starter/initiative-context-brief-template.md \
  docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md

Ask Copilot to complete the brief from initiative-overview.md. Require:

  • the requested outcome and affected users;
  • known facts with section references;
  • assumptions separated from unknowns;
  • named non-goals;
  • the next decision and its owner;
  • the relevant capabilities found in Part 1.

Review the proposed change before accepting it. Reject any statement that has no source, invents an owner, or turns an unknown into a fact.

Commit the first version:

git add docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md
git commit -m "Create grounded initiative working brief"

Checkpoint: Your brief separates source facts, assumptions, unknowns, and the next decision clearly enough for someone to use it without reading the chat.

docs.title: Part 4: Update the brief with new evidence (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open starter/late-evidence.md. Treat it as source information the owner approved after the first brief was committed.

Ask Copilot to:

  1. compare the new information with the saved brief;
  2. list which sections need to change;
  3. identify any resolved unknown;
  4. identify any statement that is now contradicted;
  5. propose a focused file update.

Review the diff. Do not rewrite unrelated sections.

Commit the revision:

git add docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md
git commit -m "Update working brief with approved evidence"

Checkpoint: Git history shows which source changes led to the revision.

docs.title: Part 5: Check the brief in a fresh session (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Before starting fresh, run /context. If the current session is crowded but the thread still matters, use /compact. For the fresh-session check, use /clear or /reset, then attach only docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md.

Ask:

Using only this working brief, report:
1. the requested outcome;
2. supported facts and their sources;
3. unresolved decisions;
4. named non-goals;
5. the next owner action.
Do not infer missing information.

Compare the answer with the file. If the answer misses or misstates any of these items, correct the brief so the new session has what it needs.

Run an independent critique:

/rubber-duck Review the initiative context brief for unsupported claims,
ambiguous ownership, hidden customer references, and decisions presented as facts.

If /rubber-duck is unavailable, stop this step. The trainer must check the current documented critique option before delivery rather than inventing a replacement command.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. docs/discovery/initiative-context-brief.md;
  2. two commits showing the first brief and the revision based on the new source.

Session m7-02 uses this brief as the source for its decision interview.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Copilot read the repository project successfully.
  • The unscoped and grounded answers were compared.
  • Every fact in the brief points to a source section.
  • Assumptions and unknowns remain separate.
  • New source information produced a focused revision.
  • A fresh session recovered the intended state from the brief alone.
  • No customer or source organization names appear.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-01 trainer guide: Work effectively in the GitHub Copilot app
docs.text:
00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide Enable timer shortcut (T)

Duration: 1 hour Audience: Product managers, product owners, business analysts, project managers, and delivery leads

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Show learners how to choose a session mode and attach approved source material in the GitHub Copilot app. Compare answers with and without those sources before creating the first Delivery Decision Studio brief.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:08 Orient learners to the app 0:08-0:18 Choose mode and context 0:18-0:28 Inspect capabilities and context health 0:28-0:40 Compare unscoped and grounded answers 0:40-0:53 Create, revise, and check a working brief 0:53-1:00 Explain boundaries and launch the lab

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
• Check that every learner can open the GitHub Copilot app.
  • Check that the learner can start a chat and open the training repository as a project.
  • Check that the learner can see the current app navigation and available Customize items.
  • Open the starter initiative and reference brief.
  • Use only the fictional scenario during the demonstration.

Important

Stop if the app, repository, or required policy access is unavailable. A generic chatbot does not meet this session's goal.

docs.title: Teach the app as a work environment
docs.text:
Show the current locations for:

  • Chats: exploratory work and interviews;
  • Projects: repository-grounded work;
  • My work: issues, pull requests, and active agent sessions;
  • Search: finding repository information;
  • Automations: recurring or on-demand tasks;
  • Customize: skills, agents, MCP servers, plugins, and canvases.

Labels can move. Teach what each area is for rather than a fixed click path.

docs.title: Modes and verified context syntax
docs.text:
• Interactive: use for interviews, source checks, and reviewed drafts.
  • Plan: use before a multi-step change so the learner can approve the plan.
  • Autopilot: reserve for work with agreed scope and permission to act without review of every action. It is not used for the Session m7-01 write.

GitHub documents @ for files, # for issues, and / for commands. Check the picker in the current app. Run /context before the first draft. Use /compact only when the learner needs to keep a long thread. Use /clear or /reset for the fresh-session test.

docs.title: Context before prompting
docs.text:
Use a simple rule:

Use only permitted sources. Attach the smallest set that answers the question.

Demonstrate the difference between:

Explain this project.

and:

Use the repository overview and the open initiative notes. Explain the product,
the affected users, the current decision, and the missing information for a
product owner. Cite the source for each factual claim.

Ask learners which sources Copilot used and which statements remain uncertain.

docs.title: Capability inspection
docs.text:
Open Customize and identify what is available in the learner's environment. Explain:

  • a skill provides a repeatable procedure;
  • an agent carries role-specific instructions and tools;
  • an MCP server lets Copilot read or act in another system;
  • a plugin is an installable package that can bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or canvases;
  • a canvas provides visible shared state;
  • an automation repeats a task with a defined scope.

Do not build these customizations in this session. Show learners how to recognize them and explain that availability depends on plan, policy, and installation.

docs.title: Demo: Create and revise a saved brief
docs.text:
1. Ask for an initiative summary without attaching the source.
  2. Mark unsupported statements.
  3. Attach lab/starter/initiative-overview.md and ask again with source references.
  4. Ask Copilot to complete initiative-context-brief-template.md.
  5. Review and commit the brief.
  6. Reveal lab/starter/late-evidence.md.
  7. Ask Copilot for a focused update and review the diff.
  8. Run /rubber-duck for an independent critique.
  9. Start a fresh session with only the saved brief and check that it can identify the outcome, facts, unresolved decisions, non-goals, and next owner action.

Stress the pattern:

Read -> propose -> review -> write -> verify

Point out that learners will use this same pattern in every later session.
