docs.title: Session m7-02: Interview ideas and shape better work
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Session m7-01 and working GitHub Copilot access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Continue the Delivery Decision Studio path with your Session m7-01 context brief. Install the supplied project skill and use it to ask questions in dependency order. Turn the approved answers into a decision brief and issue proposal. When a late constraint arrives, revise only the affected decisions.

The fictional Service Request Portal remains the initiative. Do not use customer requests or source organization names in the standard lab.

Important

GitHub Copilot is required. Check access before the session. If Copilot cannot run the interview, stop the lab.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
By the end of this session, learners will be able to:

  • Install and check the supplied decision-interview project skill.
  • Run a dependency-ordered interview with GitHub Copilot.
  • Ask only questions whose prerequisites are settled.
  • Resolve scope, constraints, success, failure, ownership, and approval.
  • Review Copilot recommendations before accepting or revising them.
  • Create a reviewed Markdown decision brief in the repository.
  • Draft an issue proposal with testable acceptance criteria and a practical definition of done.
  • Reopen only the decisions affected by new evidence.
  • Check that the revised brief and issue proposal agree.
  • Check context usage before each interview round and start fresh for the final review.
  • Request an independent critique before approving the brief and proposal.
  • Assign an owner and reviewer before work enters a sprint.

docs.title: Session flow
docs.text:
Vague request
  -> project skill installation
  -> GitHub Copilot decision interview
  -> human review and decisions
  -> Markdown decision brief
  -> GitHub issue proposal
  -> acceptance criteria
  -> definition of done

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Marp slides slides.md Starter request and repository templates lab/starter/ Completed Copilot-reviewed examples lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Teach the interview pattern, not skill authoring.
  • Use the supplied project skill; learners do not author a new skill in this session.
  • Use only approved, sanitized material.
  • Treat Copilot questions, recommendations, and drafts as proposals.
  • Keep product and approval decisions with named people.
  • Do not create or update a live work item until the request owner approves the brief.
  • Keep the lab no-code. Learners install and use the supplied skill; they do not author or edit it.
  • Session m7-03 creates the approved GitHub issues. Session m7-02 prepares the source brief and issue proposal.

docs.title: Interview ideas and shape better work
docs.text: Session m7-02 | Product and Delivery Teams | 3 hours

docs.title: GitHub Copilot is required
docs.text:
Before the session:

  • Copy the supplied project skill to .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md.
  • Start a new project session.
  • Check decision-interview under Customize → Skills.
  • Run /decision-interview with the short test request.

Stop the lab if any check fails.

docs.title: Start with the actual problem
docs.text:
"Make request status clearer so people stop asking support."

Before this idea can enter a sprint, decide who it serves and what it changes. You also need decisions about data, scope, ownership, and approval.

The Delivery Decision Studio path carries the Session m7-01 context brief into this interview. Service Request Portal remains the initiative.

docs.title: The shaping flow
docs.text:
Vague request
  -> project skill installation
  -> GitHub Copilot decision interview
  -> human decisions
  -> Markdown decision brief
  -> GitHub issue proposal
  -> acceptance criteria
  -> definition of done

Do not jump from one sentence to an issue template.

The project skill keeps this method consistent across requests. It does not make the decisions.

docs.title: Interview as a decision tree
docs.text:
Each answer can raise new questions.

Ask the current frontier: every decision the owner can make now without guessing about an unsettled decision.

Questions that depend on this round wait for the next round.

docs.title: Work in rounds
docs.text:
Round 1: outcome, affected user, current pain
Round 2: scope, current state, constraints
Round 3: success, failure, edge cases
Round 4: owner, reviewer, approval, rollout

Ask GitHub Copilot to work out the next frontier from the answers the owner accepted.

Use Interactive mode for each frontier. Switch to Plan before proposed file changes. Autopilot is outside this interview.

docs.title: Check context between rounds
docs.text:
• Run /context.
  • Use /compact only when the same thread must continue.
  • Use /clear or /reset when old assumptions are polluting the interview.
  • Resume with the approved context and the owner's settled decisions, not a transcript.

docs.title: Give a recommendation
docs.text:
For each question:

  1. State the decision clearly.
  2. Offer concrete choices when useful.
  3. Recommend an answer and explain the tradeoff.
  4. Wait for the request owner to decide.

GitHub Copilot frames the choice. A person owns the choice.

docs.title: Facts and decisions are different
docs.text:
Use approved evidence for facts Ask people for decisions Existing workflow Which users are in scope Current labels or fields Which behavior should change Known technical limits Which tradeoff to accept Policy and data rules Who approves release

Mark unsupported claims as unverified. Do not present them as facts.

docs.title: Six branches must close
docs.text:
• Scope: who and what are included?
  • Constraints: what limits the solution?
  • Success: what observable result matters?
  • Failure: what can go wrong, and what should happen?
  • Ownership: who decides and who maintains it?
  • Approval: who reviews the brief and accepts the work?

An open branch stays visible.

docs.title: The decision brief
docs.text:
A useful brief records:

  • problem and target outcome;
  • users, scope, and exclusions;
  • constraints and dependencies;
  • success and failure measures;
  • settled decisions and open questions;
  • owner, reviewer, and approval gate.

Keep it short enough to review in one sitting.

docs.title: Create a GitHub issue proposal
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to draft:

  • user and outcome;
  • defined scope and non-goals;
  • acceptance criteria;
  • dependencies and risks;
  • owner and reviewer;
  • definition of done.

Compare the draft with the approved brief. Each field should trace to an approved answer or an open question.

Session m7-03 creates the approved issues through GitHub MCP.

docs.title: Reopen only the affected branch
docs.text:
Late evidence changes requester and support visibility.

Approved brief
  + new visibility constraint
  → reopen visibility decisions
  → update affected criteria
  → preserve unrelated decisions

Do not restart the interview or rewrite settled scope without evidence.

docs.title: Check in a fresh session
docs.text:
Give a new session only:

  • the revised decision brief;
  • the revised issue proposal.

Ask it to find contradictions, unresolved owners, and acceptance criteria with no source decision.

The fresh session shows which assumptions you left in the conversation instead of recording in the files.

Then use /rubber-duck to challenge unsupported criteria, hidden scope, and missing owners.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria describe evidence
docs.text:
Weak:

Status is easy to understand.

Testable:

A requester can see the current status and last updated time for each submitted request.

Include a failure case when the feature can mislead, expose data, or block progress.

docs.title: Definition of done closes delivery
docs.text:
Acceptance criteria describe product behavior.

Definition of done covers the work needed to release and hand over safely:

  • criteria reviewed;
  • permissions checked;
  • supported states documented;
  • test or review results attached;
  • product and service owners approve.

docs.title: Azure Boards update paths
docs.text:
The interview always runs with GitHub Copilot.

Azure Boards path Method MCP Copilot prepares and reviews the approved update before the MCP tool sends it Browser Copilot prepares the exact values, then the learner enters and checks them

There is no static or no-Copilot route.

docs.title: Lab deliverables
docs.text:
1. The installed decision-interview project skill.
  2. A revised decision brief.
  3. An aligned GitHub issue proposal.
  4. Any fixes made after the fresh-session check.

The request owner decides whether the brief is ready for issue planning.

docs.title: Stop conditions
docs.text:
Stop when:

  • GitHub Copilot access does not pass preflight;
  • the input is not approved or sanitized;
  • a required decision owner is absent;
  • policy or data boundaries are unclear;
  • the team cannot state how success or failure will be observed.

Record content blockers. Resolve Copilot access before starting the exercise.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-02 lab: Interview a request and revise the decision brief
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Beginner

Prerequisites: Session m7-01 and working GitHub Copilot app access

Deliverable: An approved decision brief and issue proposal produced through a repeatable project skill

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
Install a repository skill and use it to interview the request owner. Turn the decisions into a brief and issue proposal. When a late constraint arrives, revise the affected decisions and check that both files still agree.

Part Work Time 1 Install and check the interview skill 20 min 2 Run the first decision interview 35 min 3 Create the decision brief and issue proposal 25 min 4 Reopen one branch for a late constraint 25 min 5 Check readiness in a fresh session 15 min

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

Use the Session m7-01 initiative-context-brief.md. If the trainer is delivering Session m7-02 alone, use starter/vague-request.md.

Check GitHub Copilot access before starting. If access is unavailable, stop. Also stop if Copilot cannot read the training repository or load project skills.

docs.title: Part 1: Install and check the interview skill (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Copy the supplied project skill into the root of the training repository:

mkdir -p .github/skills/decision-interview
cp sessions/session-m7-02-interview-and-shape-work/lab/starter/.github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md \
  .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md
git add .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md
git commit -m "Add decision interview skill"

Open a new GitHub Copilot app session for the project. Open Customize → Skills → Installed and check that decision-interview appears.

Select Interactive mode for the interview. Use Plan only when Copilot proposes file changes. Do not use Autopilot because the request owner must answer each round of questions.

Run a short test:

/decision-interview

Test request: Add a clearer request status.
Ask only the first decision frontier, then stop.

If the skill does not appear:

  1. check the file is at .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md;
  2. check the skill name and description are present in its frontmatter;
  3. reopen the project or start a new session;
  4. stop if the project skill still does not load.

Copilot CLI users can run /skills reload and /skills info decision-interview.

Checkpoint: Copilot invokes the supplied skill and returns a numbered first frontier instead of drafting a work item.

docs.title: Part 2: Run the first decision interview (35 minutes)
docs.text:
Attach the Session m7-01 working brief or starter/vague-request.md, then run:

/decision-interview

Interview me as the request owner. Use only the attached source. Continue until
scope, users, success, failure, ownership, approval, and non-goals are decided or
assigned as open questions.

For each frontier:

  1. answer as the request owner;
  2. accept, reject, or revise each recommendation;
  3. require Copilot to restate the decision and reason;
  4. check that dependent questions wait for earlier decisions;
  5. ask for the next frontier.

Stop when each branch has a decision or a named open question.

After each round, run /context. Use /compact only if the interview must remain in the same session and context pressure is high. If the interview has drifted, use /clear or /reset, attach the approved context brief, and provide only the decisions the owner has settled and the open questions needed to continue.

Checkpoint: As the request owner, you can state the settled decisions, their reasons, and the open questions without relying on the chat transcript.

docs.title: Part 3: Create the decision brief and issue proposal (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to create:

  • docs/discovery/decision-brief.md from starter/decision-brief-template.md;
  • docs/discovery/issue-proposal.md from starter/issue-proposal-template.md.

Review both changes before accepting them.

The brief must separate:

  • facts from the source;
  • request-owner decisions;
  • unresolved questions and owners;
  • in-scope and out-of-scope behavior;
  • success and failure evidence;
  • approval state.

The issue proposal must trace each acceptance criterion to the approved brief. Do not create the GitHub issue yet.

Commit the first accepted versions.

docs.title: Part 4: Reopen one branch for a late constraint (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Open starter/late-constraint.md.

Run the skill again:

/decision-interview

Use the approved decision brief and @late-constraint.md. Reopen only the branches
affected by the new constraint. Show which prior decisions remain unchanged.

Answer the new frontier as the request owner. Update the decision brief and issue proposal.

Review the diff:

  • unchanged decisions should remain stable;
  • changed decisions should include a reason;
  • acceptance criteria should reflect the new constraint;
  • the issue proposal should contain no decision absent from the brief.

Commit the revision separately.

Checkpoint: Your repository history shows which decisions changed without rewriting the rest of the brief and proposal.

docs.title: Part 5: Check readiness in a fresh session (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Start a new session with /clear or /reset. Attach only the decision brief and issue proposal.

Ask Copilot to report:

  1. the approved outcome and non-goals;
  2. each acceptance criterion and its source decision;
  3. unresolved questions and owners;
  4. any contradiction between the two files;
  5. a readiness result: Ready, Revise, or Blocked.

Fix any contradiction and rerun the check.

Then request independent critique:

/rubber-duck Challenge the decision brief and issue proposal. Find unsupported
criteria, hidden scope, missing owners, and conflicts with the late constraint.

If the command is unavailable, stop this step and follow a trainer-verified documented critique route. Do not invent a command.

docs.title: Final deliverable
docs.text:
Submit:

  1. the installed decision-interview project skill;
  2. the approved decision brief;
  3. the aligned issue proposal;
  4. any fixes made after the fresh-session check.

Session m7-03 uses the approved brief and issue proposal to create live GitHub issues.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• The project skill was installed and its invocation passed.
  • Questions followed dependency order.
  • Owner decisions and reasons are recorded.
  • A late constraint reopened only affected branches.
  • The brief and issue proposal were revised together.
  • A fresh session found no contradiction.
  • Any useful critique was applied to the brief or proposal.
  • No customer or source organization names appear.

docs.title: Trainer supplement: Shape a requirement in Azure Boards
docs.text:
Use GitHub Copilot to interview the request owner, review a seeded Azure Boards requirement, and prepare approved updates.

Time: Use the two-hour Session m7-02 lab plan. This companion replaces Phases 4 and 5.

Important

The trainer must select and prepare this route before the workshop. It is not part of the standard learner path.

docs.title: Deliverable
docs.text:
Record these items in work-item-update-plan.md:

  • the approved decisions;
  • planned field changes;
  • the saved field values;
  • open gaps and next action;
  • the IDs of child Tasks created after the parent update.

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
You need:

  • GitHub Copilot access;
  • the supplied decision-interview project skill;
  • a request owner and delivery reviewer;
  • the seeded Show request status in the portal requirement in an approved training project;
  • either an Azure Boards browser session or an approved MCP connection that can read and update work items.

Before starting:

  1. Run one prompt and one follow-up in GitHub Copilot.
  2. Open ../starter/vague-request.md.
  3. Open work-item-update-plan.md.
  4. Open the seeded requirement.
  5. Check the title and the session-m7-02 and service-request-portal tags.
  6. Record the current description, acceptance criteria, priority, state, board column, and readiness value.
  7. Check which field, board column, or approved tag represents readiness.
  8. Check the trainer's reset method.

Important

Stop if GitHub Copilot access fails. Fix access before the exercise starts. If Azure Boards MCP is unavailable, use the browser. If neither Azure Boards path works, stop and resolve project access.

Do not configure a new organization, process, field, or MCP server during the lab.

docs.title: Safety boundaries
docs.text:
• Use only the fictional Service Request Portal item.
  • Read the item before proposing an update.
  • Treat every Copilot change as a draft.
  • Do not change area paths, iteration paths, identities, links, process settings, or team settings.
  • Do not create child Tasks until the request owner records approval.
  • Change only the seeded requirement and Tasks created by your pair.
  • Never delete the seeded requirement.
  • Do not paste tokens, credentials, personal data, or live customer material into prompts.

docs.title: Phase 1: Run the Copilot interview
docs.text:
Run the decision-tree interview against:

Make request status clearer so people stop asking support.

Work through the branches for scope, constraints, success, failure, ownership, and approval. Settle each branch or assign its open question to an owner. Record the approved decisions in the update plan.

Ask the request owner to check that the recorded decisions match what you agreed before you review Azure Boards.

docs.title: Phase 2: Compare the findings with the requirement
docs.text:
Read the seeded item without changing it. Ask GitHub Copilot to compare the current fields with the approved decisions.

Field Review question Description Does it name the user, current problem, target outcome, scope, and non-goals? Acceptance criteria Can a reviewer observe the main path, permission boundary, stale or unmapped state, and excluded behavior? Priority Does the value match approved impact and urgency? State Does the state match the request owner's decision? Board column Is the item still in refinement, or is it approved for planning? Readiness Does the team's existing field, column, or tag state readiness?

Record the current value, Copilot proposal, reason, and owner decision. A field may stay unchanged.

docs.title: Phase 3: Prepare the update
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to draft exact field values from the approved decisions.

For the supplied scenario, use these expected changes to review the draft:

Field Proposed direction Description Cover facilities and equipment requesters, public status, last updated time, safe summary, and named exclusions. Acceptance criteria Add requester-only access, mapped status, stale and unmapped application behavior, safe summary behavior, and unchanged behavior for excluded request types. Priority Propose 1 and record the 20% contact-reduction target as the reason. The request owner may choose another value. State Use the team's approved state for an item that can enter planning. Board column Move from New only after approval. Use the team's existing ready-for-planning column. Readiness Set the existing readiness field or tag to the team's ready value.

Do not save yet.

docs.title: Phase 4: Request owner approval
docs.text:
Show the request owner:

  1. the approved decisions;
  2. the field comparison;
  3. the exact proposed values;
  4. the proposed child Tasks.

The request owner records:

  • Approved: update the parent, then create the approved child Tasks.
  • Approved with changes: revise the proposal, record the changes, then update.
  • Needs another interview round: return to the open branches. Do not update the item.

Silence is not approval. The delivery reviewer cannot approve for the request owner.

docs.title: MCP path
docs.text:
Use the approved Azure Boards MCP connection to:

  1. read the seeded requirement;
  2. prepare an update request without sending it;
  3. compare the request with the update plan;
  4. update only accepted fields;
  5. read the item again and record the saved values;
  6. create child Tasks after the parent matches the approval;
  7. read the parent links and record the Task IDs.

If MCP cannot show the pending update or read back the saved result, use the browser path.

docs.title: Browser path
docs.text:
1. Use the Copilot draft as the source for each accepted value.
  2. Edit only the accepted description, acceptance criteria, priority, state, board column, and readiness field or tag.
  3. Compare the form with the update plan.
  4. Save the requirement.
  5. Reopen it and record the saved values.
  6. Create only the approved child Tasks.
  7. Check each Task links to the seeded requirement.

Do not use bulk edit.

docs.title: Child Task gate
docs.text:
Create child Tasks only after the request owner accepts the parent changes. The supplied scenario normally needs two:

  • implement the requester status view and safe application fallback behavior;
  • validate state mapping, freshness behavior, and requester-only access.

Give each Task a clear result and owner role. If a blocking decision remains open, leave the child Task table empty.

docs.title: Review and deliver
docs.text:
Before delivery, check:

  • saved fields match the update plan;
  • acceptance criteria include positive and failure behavior;
  • readiness did not move while a blocking decision remained open;
  • every created Task links to the parent;
  • the next action has an owner.

Fix mismatches and list unresolved gaps with an owner and next action.

docs.title: Reset and cleanup
docs.text:
Use the trainer's reset method. If the trainer directs cleanup in the browser or through MCP:

  1. Remove only child Tasks created by your pair.
  2. Restore only the fields listed in the trainer's seed record.
  3. Read the item again.
  4. Check the seeded title, tags, field values, and empty child-link list.

If you cannot prove that your pair created a child Task, leave it in place and tell the trainer.

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Demonstrate how the supplied decision-interview project skill uses the Session m7-01 context brief to turn an unclear request into a reviewed decision brief and issue proposal.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:06 Show the vague request and the cost of guessing 0:06-0:15 Explain the decision tree, frontier, and rounds 0:15-0:25 Model strong Copilot questions and recommendations 0:25-0:42 Run the Service Request Portal interview with GitHub Copilot 0:42-0:51 Review the answers and build a decision brief 0:51-0:57 Convert the brief into a GitHub issue proposal 0:57-1:00 Explain the lab and review roles

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
Complete this check before learners begin:

  • Check that every learner can open the GitHub Copilot app and the training repository project.
  • Copy the supplied skill to .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md.
  • Open a new app session and check that decision-interview appears under Customize → Skills → Installed.
  • Run /decision-interview with the short test request from the lab.
  • Test one prompt and one follow-up answer.
  • Check Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot modes are visible. The interview uses Interactive; artifact changes use Plan.
  • Check /context, /compact, /clear or /reset, and /rubber-duck in the current command picker.
  • Use only the supplied fictional scenario during the demonstration.
  • Open the starter templates and completed solution in separate windows.
  • Assign a request owner and delivery reviewer for each pair.

Important

Stop if the GitHub Copilot app or repository project is unavailable. Resolve licensing, sign-in, policy, client, or repository access before the session starts.

For a planned trainer-only Azure Boards delivery, check that learners can use either an approved MCP connection or the browser. Azure Boards changes the update method. It never replaces GitHub Copilot.

docs.title: The frontier controls question order
docs.text:
Explain the frontier as the decisions the owner can make now because their prerequisites are settled. Ask all of those questions in one round. Hold any question that depends on an answer still open in that round.

For example, do not ask for notification wording before the group decides whether the first release includes notifications. Do not ask for a success target before the group agrees on the problem and affected user.

docs.title: Recommendations make choices easier to review
docs.text:
Each Copilot question should include a recommended answer. The recommendation shows its reasoning and gives the request owner something concrete to accept or revise.

Use this format:

Q1: Target user
Which group has the problem in the first release?

Recommendation: Start with employees who submitted a request. Leave service agents
out of the first release because they already have an internal queue.

docs.title: Facts do not belong in the decision queue
docs.text:
GitHub Copilot should use approved sources for facts such as current status values, portal fields, or published retention rules. The request owner decides product behavior, tradeoffs, ownership, and approval.

When a source is unavailable, mark the claim as unverified. Do not turn it into a question for the owner to decide.

docs.title: Keep context healthy
docs.text: Run /context after each interview round. Compact only when the same thread must continue. Start fresh when old recommendations begin to leak into new decisions. When starting fresh, carry only the owner's settled decisions and open questions. The decision brief becomes the saved record.

docs.title: Use an independent critic
docs.text: Before approval, run /rubber-duck against the brief and issue proposal. The critic should look for unsupported criteria, missing owners, hidden scope, and visibility-rule conflicts. The request owner decides which feedback to apply.

docs.title: Demonstration scenario
docs.text:
Start with:

Make request status clearer so people stop asking support.

Run the demonstration through /decision-interview. The skill must ask a numbered frontier and wait for owner decisions instead of drafting the final brief.

docs.title: Round 1: Define the problem
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to cover:

  1. Who is asking for updates?
  2. What do they need to know?
  3. What business or service problem should change?

Recommended direction: people who submitted a request need a plain-language status and recent update. Aim first to reduce manual "what is happening?" contacts. Keep service-process redesign outside this work.

docs.title: Round 2: Set the scope
docs.text:
Use the first answers to ask:

  1. Which request types are included?
  2. Which existing states can the portal expose?
  3. Are email, chat, or mobile notifications included?
  4. What data must remain hidden?

Recommended direction: cover facilities and equipment requests in the web portal. Show a mapped public status, last updated time, and safe summary. Exclude outbound notifications, internal notes, agent names, and security details.

docs.title: Round 3: Define success and failure
docs.text:
Ask:

  1. How will the team know the change helped?
  2. What must never happen?
  3. What should the requester see when a status is missing or stale?
  4. Which accessibility and permission checks apply?

Recommended direction: measure fewer status-chasing contacts and check that every supported request shows a public status. Failure includes exposing internal notes, showing a status to the wrong requester, or presenting stale data as current.

docs.title: Round 4: Close ownership and approval
docs.text:
Ask:

  1. Who owns the public status mapping?
  2. Who approves the decision brief?
  3. Who validates service behavior and access rules?
  4. Who can approve release?

Recommended direction: the portal product owner owns the work item. The service operations manager approves wording and state mapping. The privacy reviewer checks data exposure. The product owner accepts the completed work after test or review results are attached.

docs.title: Build the decision brief
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to create docs/discovery/decision-brief.md from answers the owner accepted. Then review:

  • problem and target outcome;
  • users and scope;
  • non-goals;
  • constraints and dependencies;
  • success and failure measures;
  • decisions and open questions;
  • owner, reviewers, and approval gate.

Keep it short enough to review in one sitting. Review the proposed repository change before accepting it.

docs.title: Build the issue proposal
docs.text:
Ask GitHub Copilot to convert the approved brief into an issue proposal:

  1. Write one user outcome.
  2. Copy the agreed scope and non-goals.
  3. Turn success and failure cases into observable acceptance criteria.
  4. Add dependencies and open risks.
  5. Name the owner and reviewer.
  6. Add a definition of done that covers test or review results and approval.

Have learners check every field Copilot drafts against the approved brief. Session m7-03 creates the approved issue set through GitHub MCP.

docs.title: Reopen an affected branch
docs.text: Reveal lab/starter/late-constraint.md. Ask the skill to reopen only visibility decisions. Show that scope, request types, notification exclusion, and ownership stay unchanged while role-specific acceptance criteria are revised.

docs.title: Facilitation notes
docs.text:
• Ask no more than four questions in a demonstration round.
  • Let the request owner reject recommendations. A visible correction helps the class see who owns the decision.
  • Keep unresolved items in an open-questions table with an owner and due point.
  • Push back when criteria use words such as "easy," "fast," or "clear" without a result someone can check.
  • Keep estimation outside the exercise. The goal is readiness.

docs.title: Lab launch
docs.text:
Learners use the Service Request Portal context from Session m7-01 or ../lab/starter/vague-request.md.

Each learner or pair needs a request owner and delivery reviewer. The request owner approves the decision brief. The delivery reviewer checks the brief and proposal in a fresh session.

docs.title: Trainer-only Azure Boards supplement
docs.text:
Use ../lab/azure-boards/README.md when learners have a seeded training requirement. The companion replaces work-item drafting in Phases 4 and 5.

Before the lab, check the field labels used for priority and readiness. Learners may use MCP or the browser to apply approved changes. They must use GitHub Copilot for the interview and draft review.

Azure Boards is trainer-only. Keep the standard learner path in GitHub.

docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-03: Plan work with GitHub Issues and MCP
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions m7-01 to m7-02, GitHub Copilot app access, and an approved GitHub MCP connection

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Continue the Delivery Decision Studio path by turning the approved Session m7-02 decision brief into a GitHub issue hierarchy. Check the GitHub MCP connection and inspect the repository before you plan any writes. Use Markdown to preview the full issue set, then create the approved issues. Read them back from GitHub to check and correct the result. The created GitHub issues are authoritative.

The session teaches safe tool use. Learners do not develop an MCP server.

Important

The GitHub MCP connection and write access to the training repository are required. Stop if the learner cannot inspect tools, preview the write, or check the created issues.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
In this session, you will:

  1. Explain what an MCP server lets Copilot do.
  2. Inspect the GitHub tools available to the current session.
  3. Split an approved outcome into a parent issue and child issues with defined scope.
  4. Review issue titles, descriptions, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and ownership.
  5. Approve a GitHub write operation only after checking its target and arguments.
  6. Retrieve the created issues and compare them with the approved plan.
  7. Preview, apply, and check a focused correction.
  8. Classify concrete existing issues as duplicate, partial overlap, conflict, or unrelated.
  9. Leave a checked live issue set that Session m7-04 can read directly.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Slides slides.md Approved brief and templates lab/starter/ Reference preview lab/solution/

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• Use only the approved training repository.
  • Read before writing.
  • Ask Copilot to show the complete proposed issue set before creation.
  • Treat issue-plan Markdown as a temporary preview. Do not use it as the source of record after creation.
  • Keep issue creation within the agreed count and labels.
  • Check every created issue through a fresh GitHub read.
  • Use an optional Azure Boards route only when it remains the approved system of record.
  • GitHub MCP supplies tools. A plugin may package an MCP server, but plugin installation does not prove that the approved GitHub connection is active.
  • Keep the lab no-code and free of customer or source organization names.

docs.title: Plan work with GitHub Issues and MCP
docs.text: Session m7-03 | Product and Delivery Teams | Intermediate

docs.title: Turn the brief into GitHub issues
docs.text:
Session m7-02 produced an approved decision brief.

Session m7-03 turns it into real GitHub issues.

This is the third step in Delivery Decision Studio.

docs.title: MCP in one sentence
docs.text:
An MCP server gives Copilot named tools for reading or changing another system.

You use the tools in this session without building the server.

A plugin may bundle an MCP server with skills or other customizations. Check the active GitHub MCP connection itself before reading or writing issues.

docs.title: An issue is a contract for the next person
docs.text:
The issue should let a contributor decide whether they can start, what success looks like, and who will review it.

Issue element What it prevents Outcome Work that repeats a vague request Acceptance evidence "Done" without a way to prove it Non-goal Scope growth during implementation Dependency Work that starts before a needed decision Ownership gap Silent assumptions about who decides

Write enough detail for the next contributor to act.

docs.title: Parent and child issues answer different questions
docs.text:
The parent issue holds the outcome, shared constraints, and review path. Each child issue owns one independently reviewable result.

Parent: Improve request-status visibility
  ├─ Child: Define the status data contract
  ├─ Child: Implement the API response
  └─ Child: Add the client status view

If two child issues must edit the same behavior at the same time, sequence them or clarify the design first.

docs.title: Writing through MCP is still an operation
docs.text:
Copilot can prepare the issue plan. A person approves the write only after seeing the target repository and expected result.

After the write, fetch the issue again. Compare what GitHub stored with the approved plan instead of relying on the tool's success message.

The Markdown plan is a temporary preview. The created GitHub issues are authoritative.

docs.title: Read before writing
docs.text:
1. Check the repository.
  2. Inspect existing labels and milestones.
  3. Search for duplicate issues.
  4. Read the approved brief.
  5. Report permission or context uncertainty.

docs.title: Existing work needs a disposition
docs.text:
Candidate Decision Exact duplicate Reuse or close according to repository policy Partial overlap Extend the existing issue and create only the missing work Conflict Keep separate and record why Unrelated Leave unchanged

The lab includes open, closed, overlapping, and conflicting status issues.

docs.title: Decompose by outcome
docs.text:
Create one parent issue and child issues with defined scope.

Each child needs:

  • an independently reviewable result;
  • acceptance evidence;
  • a non-goal;
  • dependencies;
  • an owner or visible ownership gap.

docs.title: Preview the complete write
docs.text:
Before approval, show:

  • repository owner and name;
  • issue count;
  • every title and body;
  • labels and milestone;
  • relationships;
  • fields left unset.

docs.title: People approve the operation
docs.text:
Copilot proposes the action.

Record Approve, Revise, or Reject before the write.

No silent batch creation.

docs.title: Generated confirmation is not verification
docs.text:
After the write:

  1. start a fresh request;
  2. retrieve the issues;
  3. compare them with the approved plan;
  4. correct one defect;
  5. retrieve the corrected issue again.

docs.title: Lab result
docs.text:
• Temporary reviewed issue preview
  • Authoritative live issue set
  • One parent issue
  • Three to five child issues
  • Fresh-read verification
  • Parent-to-child links that Session m7-04 reads directly

Stop if tool review or verification is unavailable.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-03 lab: Create, check, and correct a GitHub issue plan
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

Deliverable: A live GitHub issue hierarchy created through MCP, checked by a fresh read, and corrected through a second approved write

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Live parent and child issues
  • The corrected issue

docs.title: Lab outcome
docs.text:
Create a reviewed GitHub issue hierarchy through MCP. Read the issues back from GitHub to check what was saved. Then make one focused correction and read it back again.

Part Work Time 1 Check GitHub MCP and write access 15 min 2 Read the source and existing GitHub state 20 min 3 Design and review the issue hierarchy 30 min 4 Preview and create the issues 35 min 5 Check and correct one issue 20 min

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

Check GitHub Copilot access. Stop if access is unavailable.

docs.title: Part 1: Check GitHub MCP and write access (15 minutes)
docs.text:
In the GitHub Copilot app:

  1. open Customize → MCP → Installed;
  2. check that the approved GitHub MCP connection is available;
  3. start a session for the training repository;
  4. ask Copilot to list the GitHub tools it can use;
  5. ask it to retrieve the repository name and five open issues;
  6. check that you have issue-write permission.

GitHub MCP is built into Copilot CLI. CLI users can inspect it with:

/mcp list
/mcp show github

If the approved connection is missing, use Customize → MCP to install or configure the organization-approved server. Never paste a token into a prompt or repository file.

Stop if the read test or issue-write check fails.

GitHub MCP is the tool connection used in this lab. A plugin can bundle an MCP server with other customizations, but you must still check the active connection and its tools.

docs.title: Part 2: Read the source and existing GitHub state (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Attach the approved Session m7-02 decision brief and issue proposal. Use starter/approved-decision-brief.md when those artifacts are unavailable.

Ask Copilot to:

  1. summarize the approved outcome, non-goals, acceptance evidence, and owners;
  2. retrieve available labels and milestones;
  3. read starter/existing-issues.json, then search open and closed issues for matching live work;
  4. report every GitHub MCP read it used;
  5. identify any decision in the proposal that is absent from the brief.

Classify each candidate as duplicate, partial overlap, conflict, or unrelated. Record what you will do with it and why in the issue plan.

Checkpoint: No issue is proposed until the source and existing repository state have both been read.

docs.title: Part 3: Design and review the issue hierarchy (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Copy starter/issue-plan-template.md into your working folder.

Use this Markdown file only as a temporary preview. Do not submit or commit it. Once GitHub creates the issues, the live parent and child issues replace the preview.

Ask Copilot to propose:

  • one parent issue for the approved outcome;
  • three to five child issues with independently reviewable results;
  • dependencies and parallel work;
  • acceptance criteria and non-goals;
  • source links to the decision brief;
  • ownership gaps left unassigned.

Review the plan before any write.

Reuse or update an existing issue when it owns part of the approved outcome. Link a closed duplicate for context. Do not merge conflicting or out-of-scope work.

Reject or revise an issue that:

  • combines unrelated outcomes;
  • duplicates existing work;
  • gives reviewers no way to check acceptance;
  • invents an assignee, label, milestone, or date;
  • includes work excluded by the decision brief.

Checkpoint: Every child issue traces to a decision and can be reviewed independently.

docs.title: Part 4: Preview and create the issues (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Send:

Before using a GitHub write tool, show the repository owner and name, issue count,
full title and body for every issue, labels, milestone, parent-child references,
dependencies, and every field left unset. Wait for my approval.

Compare the preview with the issue plan. Revise it until it is safe to approve.

After approval, ask Copilot to create the issues through GitHub MCP. Save each returned issue number and URL in the parent issue or its linked child issues.

Checkpoint: The write result contains one parent and no more than five child issues in the approved repository.

docs.title: Part 5: Check and correct one issue (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Start a new Copilot request. Do not reuse the create response.

Ask Copilot to retrieve the created issues through GitHub MCP. Compare the fresh state with the approved plan:

  • title and body;
  • acceptance criteria and non-goals;
  • labels and milestone;
  • source links and relationships;
  • ownership fields.

Choose one child issue and add the missing section that names who will check the work and which decision it follows:

Verification owner: Delivery reviewer
Source decision: docs/discovery/decision-brief.md

Require a full update preview. Approve the focused write, then retrieve the issue again and check the new section is present. Keep the check in the issue; you do not need a separate document.

Checkpoint: A fresh read proves that both the original create and the correction reached GitHub.

Link every child issue from the parent. Record dependency order, unresolved ownership, your decisions about existing work, and the correction you checked. Session m7-04 reads this live issue set through GitHub MCP.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• GitHub MCP read and write access passed.
  • Existing issues were searched before creation.
  • Each duplicate and partial-overlap candidate has a recorded decision.
  • The complete write was previewed before approval.
  • Created issues match the approved decision brief.
  • A fresh read matched the created state to the approved plan.
  • A second preview, write, and fresh read checked the correction.
  • The parent issue links the child issues and records the planning decisions.
  • No invented owner, date, label, or milestone was added.
  • No customer or source organization names appear.

docs.title: Trainer Guide
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-03 trainer guide: Plan work with GitHub Issues and MCP
docs.text:
00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide Enable timer shortcut (T)

Duration: 1 hour

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Show learners how to plan a GitHub MCP write, approve it, and check what GitHub stored. This continues the Delivery Decision Studio path. Once created, the live issues become the source of record.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:08 Connect the decision brief to saved GitHub issues 0:08-0:18 Explain MCP from the learner's point of view 0:18-0:30 Inspect tools, permissions, and repository context 0:30-0:43 Decompose the initiative into an issue plan 0:43-0:53 Preview, approve, and check a write 0:53-1:00 Explain the lab guardrails

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
• Check that every learner can open the GitHub Copilot app.
  • Check that the approved GitHub MCP server is available.
  • In the app, open Customize → MCP → Installed and inspect the connection.
  • Test one GitHub read before demonstrating a write.
  • Check that learners can read the training repository and create issues in it.
  • Use a repository created for training. Do not use a production backlog.
  • Record the repository owner and name before the demonstration.

Important

Stop if the learner cannot identify the target repository, inspect the tool call, or check the resulting issue.

docs.title: Explain MCP without implementation detail
docs.text:
Use this definition:

An MCP server gives Copilot a set of named tools for reading or changing another system.

Explain these rules:

  • the tool runs with the permissions available to the connection;
  • a read operation can still expose restricted information;
  • a write operation must name its target and proposed values;
  • Copilot can propose an action, but the learner approves it;
  • check the saved result with a new read; generated confirmation text is not enough.

Do not explain server protocols, transports, or SDKs.

docs.title: 1. Read the approved source
docs.text: Open lab/starter/approved-decision-brief.md. Ask Copilot to identify the outcome, constraints, non-goals, owners, and acceptance evidence.

docs.title: 2. Inspect GitHub
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to:

  • identify the target repository;
  • list existing labels relevant to the plan;
  • search for duplicate or overlapping open issues;
  • report any permission or context uncertainty.

Use lab/starter/existing-issues.json when the training repository does not already contain the seeded records. Have learners decide what to do with each candidate:

  • reuse #241 because it partially overlaps the requester view;
  • leave #256 unchanged because notifications are out of scope;
  • reject #263 as implementation work because it conflicts with the visibility boundary;
  • link #278 only as historical context.

docs.title: 3. Propose the issue set
docs.text:
Use one parent issue and three to five child issues. Each issue should have:

  • a clear outcome;
  • defined scope;
  • acceptance criteria;
  • a non-goal;
  • dependencies;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • link to the decision brief.

Reject technical subtasks that have no independent outcome or review point. The Markdown issue plan is a temporary preview. Do not commit or hand it to the next session.

docs.title: 4. Preview the write
docs.text:
Before Copilot calls a write tool, ask it to show:

  • repository owner and name;
  • issue count;
  • each title and body;
  • labels and milestone;
  • parent-child relationship method;
  • fields that remain unset.

The learner records Approve, Revise, or Reject before the write.

docs.title: 5. Check and correct
docs.text:
After creation, retrieve the issues in a fresh read and compare them with the approved plan. Demonstrate a correction by adding the verification owner and source-decision path to one child issue. Preview the update, get approval, write it, and read it back.

Check that the live parent issue links the complete child set. Session m7-04 reads those issues directly.

docs.title: Common failure modes
docs.text: Failure Trainer response Copilot targets the wrong repository Reject the operation and restate the repository Duplicate issue exists Link or update the existing issue instead of creating another Partial overlap exists Reuse the work already covered and create only the missing outcomes Child issue is too broad Split it before the write Labels do not exist Use approved existing labels or leave the field unset Tool output claims success without a returned issue Run a fresh repository read Learner cannot review tool arguments Stop the lab

docs.title: Product notes verified October 5, 2026
docs.text:
Check current GitHub MCP availability, authentication, tool names, issue hierarchy support, and write confirmations before delivery.

Official references:

  • About the GitHub MCP server
  • Using the GitHub MCP server
  • Planning a project with GitHub Copilot

docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-04: Build and use a planning canvas
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions m7-01 to m7-03, GitHub Copilot app access, GitHub MCP access, and canvas creation access

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Continue the Delivery Decision Studio path. Use the built-in /create-canvas skill to turn the live Session m7-03 issues into a visible delivery workspace. Review the generated extension and remove capabilities you do not need. Then change GitHub state and compare it with the canvas. Detect the stale data and refresh it.

You describe and operate the canvas without hand-coding the extension.

The GitHub MCP connection supplies issue tools. A plugin may package MCP and canvas capabilities, but you must still review the connection and capabilities. Keep the lab no-code and free of customer or source organization names.

Important

Live canvas creation is required. Stop if /create-canvas, GitHub MCP, or the approved canvas actions are unavailable.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
In this session, you will:

  1. Decide when a canvas is more useful than another chat response.
  2. Describe the state and actions needed for a planning canvas.
  3. Create a canvas from a plain-language request.
  4. Review and simplify the generated capabilities.
  5. Load approved GitHub issues into the canvas.
  6. Detect drift between visible canvas state and a fresh GitHub read.
  7. Refresh and reconcile the canvas.
  8. Record ownership, refresh, recovery, and retirement conditions.
  9. Leave a live canvas linked to the GitHub issues for Session m7-05.

docs.title: Session structure
docs.text: Block Duration Material Trainer content 1 hour Trainer guide Lab 2 hours Lab guide

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Slides slides.md Canvas requirements lab/starter/

docs.title: Session m3-01 distinction
docs.text: Session m3-01 teaches canvas extension design and implementation. Session m7-04 teaches product and delivery teams to request, review, and operate a canvas through the GitHub Copilot app.

docs.title: Build and use a planning canvas
docs.text: Session m7-04 | Product and Delivery Teams | Intermediate

docs.title: Use visible state when chat stops being enough
docs.text:
A canvas helps you review several records and make repeated updates through named actions. Keep that view available after the conversation ends.

The source is the live Session m7-03 parent issue and its linked child issues, not the previous chat.

docs.title: The canvas is a planning projection
docs.text:
GitHub owns issue state. The canvas groups that state with planning information that helps people decide what to do next.

GitHub fact Canvas planning view Open issue Ready for discovery Assigned issue Ownership confirmed Blocked issue Risk, dependency, and next decision Closed issue Planning result recorded

Label the two kinds of state differently. Otherwise the team cannot tell whether they are seeing a decision or a source-system fact.

docs.title: Keep fields that change a decision
docs.text:
Field Keep it when Remove it when Risk It changes sequencing or approval It only repeats the issue body Owner The responsible person is unclear GitHub already makes it clear Next action A team needs a follow-up It is only a status synonym

The canvas should expose important work without becoming a second backlog.

docs.title: Steering needs a review loop
docs.text:
Observe source state
      ↓
Propose canvas update
      ↓
Review the affected record
      ↓
Accept, revise, or reject

Use this loop to catch stale data and updates that lack supporting sources.

docs.title: Start from live GitHub issues
docs.text:
The canvas should show:

  • parent objective;
  • issue and planning status;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • dependency and risk;
  • decision and next action.

docs.title: Create it in plain language
docs.text:
/create-canvas Create a delivery-planning canvas for the approved GitHub issues.
People can update planning status and record decisions. Copilot can summarize
and propose updates. Do not close issues, change assignees, or publish content.

This is a no-code review. Inspect generated files and capabilities, then ask Copilot for specific changes.

docs.title: Review before use
docs.text:
Ask:

  1. Does each field support a real decision?
  2. Can every action be explained?
  3. Are external writes excluded?
  4. Can the owner recover?
  5. When should the canvas be retired?

docs.title: Simpler is better
docs.text: Remove generated fields and actions that do not help the team decide or act.

docs.title: Load live GitHub issues
docs.text:
Use GitHub MCP to retrieve the Session m7-03 issues.

Copilot can move the approved fields into the canvas. GitHub remains the source for issue state.

docs.title: Label planning state separately
docs.text:
The canvas may show ready for review while the GitHub issue remains open.

That is acceptable when the canvas labels the planning state and source-system state separately.

docs.title: Check three views
docs.text:
Compare:

  • the visible canvas;
  • Copilot's report;
  • a fresh GitHub MCP read.

Resolve or explain every mismatch.

docs.title: Create visible drift
docs.text:
1. Preview and approve a GitHub issue comment through MCP.
  2. Retrieve the changed issue in a fresh request.
  3. Do not refresh the canvas.
  4. Compare the new GitHub state with the visible canvas.

The canvas should show that its last refresh is older than the source change.

docs.title: Reconcile the projection
docs.text:
Use the approved refresh capability.

Check:

  • the blocker appears in planning state;
  • the next action names the owner decision;
  • GitHub state and planning state stay distinct;
  • the last-refresh time changes.

docs.title: Critique the live state
docs.text:
Run /context, then use a fresh session when needed.

Ask /rubber-duck to find stale claims, mixed state labels, unsafe actions, and missing owners.

The live canvas and linked issues are authoritative for Session m7-05.

docs.title: Lab result
docs.text:
• Learner-created canvas
  • Reviewed state and actions
  • Live GitHub issue data
  • A detected and reconciled state mismatch
  • Owner, refresh, recovery, and retirement rules
  • Four linked status-visibility workstream candidates

Stop if live canvas creation is unavailable.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-04 lab: Build a planning canvas and reconcile stale state
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

Deliverable: A project-scoped planning canvas that detects and reconciles a real GitHub state change

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• The generated and reviewed canvas extension
  • The live planning canvas
  • One controlled GitHub state change
  • Links from the canvas to the live GitHub issues

docs.title: Lab outcome
docs.text:
Create and review a planning canvas with the official /create-canvas skill. Load live issue state through GitHub MCP. Then make a controlled change in GitHub so you can detect stale canvas data and refresh it.

Part Work Time 1 Check canvas and MCP capabilities 15 min 2 Define the minimum canvas contract 20 min 3 Create and simplify the canvas 30 min 4 Load and operate live issue state 25 min 5 Create and detect state drift 15 min 6 Reconcile and record ownership 15 min

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

Check GitHub Copilot access before starting. Stop if access is unavailable.

docs.title: Part 1: Check canvas and MCP capabilities (15 minutes)
docs.text:
1. Open a GitHub Copilot app session for the training repository.
  2. Type / and check that /create-canvas appears.
  3. Open Customize → Canvas and inspect installed canvases.
  4. Open Customize → MCP → Installed and check GitHub MCP.
  5. Ask Copilot to retrieve the Session m7-03 parent issue and child issues.

/create-canvas is a built-in app skill. Do not install a community replacement. Stop if the skill or GitHub reads are unavailable.

Use a fresh GitHub MCP read as the authoritative issue list. Start from the live Session m7-03 parent issue and follow its child links. Do not reconstruct the set from chat history or a separate Markdown file.

docs.title: Part 2: Define the minimum canvas contract (20 minutes)
docs.text:
Complete starter/canvas-requirements.md.

The canvas must answer:

  • What outcome are we delivering?
  • Which issues are planned, active, blocked, or ready for review?
  • Who owns the next action?
  • Which dependency or risk needs attention?
  • When did GitHub state last refresh?

Allow only these actions:

  • refresh issue state from GitHub;
  • change planning status in the canvas;
  • record a risk or decision;
  • assign the next planning action.

The canvas must not close issues, change assignees, or publish comments.

Checkpoint: Every field and action supports a named planning decision.

docs.title: Part 3: Create and simplify the canvas (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Run:

/create-canvas

Create a project-scoped delivery-planning canvas from
@starter/canvas-requirements.md. Store it under .github/extensions. It must show
the parent outcome, child issues, planning status, GitHub state, owner, dependency,
risk, next action, and last refresh. It may read GitHub state but must not write
to GitHub.

The agent should create the extension and open it in the side panel.

Review:

  • the files created under .github/extensions;
  • the visible fields and actions;
  • the capabilities exposed to Copilot;
  • any package or dependency added by the extension.

Inspect the generated files and ask Copilot for specific changes. Do not hand-edit extension code; this is a no-code review.

Ask Copilot to remove generated state or actions that exceed the approved contract.

Checkpoint: The canvas is smaller after review and contains no GitHub write action.

docs.title: Part 4: Load and operate live issue state (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Ask Copilot to retrieve the Session m7-03 issues through GitHub MCP and load:

  • issue number and title;
  • GitHub state;
  • planning status;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • dependency;
  • next action;
  • retrieval time.

Then:

  1. change one planning status through the visible canvas controls;
  2. ask Copilot to change another planning status through a canvas capability;
  3. add one risk with an owner;
  4. add one decision with a reason;
  5. ask Copilot for a current canvas summary.

Compare the visible state with Copilot's summary.

docs.title: Part 5: Create and detect state drift (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Choose one child issue. Through GitHub MCP, preview this comment:

Planning update: waiting for a product-owner decision on the public status
vocabulary. Do not start implementation until the decision brief is updated.

Approve the comment, then retrieve the issue in a fresh request.

Do not refresh the canvas yet. Ask Copilot to compare:

  • the current visible canvas;
  • the fresh GitHub issue;
  • the canvas's last-refresh time.

You should now see that the canvas is stale compared with the issue you just read.

docs.title: Part 6: Reconcile and record ownership (15 minutes)
docs.text:
Use the canvas refresh action or ask Copilot to call the approved refresh capability.

Check that:

  • the issue's planning status reflects the new blocker;
  • the next action names the product-owner decision;
  • the GitHub state and planning state remain distinct;
  • the last-refresh time changed.

In the live canvas, record who owns it, how to refresh it, and how to recover after an interruption. Also record when to retire it and the next safe action. Check that it links the four status-visibility issues for Session m7-05.

Run /context. If the creation thread is crowded, start a fresh session and retrieve the live GitHub issues and open the canvas. Then run:

/rubber-duck Critique the live planning canvas against the linked GitHub issues.
Find stale source claims, mixed GitHub and planning states, unsafe actions, and
missing ownership.

Apply useful findings directly to the canvas.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• /create-canvas created a project-scoped extension.
  • Generated files and capabilities were reviewed.
  • Unnecessary state and actions were removed.
  • Live GitHub issues were loaded through MCP.
  • One visible and one agent-requested canvas update succeeded.
  • A reviewed GitHub change made the canvas stale.
  • A fresh read detected the mismatch.
  • Refresh reconciled the canvas without hiding the source difference.
  • The live canvas contains the owner, recovery, refresh, and retirement rules.
  • The live canvas links the four Session m7-05 issue roles.
  • No customer or source organization names appear.

docs.title: Delivery objective
docs.text: Show learners how to create and review a project-scoped planning canvas in the Delivery Decision Studio path. Explain that the canvas displays GitHub state alongside planning information. GitHub remains the source of record.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment 0:00-0:08 Decide when visible state helps 0:08-0:18 Translate live issues into canvas requirements 0:18-0:32 Create the canvas with /create-canvas 0:32-0:43 Review state, actions, and boundaries 0:43-0:53 Create drift and reconcile the canvas 0:53-1:00 Explain ownership and launch the lab

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
• Check that every learner has the GitHub Copilot app.
  • Check that /create-canvas is available.
  • Open Customize → Skills → Installed and show that create-canvas is a built-in skill.
  • Check that the learner can read the Session m7-03 issues through GitHub MCP.
  • Use a training repository and synthetic issue data.
  • Name the canvas owner and reviewer.
  • Retrieve the Session m7-03 parent issue and linked child issues.
  • Check /context, /clear or /reset, and /rubber-duck.

Important

Stop if canvas creation, GitHub reads, or the required canvas actions are unavailable. A static JSON edit does not meet this session's outcome.

docs.title: When to use a canvas
docs.text:
Use a canvas when work needs:

  • visible shared state;
  • repeated updates;
  • several related records;
  • named actions;
  • a view people can review after the chat ends.

Show that a single answer, draft, or short interview can stay in chat without adding a canvas.

docs.title: Translate the plan into requirements
docs.text:
Start from lab/starter/canvas-requirements.md. The minimum planning state is:

  • parent objective;
  • issue number and title;
  • status;
  • owner or ownership gap;
  • dependency;
  • risk;
  • decision;
  • next action.

The source set is fixed: public status mapping, requester status view, empty and stale states, and access-boundary verification.

The minimum actions are:

  • load or refresh approved GitHub issues;
  • change a planning status;
  • record a decision;
  • add or update a risk;
  • produce a current summary.

Closing issues, changing assignees, or publishing updates stays outside the canvas unless the learner adds and approves those capabilities.

docs.title: Demonstration prompt
docs.text:
/create-canvas Create a delivery-planning canvas for the approved GitHub issues.
Show the parent objective, issue number, status, owner, dependency, risk,
decision, and next action. People can update planning status and record
decisions. Copilot can summarize the canvas and propose updates. Do not close
issues, change assignees, or publish content without a separate confirmation.

After generation, ask learners what they would remove. Keep only what supports a decision or action.

docs.title: Review the generated canvas
docs.text:
Check:

  1. Does every state field support a real decision?
  2. Can each action be explained in one sentence?
  3. Does the canvas distinguish planning state from GitHub issue state?
  4. Are external writes excluded or separately approved?
  5. Can the owner recover after an interrupted update?
  6. Is there a clear reason to retire the canvas?

docs.title: Demo update and drift
docs.text:
1. Ask Copilot to retrieve the Session m7-03 issues through GitHub MCP.
  2. Load the approved issue fields into the canvas.
  3. Change one status through the visible controls.
  4. Ask Copilot to record one decision.
  5. Add the lab's reviewed blocker comment to one GitHub issue through MCP.
  6. Read the issue again without refreshing the canvas.
  7. Show the mismatch and last-refresh time.
  8. Refresh the canvas and check the blocker and next action.

Leave learners with the live canvas and linked GitHub issues. Do not create a separate transfer file.

docs.text:

docs.title: Session m7-05: Orchestrate agents and workstreams
docs.text:
Open slides Slides in new tab Download PDF Close slides

Module: Product and Delivery Teams

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Live GitHub Copilot app orchestration access; Sessions m7-01 to m7-04 for the product route, or Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m2-05 for the developer route

Duration: 3 hours (1 hour trainer content + 2 hours lab)

Last updated: October 15, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use parent-led orchestration for one delivery objective. Split four live GitHub issues into independent workstreams, then monitor the child sessions and review their results.

If you are following the developer route after Session m2-05, review a local readiness evaluator, its tests, and a synthetic PR snapshot instead. You do not need a GitHub MCP connection or product-track artifacts for that route. Both routes use the same two-hour lab.

The plan stays small. Each workstream needs a question, input paths or issues, a stop condition, and a reviewer. GitHub Copilot keeps session status, links, timing, and usage on the orchestration surface.

Live orchestration access is required. There is no role-play or prepared-result route.

docs.title: Learning objectives
docs.text:
In this session, you will:

  1. Split one objective into independent workstreams.
  2. Set approved inputs and hard stop conditions.
  3. Start and monitor child sessions through /orchestrate.
  4. Redirect, stop, accept, or reject work.
  5. Return a reviewed parent result backed by the selected route's sources.
  6. Separate local test success from PR readiness in the developer route.

docs.title: Session m5-01 distinction
docs.text: Session m5-01 uses an optional framework for persistent roles and routing. Session m7-05 uses built-in orchestration for temporary workstreams. The parent reviews every result and keeps decision authority.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Resource Location Trainer guide trainer-content/README.md Slides slides.md Lab guide lab/README.md Learner assets lab/starter/ Reference solution lab/solution/

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
Check the built-in orchestrate skill and /orchestrate command in the GitHub Copilot app. Product learners also need GitHub MCP read access to their parent and child issues. Developers need Python 3.10 or later and local project read access instead.

Stop if orchestration or the selected route's source access is unavailable. Fix access before the lab.

docs.title: Agenda
docs.text: Segment Time Parent objective and boundaries 10 min Minimal workstream plan 10 min Monitor and intervene 12 min Live demonstration 13 min Review and lab handoff 15 min

docs.title: Required access
docs.text:
• /orchestrate must create and coordinate live child sessions.
  • Product route: GitHub MCP must read the selected issues.
  • Developer route: local project read access and Python 3.10 or later.
