Stop if orchestration or the selected route's inputs are unavailable.

docs.title: Choose one lab route
docs.text:
Route Inputs Result Product and delivery Four live GitHub issues Parent result used by Session m7-06 Developer Local evaluator, tests, synthetic PR snapshot Separate implementation, coverage, and PR conclusions

Each route takes 120 minutes. Developers need Session m2-05, not Sessions m7-01 to m7-04.

docs.title: One parent objective
docs.text:
Review the four approved status-visibility issues and return one reviewed result for each.

The parent owns scope and review.

docs.title: Keep the plan small
docs.text:
Each workstream needs:

  • a question with a clear scope;
  • approved inputs;
  • a stop condition;
  • a reviewer.

The orchestration surface already holds session links, status, timing, and usage.

docs.title: Four independent workstreams
docs.text:
Workstream Question Public mapping Is the mapping ready for approval? Requester status Is the issue ready for implementation review? Empty and stale states Are fallback states testable? Access boundary Is the approved evidence ready?

Move shared questions back to the parent.

docs.title: Developer workstreams
docs.text:
Question Input Does implementation meet the behavior contract? Brief and evaluator What do tests prove or miss? Brief, tests, and evaluator Is the supplied PR ready? Brief and PR snapshot

Children read the same fixed inputs. They do not wait for one another or edit.

docs.title: Practise steering
docs.text:
Redirect the test reviewer after its first answer:

Check criterion 5. Does the test prove sorted reason codes, the exact complete
reason list, or both? Do not edit files.

Inspect the revised answer. A follow-up question does not prove the first answer was wrong.

docs.title: Reconcile the readiness claim
docs.text:
The synthetic author says: "Local tests pass, so the PR is READY."

Check the actual snapshot:

  • required integration-tests failed;
  • blocking thread R1 is unresolved.

Check the parent's decision against the snapshot. Do not manufacture conflicting child answers. Local success does not override PR blockers.

docs.title: Start live orchestration
docs.text:
/orchestrate Use the four workstreams in my approved plan. Keep them independent.
Each result must answer its question, cite approved inputs, state unresolved
gaps, and give a recommendation. Obey each stop condition.

docs.title: Monitor on the platform
docs.text:
Signal Action Safe and on scope Wait Safe work needs correction Redirect A boundary is crossed Stop The result meets the plan Accept The result lacks support Reject Human authority is required Escalate

Do not maintain a second status log.

docs.title: Review each result
docs.text:
• Does it answer the assigned question?
  • Does it use only approved issue evidence?
  • Did it obey the stop condition?
  • Are gaps listed?
  • Is the recommendation supported?

Reject answers that lack supporting sources.

docs.title: The parent result is the handoff
docs.text:
The reviewed result:

  • links findings to live GitHub issues;
  • shows rejected claims;
  • names gaps and owners;
  • recommends the next follow-up.

Session m7-06 reads this result and the live issues.

docs.title: The human keeps authority
docs.text: Copilot coordinates work. A person reviews results and approves any issue update, publication, or release statement.

docs.title: Session m5-01 is different
docs.text: Session m5-01 Session m7-05 Persistent roles and routing Temporary workstreams Optional framework setup Built-in orchestration Shared memory Live issue evidence

docs.title: Lab deliverable
docs.text:
1. Approved orchestration plan
  2. Live child-session results
  3. Reviewed parent result linked to live issues

Keep progress on the orchestration surface. Do not copy it into a delivery-status form or copy session identifiers.

For developers, use the developer plan and reviewed parent result instead of live issues. Include the actual redirection, rejected or unresolved claims, and observed usage.

docs.title: Lab
docs.text: Overview Lab Trainer Guide

docs.title: Session m7-05 lab: Orchestrate agents and workstreams
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Live app orchestration access; Sessions m7-01 to m7-04 and GitHub MCP read access for the product route, or Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m2-05 for the developer route

Deliverable: An accepted orchestration plan and a reviewed parent result from live child sessions

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• An accepted orchestration plan
  • A reviewed parent result backed by the selected route's source files or issues

docs.title: Choose one route
docs.text:
Read the course safety baseline. Both routes require the app's built-in /orchestrate skill and live child sessions. Stop if orchestration access is unavailable. Separate prompts and prepared answers do not complete the lab.

Route Use after Inputs Lab time Product and delivery Sessions m7-01 to m7-04 Live GitHub issues through MCP 120 min Developer Sessions m1-01 to m1-03, m2-01 to m2-04 and m2-05 Local Python code and a synthetic PR snapshot 120 min

Complete one route. Developers do not need the product route's GitHub issues, canvases, or MCP access.

docs.title: Product and delivery route
docs.text: The GitHub access requirements below apply to this route only.

docs.title: Scenario
docs.text: You will work with four live GitHub issues: public status mapping, requester status, empty and stale states, and requester access. Orchestrate one workstream per issue. Session m7-06 will use your reviewed parent result as an authoritative input.

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
• Check GitHub Copilot access before the lab.
  • Check /orchestrate is available.
  • Check GitHub MCP can retrieve the approved parent and child issues.
  • Check that you can open, redirect, and stop child sessions.
  • Use only supplied synthetic material or approved sanitized work.
  • Stop any work that requests production data, personal data, secrets, external contact, publication, or unapproved changes.

Important

Stop if GitHub Copilot access, orchestration, or issue access is unavailable. Do not replace the live run with separate prompts, role-play, or prepared outputs.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text: Exercise Work Time 1 Approve and start the plan 30 min 2 Monitor and intervene 35 min 3 Review results 35 min 4 Return the parent result 20 min

docs.title: Exercise 1: Approve and start the plan
docs.text:
Open starter/orchestration-plan-template.md.

  1. Retrieve the approved parent and child issues through GitHub MCP.
  2. Define one question with a clear scope for each child issue.
  3. Name the approved issue and linked evidence for each workstream.
  4. Add a hard stop condition and reviewer.
  5. Check that no child depends on another child result.
  6. Submit the plan through /orchestrate.

Use this prompt:

/orchestrate Use the four workstreams in my approved plan. Keep them independent.
Each result must answer its assigned question, cite its approved inputs, state
unresolved gaps, and give a recommendation. Obey each stop condition. Do not
publish, contact people, access restricted data, or change systems.

Open each child session from the orchestration surface. Check its question, inputs, stop condition, and reviewer.

docs.title: Exercise 2: Monitor and intervene
docs.text:
Use the orchestration surface as the live record. Do not copy session identifiers, status, timing, or usage into the plan.

Signal Action Safe and on scope Wait A safe result needs a precise correction Redirect A boundary is crossed Stop The result answers the question with evidence Accept The result is unsupported or outside scope Reject Human authority is required Escalate

Redirect only when the child can safely fix a specific problem with scope or supporting sources.

docs.title: Exercise 3: Review results
docs.text:
Review each child result against its workstream:

  • Does it answer the assigned question?
  • Does it use only the approved issue and linked evidence?
  • Did it obey the stop condition?
  • Are unresolved gaps listed?
  • Is the recommendation supported?

Reject unsupported claims. Redirect a safe, repairable result. Stop work that crosses a hard boundary.

docs.title: Exercise 4: Return the parent result
docs.text:
Ask the parent to summarize only the reviewed child results.

The parent result must:

  • link each finding to its GitHub issue;
  • separate accepted findings from rejected claims;
  • name unresolved gaps and their owners;
  • state which issues are ready for follow-up;
  • avoid publication or source-system changes.

Add the reviewed result to the approved parent GitHub issue if the trainer has approved that write. Retrieve the issue again to check the update.

Session m7-06 uses the live GitHub issues and this parent result. Do not create a separate handoff form.

docs.title: Completion check
docs.text:
• Approved plan with four workstreams, each with a defined scope.
  • Live child results on the orchestration surface.
  • At least one deliberate wait, redirect, stop, accept, or reject decision.
  • Reviewed parent result linked to the live GitHub issues.
  • Fresh-read verification after any approved issue update.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Response /orchestrate is missing Stop and resolve license, policy, client, or command access. A child requests restricted data Stop the child and record the boundary in the parent result. A result cites no issue evidence Reject it or redirect the child. Two workstreams overlap Pause one and move the shared question to the parent. An issue cannot be retrieved Stop that workstream until approved issue access is restored.

docs.title: Goal and access
docs.text:
Supervise independent read-only reviews of a readiness evaluator, its tests, and a supplied PR snapshot. Passing local tests and PR readiness are different claims.

You need the GitHub Copilot app with /orchestrate, local project read access, and Python 3.10 or later. Check that you can open, redirect, and stop child sessions. If any requirement is unavailable, stop this route. No GitHub connection, MCP server, or remote write is needed.

docs.title: Prepare the local project
docs.text:
From the curriculum root, copy these files to a fresh workspace:

mkdir -p ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer
cp -R sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/solution/readiness_guard \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cp -R sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/solution/tests \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cp sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/starter/issue-brief.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cp sessions/session-m2-05-copilot-app-for-developers/lab/starter/prepared-evidence/05-pr-snapshot.json \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/pr-snapshot.json
cp sessions/session-m7-05-orchestrate-workstreams/lab/starter/developer-review-brief.md \
  sessions/session-m7-05-orchestrate-workstreams/lab/starter/developer-orchestration-plan.md \
  ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer/
cd ~/copilot-labs/session-m7-05-developer
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

The supplied reference implementation's six tests should pass. You will review the implementation; do not repair it or install packages. Attach this folder as an app project. Keep the children read-only and restrict tool access to the named files and test command. Do not grant network or GitHub write access.

docs.title: Exercise D1: Accept the work split (25 minutes)
docs.text:
Read developer-review-brief.md and complete developer-orchestration-plan.md.

Use independent questions:

Workstream Question Inputs Implementation Does the evaluator meet the brief's behavior contract? issue-brief.md, readiness_guard/ Tests What do the tests prove, and what remains untested? issue-brief.md, tests/, readiness_guard/ PR state Is the supplied PR ready based on its required checks and threads? issue-brief.md, pr-snapshot.json

Each child works from its own inputs and does not wait for another child. The parent compares the results afterward. Name a reviewer and set stop conditions and a usage limit. The test reviewer may run only the supplied test command.

docs.title: Exercise D2: Start and inspect live work (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Submit the accepted plan:

/orchestrate Use developer-orchestration-plan.md to start independent read-only
reviews of implementation, tests, and PR state. Each child must answer its
question, cite files or JSON fields, and state uncertainty. Keep scope limited to
the named local files and test command. Do not edit, install, use the network, or
change GitHub. Stop at the agreed usage limit. The parent alone reconciles results.

Open the live children and check their inputs and task boundaries. If the command does not create live child sessions, stop and resolve the feature or plan. Do not substitute /fleet, separate chats, or captured answers.

docs.title: Exercise D3: Redirect and reconcile (35 minutes)
docs.text:
After the test reviewer returns its first result, redirect that child:

Check your test-coverage conclusion against acceptance criterion 5 in
issue-brief.md. Explain whether sorted reason codes are tested and whether the
test also proves the exact complete reason list. Do not edit or broaden the task.

Compare the child's original and revised answers. This is a planned follow-up question, not proof that the first answer was wrong. Stop a child if it crosses scope; do not stage a harmful action merely to demonstrate stopping.

Then ask the parent to reconcile all results with the provisional READY note in developer-review-brief.md. Check any disagreement against the source files. If children agree, say so; do not fabricate conflicting child conclusions.

docs.title: Exercise D4: Review the parent result (30 minutes)
docs.text:
Require the parent to return:

  • a separate verdict for implementation behavior, test coverage, and PR readiness;
  • accepted findings with file or JSON-field references;
  • rejected or unresolved claims and the reason;
  • the effect of the child redirection;
  • remaining gaps and the next human decision.

Check that the parent explains why passing local tests cannot override a failed required PR check or unresolved blocking thread. Review the result yourself and keep it in the app session. Do not copy session identifiers or a second progress log into the plan. Inspect the app's usage display and explain whether orchestration was worth using for this work.

docs.title: Developer completion check
docs.text:
• Accepted plan with independent questions and a usage limit.
  • Live child sessions inspected on the orchestration surface.
  • Test reviewer redirected and its revised answer checked.
  • Provisional READY note accepted or rejected using the actual PR fields.
  • Parent result separates implementation, test coverage, and PR state.
  • No source files, packages, or external systems changed.
  • A human decision and observed usage are recorded in the parent result.

Compare your reviewed result with solution/developer-review-reference.md. That reference cannot replace live child-session work.

docs.title: Trainer supplement: Orchestrate work tracked in Azure Boards
docs.text:
Time: 45 to 60 minutes inside the existing two-hour lab

Use: Use Azure Boards as the approved issue source for the main lab.

Deliverable: Live child-session results, reviewed parent result, and checked planning updates

Important

The trainer must select and prepare this route before the workshop. It is not part of the standard learner path.

Use a seeded Azure Boards Epic or Feature for the same four Session m7-03 issue roles. Keep the authoritative plan and status in Azure Boards, and repository work in GitHub.

GitHub Copilot must perform the orchestration. Azure Boards MCP and the browser are planning interfaces. They do not replace the built-in /orchestrate skill.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
You need:

  • access to a training Azure DevOps project with the seeded status-visibility Epic or Feature;
  • permission to read and update the seeded child work items;
  • an approved Azure Boards MCP connection or browser access;
  • the work item IDs or seed tag supplied by the trainer;
  • live GitHub Copilot orchestration through /orchestrate;
  • access to the fictional GitHub repository when a selected item requires repository evidence.

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
1. Open the seeded parent and check that it is tagged for Session m7-05 training.
  2. Record the parent ID, process type, starting state, and selected child IDs.
  3. Type / in the GitHub Copilot app and check that /orchestrate is available.
  4. Open Customize → Skills → Installed and check the built-in orchestrate skill.
  5. Check that you can open, steer, and stop those sessions.
  6. Name who reviews the parent result and who may approve Boards updates.

Important

Stop if GitHub Copilot orchestration is unavailable. Fix access before you continue. Do not use separate prompts, role-play, exports, or prepared results as a substitute.

Use only the seeded fictional items. Do not open production work items, add real organization data, or change project settings.

docs.title: Parent objective
docs.text:
Use the seeded status-visibility Epic or Feature.

Review the four approved status-visibility items and return one reviewed result for each. Do not change production systems or publish claims.

docs.title: Step 1: Select independent child work items
docs.text:
Open the parent item through approved MCP tools or the browser. Select up to four children. Give each a separate question and approved inputs.

Mirror the standard lab wording:

Session m7-03 issue role Azure Boards child wording Public status mapping Public status mapping approval Requester status view Requester view field review Empty and stale states Empty and stale state validation Requester access verification Requester-only access evidence

For each selected item, record the question and its scope, approved inputs, hard stop condition, and reviewer.

Check that each selected child can work without waiting for another child's result. Keep shared dependencies with the parent or run dependent work in sequence.

docs.title: Step 2: Record the contracts
docs.text:
For each selected child:

  1. Move the item to the mapped active state.
  2. Add the question, scope, and stop condition to the description or a comment.
  3. Keep shared decisions in the parent item.

Use the project's existing state mapping. Check the item ID before every MCP or browser write.

docs.title: Step 3: Start GitHub Copilot orchestration
docs.text:
Build the parent instruction from the selected work items. Include each item ID, question and its scope, approved inputs, stop condition, and reviewer.

Start the work through /orchestrate. Check that GitHub Copilot created one live child session for each selected item. Use the orchestration surface to track the sessions. Do not copy live session identifiers into Boards.

Repository work must name the allowed repository and path. The child session may return evidence or a draft pull request when the contract allows it. It must not close the Boards item, approve a pull request, merge, deploy, or make the release decision.

docs.title: Step 4: Inspect and control the work
docs.text:
Inspect the live child sessions in GitHub Copilot. Use Azure Boards MCP or the browser to record progress.

Signal Action Work is safe and on scope Wait A safe result needs a specific correction Redirect A completed result is unusable or outside scope Reject Work crosses an access, data, usage, or authority boundary Stop The contract is met Accept

Record the control decisions you actually make. Stop unsafe work, reject unsupported claims, and escalate decisions that require human authority.

docs.title: Step 5: Review and update Boards
docs.text:
1. Add the decision and reason to the child item.
  2. Move accepted items to the project's reviewed or completed state.
  3. Keep revised items active with one clear correction.
  4. Move rejected items to the agreed closed state without approving their content.
  5. Stop unsafe work and record the boundary that ended it.

Return to Exercise 4 in ../README.md. Use the reviewed parent result to update the parent item only when that write is approved. Retrieve the item again to check the change.

docs.title: Safety boundaries
docs.text:
• Work only with the seeded training hierarchy.
  • Do not change project process settings, team configuration, area paths, or iteration paths.
  • Do not create service commitments or release claims without evidence.
  • Do not place secrets, personal data, production records, or real organization names in work items.
  • Do not let an agent approve, merge, deploy, contact people, or close the parent decision.
  • Stop when an item requests restricted data or needs authority the learner does not have.

docs.title: Reset and cleanup
docs.text:
1. Restore each selected item to the starting state recorded during preflight.
  2. Remove only links, tags, or assignments that you added when project policy allows it.
  3. If a training comment cannot be removed, add a short cleanup note.
  4. Close the GitHub Copilot child sessions and follow the repository's branch or pull-request cleanup policy.
  5. Do not delete the seeded hierarchy unless the trainer gives a reset instruction for those exact item IDs.

If the trainer supplied a seed/reset tool, follow that tool's README. This lab does not run reset commands.

00:00 Start timer Reset timer Print guide Enable timer shortcut (T)

Duration: 1 hour

Format: Presentation plus live demonstration

docs.title: Delivery goal
docs.text:
Show learners how to direct four issue-based workstreams through live GitHub Copilot orchestration. Use the orchestration surface to track the running work. Keep only the decisions needed before work starts in the plan.

For developers after Session m2-05, use the local PR-readiness route instead. It reviews implementation behavior, tests, and a supplied snapshot without GitHub MCP access. Preserve the product route's live issue workflow and Session m7-06 handoff.

docs.title: One-hour plan
docs.text: Time Segment Outcome 0:00-0:10 Parent objective and workstream boundaries Split work without hidden dependencies. 0:10-0:20 Minimal workstream plan Set questions, inputs, stops, and reviewers. 0:20-0:32 Monitor and intervene Wait, redirect, stop, accept, reject, or escalate. 0:32-0:45 Live demonstration Review child sessions on the orchestration surface. 0:45-0:55 Review the parent result Keep supported findings and visible gaps. 0:55-1:00 Lab handoff Check access and deliverables.

docs.title: Required preflight
docs.text:
• Check /orchestrate and the built-in orchestrate skill.
  • Product route: check GitHub MCP read access to the selected issues.
  • Developer route: run the supplied Python tests and check local project read access.
  • Use synthetic or approved sanitized work.
  • Check that the trainer can open, redirect, and stop child sessions.
  • Decide who may approve issue updates.

Stop if orchestration or the selected route's source access is unavailable.

docs.title: Minimal workstream plan
docs.text:
Each workstream needs:

  • one question with a clear scope;
  • approved issue inputs;
  • one hard stop condition;
  • one reviewer.

Do not copy session links, status, timing, usage, or progress into the plan. GitHub Copilot already holds that state.

Workstream Question Approved input Stop condition Reviewer Public mapping Is the public mapping ready for approval? Mapping issue and linked evidence Restricted data or invented states are required Product owner Requester status Is the issue ready for implementation review? Requester-status issue and linked evidence An unsupported field or forecast is required Delivery reviewer Empty and stale states Are fallback states testable? Fallback-state issue and linked evidence An unsupported commitment is required Service reviewer Access boundary Is requester access evidence ready? Access issue and linked synthetic evidence Production or personal data is requested Privacy reviewer

docs.title: Monitor the live work
docs.text:
Use the current session management surface.

Signal Action Safe and on scope Wait Safe work needs a precise correction Redirect A hard boundary is crossed Stop The result meets the plan Accept The result lacks support Reject Human authority is required Escalate

As you inspect the work, show learners why you choose to wait, redirect, stop, accept, reject, or escalate.

docs.title: Review the parent result
docs.text:
Review how the parent connects findings to live issues. Check that it shows rejected claims, names open gaps, and recommends the next follow-up. It must not publish or change source systems without approval.

Session m7-06 reads the live issues and the reviewed parent result. There is no manual delivery-status record or static handoff.

docs.title: Developer demonstration
docs.text:
Use the developer route in lab/README.md and keep the same one-hour teaching plan. Replace the four issue questions with implementation, tests, and PR-state questions from developer-orchestration-plan.md.

Before delivery:

  1. Copy the supplied reference implementation and six tests from Session m2-05.
  2. Run the documented unittest command and retain the actual result.
  3. Read developer-review-brief.md and pr-snapshot.json.
  4. Check that child sessions can read the shared files without editing them or using the network.
  5. Agree a usage limit and identify the human reviewer.

Run /orchestrate with the accepted questions. Open each child on the app surface. Redirect the test reviewer to criterion 5 after its first answer; inspect the revised answer rather than assuming the first was wrong.

Require the parent to evaluate the provisional author note that green local tests make the PR ready. The supplied snapshot has a failed required integration check and unresolved blocking thread R1. Those remain blockers even when local tests pass. Children may agree; never fabricate a disagreement.

Allow 25 minutes for the developer work split, 30 for live inspection, 35 for steering and reconciliation, and 30 for parent review. Grade the findings learners checked and how they redirected the work. Do not grade an exact child count or speedup.

Use lab/solution/developer-review-reference.md after the human review. It explains the source facts but cannot replace live child results.

docs.text:
Learners submit:

  1. the approved orchestration plan;
  2. the live orchestration result;
  3. fresh-read proof for any approved GitHub issue update.

For the developer route, require the accepted developer plan and the app's reviewed parent result, including the redirection, rejected readiness claim, and observed usage. Do not require an issue update or Session m7-06 handoff.

For an Azure Boards delivery, use the trainer supplement. GitHub Copilot still performs the orchestration.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Build one draft-only automation from the reviewed Session m7-05 result. It reads live GitHub issues and the parent orchestration result, then drafts a stakeholder update for human review.

Run the automation, update one approved issue, and run it again. Compare the results on the platform before finishing the stakeholder update. Keep scheduling disabled unless the trainer approves it.

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
• Define an automation's inputs, output, and limits in a short table.
  • Use live GitHub issues and the parent orchestration result as authoritative inputs.
  • Restrict the automation to one draft stakeholder update.
  • Review run records on the platform instead of copying them into a separate form.
  • Rerun after an approved issue change.
  • Decide whether to keep, revise, disable, or pause the automation.
  • Name the authoritative planning system.

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
• The automation may read only approved GitHub issues and the Session m7-05 parent result.
  • Its only permitted output is a draft stakeholder update.
  • It may not publish, message people, edit issues, change labels, or write to external systems.
  • A person reviews every draft.
  • The enabled or disabled state must match the definition.

docs.title: Define the automation
docs.text: Field Decision Trigger and cadence Manual; no schedule Authoritative inputs Live issues and parent result Permitted output One draft stakeholder update Prohibited side effects No posts, messages, edits, or external writes Reviewer Named human role Stop conditions Named hard boundaries Current state Enabled or disabled

Inspect run status, identifiers, timing, usage, and supporting results on the platform. Do not recreate those fields in a form.

docs.title: Create one manual automation
docs.text:
Read the approved status-visibility GitHub issues and the reviewed Session m7-05
parent result. Draft one stakeholder update from supported issue state. Name
unresolved exceptions and owners. Do not publish or change systems.

Use the minimum GitHub read tools.

docs.title: Review the first run
docs.text:
• Trace every claim to an issue or the parent result.
  • Keep unresolved evidence visible.
  • Reject unsupported causes and forecasts.
  • Check that no prohibited side effect occurred.
  • Choose Keep, Revise, Disable, or Pause.

docs.text:

Retrieve the issue again. Then run the same automation.

State:

  • supported status changes;
  • unresolved exceptions and owners;

  • the next action.

A person shares the update.

Use Azure Boards when the delivery backlog lives there.

Do not maintain competing status fields.

Enable a cadence only after separate approval. Update the current state when the automation is enabled or disabled.

docs.title: Session m7-06 lab: Create and review a delivery automation
docs.text:
Duration: 2 hours

Difficulty: Intermediate

Prerequisites: Sessions m7-01 to m7-05, Automations access, and GitHub MCP access

Deliverable: One reviewed stakeholder update from a draft-only automation

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• A concise automation definition
  • One reviewed stakeholder update

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
Create one automation that reads the live GitHub issues and the reviewed Session m7-05 parent result. Review its first draft, then apply one approved issue change and run it again. Compare the drafts to see how that change affected the update.

The core lab uses a manual trigger and draft-only output. Scheduling stays disabled.

Part Work Time 1 Check access and retrieve inputs 20 min 2 Complete the automation definition 20 min 3 Create and run the automation 30 min 4 Review the draft 20 min 5 Update one issue and rerun 20 min 6 Finalize the stakeholder update 10 min

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
Complete the track capability setup.

Check GitHub Copilot Automations access and GitHub MCP access before the lab.

Stop if GitHub Copilot access, Automations, or GitHub MCP access is unavailable. Fix access before continuing.

docs.title: Part 1: Check access and retrieve inputs
docs.text:
1. Open Automations in the GitHub Copilot app.
  2. Check that New automation is available.
  3. Retrieve the approved parent and child GitHub issues through GitHub MCP.
  4. Open the reviewed Session m7-05 parent orchestration result.
  5. Check that issue state and the parent result agree on the four workstreams.

Do not copy platform state into local handoff files.

docs.title: Part 2: Complete the automation definition
docs.text:
Copy starter/automation-definition-template.md into your working folder.

Complete only these fields:

  • trigger and cadence;
  • authoritative inputs;
  • permitted output;
  • prohibited side effects;
  • reviewer;
  • stop conditions;
  • current enabled or disabled state.

In your definition, use a manual trigger and limit the output to one draft stakeholder update. Enable the automation only for supervised lab runs.

docs.title: Part 3: Create and run the automation
docs.text:
Create a local automation with the minimum GitHub read tools.

Use this prompt:

Read the approved status-visibility GitHub issues and the reviewed Session m7-05
parent orchestration result. Follow @automation-definition-template.md. Draft one
stakeholder update from supported issue state. Name unresolved exceptions and
owners. Do not publish, message people, edit issues, change labels, call
unapproved tools, or invent missing values.

Review the trigger, tools, prompt, and enabled state before the run. Keep any schedule disabled.

docs.title: Part 4: Review the draft
docs.text:
Inspect the run on the Automations surface.

Check that:

  • each status claim traces to a live issue or the reviewed parent result;
  • unresolved evidence remains visible;
  • no unsupported cause or forecast appears;
  • no prohibited side effect occurred;
  • the output is one draft stakeholder update.

Choose Keep, Revise, Disable, or Pause. Update the definition's current state to match that decision. Do not create a separate status record.

docs.title: Part 5: Update one issue and rerun
docs.text:
Open starter/approved-input-change.md.

  1. Apply the approved synthetic evidence update to the named training issue through a reviewed GitHub MCP write.
  2. Retrieve the issue again and check the new state.
  3. Run the same automation. Do not create a second automation.
  4. Compare the two runs on the Automations surface.
  5. Check that only the approved issue change explains the draft change.

docs.title: Part 6: Finalize the stakeholder update
docs.text:
Complete starter/stakeholder-update-template.md from the second reviewed draft.

The update must state:

  • the reporting scope;
  • supported status changes;
  • unresolved exceptions and owners;
  • the review decision;
  • the next action.

Name GitHub or Azure Boards as the authoritative planning system. Leave sharing the update to a person, not the automation.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Live issues and the Session m7-05 parent result were the only status inputs.
  • The concise automation definition is complete.
  • The automation produced one draft stakeholder update.
  • The platform holds run status, tool calls, and output.
  • One approved issue change was checked with a fresh read.
  • The same automation ran again.
  • A person chose Keep, Revise, Disable, or Pause.
  • Scheduling remains disabled.
  • No prohibited side effect occurred.

  2. Write effective prompts and choose the context each task needs

docs.text:

docs.title: Track: Product and Delivery Teams
docs.text: Target Audience: Product Managers, Product Owners, Business Analysts, Project Managers, delivery leads, and other non-developer roles Duration: 18 hours (6 sessions × 3 hrs) Difficulty: Beginner → Intermediate Recommended Delivery: 3 days

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Use the GitHub Copilot app to work through one product initiative across six sessions. The path is called Delivery Decision Studio. That is the curriculum's name, not a GitHub product or app mode.

Gather context and settle product decisions first. Then plan the issues, build a planning canvas, supervise parallel reviews, and draft a follow-up within the agreed limits.

The initiative is the fictional Service Request Portal. Do not replace it with customer work in the standard path. Trainer-approved substitutions must be synthetic, sanitized, and free of customer or source organization names.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A GitHub account with GitHub Copilot access
  • Browser access to the training repository
  • The GitHub Copilot app
  • The approved GitHub MCP server with access to the training repository
  • Canvas creation, orchestration, and Automations access
  • Basic knowledge of the learner's product or delivery process

You do not need programming experience, Git command-line knowledge, or repository administration skills.

GitHub Copilot access is required for Sessions m7-01 to m7-06. Learners without access should not take this track. Stop and reschedule their training after access is available.

docs.title: Capability setup
docs.text: Complete this setup before Session m7-01. Check the tools again before each later session. Organizational policy can change which tools the app makes available.

docs.title: 1. Open the training project
docs.text:
1. Sign in to the GitHub Copilot app.
  2. Add or open the approved training repository under Projects.
  3. Start an interactive session.
  4. Ask Copilot to read one known file from the repository.
  5. Stop if it cannot read the approved project.

docs.title: 2. Inspect installed customizations
docs.text:
Open Customize, then Installed. Record the available:

  • skills;
  • MCP servers;
  • plugins;
  • canvases.

Use only capabilities approved for the training repository.

An MCP server and a plugin do different jobs:

  • MCP server: exposes named tools and data sources to Copilot.
  • Plugin: installs a reusable package that may include skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or canvases.

A plugin installation does not tell you whether GitHub MCP can read the training repository. Test the connection separately.

docs.title: 3. Check skills
docs.text:
Sessions m7-04 and m7-05 use the built-in /create-canvas and /orchestrate skills. Type / in a session and check that both commands appear before those sessions. They are built-in app skills, so do not install look-alike community skills.

Session m7-02 supplies a project skill under .github/skills/decision-interview/SKILL.md. After copying it into the training repository:

  1. commit the skill;
  2. open a new app session for the project;
  3. open Customize → Skills → Installed;
  4. check that decision-interview appears;
  5. run /decision-interview with a short test request.

Copilot CLI users can check the same project skill with:

/skills reload
/skills info decision-interview

docs.title: 4. Check GitHub MCP
docs.text:
Sessions m7-03 to m7-06 require GitHub repository tools.

In the app:

  1. open Customize → MCP → Installed;
  2. check that the approved GitHub MCP connection is available;
  3. start a session and ask Copilot to list the available GitHub tools;
  4. test one read against the training repository;
  5. do not continue to a write lab until the read succeeds.

GitHub MCP is built into Copilot CLI. CLI users can inspect it with:

/mcp list
/mcp show github

If an additional MCP server is required, install it through Customize → MCP or /mcp add using the organization-approved server definition. Do not paste personal access tokens into prompts or repository files.

docs.title: 5. Check session-specific tools
docs.text:
Session Required tool or access m7-01 App project and repository reads m7-02 Project skill decision-interview m7-03 GitHub MCP issue reads and writes m7-04 Built-in /create-canvas and GitHub MCP reads m7-05 Built-in /orchestrate, child-session steering, and GitHub MCP m7-06 Automations and GitHub MCP

When a required tool is unavailable, stop that lab. Do not replace hands-on work with role-play or claim that a static artifact proves the workflow ran.

docs.title: 6. Check session controls and context syntax
docs.text:
Before Session m7-01, check these controls in the current app:

  • session modes: Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot;
  • @ for adding files, # for referencing issues, and / for commands;
  • /context for current context usage;
  • /compact for summarizing an active session under token pressure;
  • /clear or /reset for a fresh session;
  • /rubber-duck for an independent critique from a different model.

GitHub notes that command availability depends on context. Type / in the app before delivery. If a command is missing, record it in the trainer notes. Do not teach a substitute without checking that it works.

docs.title: Delivery Decision Studio continuity
docs.text:
Use these roles throughout the path:

Role Responsibility Decision owner Makes product and scope decisions Delivery reviewer Checks results, readiness, and handoffs Work-system steward Checks the authoritative GitHub or Azure Boards state Trainer Checks access and teaches optional maturity guidance

Save and reuse these results:

Session Authoritative result Used next m7-01 initiative-context-brief.md Grounded context for Session m7-02 m7-02 decision-brief.md, issue-proposal.md Product decisions for Session m7-03 m7-03 Live parent and child GitHub issues Issue state for Session m7-04 m7-04 Live canvas linked to GitHub issues Reconciled planning view for Session m7-05 m7-05 orchestration-plan.md, live issues, reviewed parent result Authoritative inputs for Session m7-06 m7-06 automation-definition.md, stakeholder-update.md Human-owned operating decision

At each step, record the next action and open questions in the file or work system listed above.

docs.title: What learners should bring
docs.text:
• The supplied Service Request Portal initiative
  • The supplied synthetic issue and status data
  • The approved live issue state from the training repository
  • One recurring workflow pattern they want to evaluate
  • Their team's definition of ready or done
  • One decision that must remain with a named person

The supplied scenario covers every exercise and is the default learner path.

docs.text: Day Sessions Focus Day 1 Sessions m7-01 to m7-02 App fluency, context, and interviewing Day 2 Sessions m7-03 to m7-04 GitHub issues, MCP, and planning canvases Day 3 Sessions m7-05 to m7-06 Orchestration, automation, and work-system handoff

docs.title: Learning outcomes
docs.text:
After this track, you should be able to:

  1. Compare unscoped and repository-grounded Copilot work.
  2. Install and use a project skill to create and revise a decision brief.
  3. Use GitHub MCP to preview, create, check, and correct an issue plan.
  4. Create a planning canvas and reconcile it after GitHub state changes.
  5. Use built-in orchestration to supervise, redirect, and review child sessions.
  6. Run a draft-only Automation twice and compare the recorded results.
  7. Decide which approved work system remains authoritative.

docs.title: Trainer guidance
docs.text:
• Use the supplied Service Request Portal path in standard delivery.
  • Keep customer and source organization names out of prompts, artifacts, issues, screenshots, and demonstrations.
  • Keep using the same initiative so learners can see how each session uses the previous session's work.
  • Check current official GitHub documentation and organizational policy before every live delivery.
  • Treat generated output as a proposal. The accountable person accepts, rejects, or revises it.
  • Keep the path no-code. Learners review generated extensions and tool calls but do not write application code, MCP servers, plugins, or canvas extensions.

docs.title: Trainer-only Azure Boards supplement
docs.text:
Use Azure Boards only when the delivery plan calls for it before the workshop. Do not introduce it as an alternate learner path during the standard labs.

The tools described in scripts/azure-boards/README.md seed, check, and reset a synthetic backlog for Agile or Scrum projects. They check existing project settings and never create them.

Use the Session m7-02 supplement to shape a seeded requirement. Use the Session m7-05 supplement to supervise seeded workstreams. Both still require GitHub Copilot.
